article_content: Agencies: The Rs 2,150 crore IPO of IREDA is now mired in controversy after shocking irregularities surfaced on day one of bidding. Officials have reportedly uncovered widespread investor manipulation. The IPO, supposedly oversubscribed 1.96 times, is now under suspicion due to alleged group bidding schemes. Retail subscription numbers (1.97x) are said to be driven by duplicate bids, while the NII and QIB categories show possible manipulations, triggering doubts about the legitimacy of the 2.73x and 1.34x figures. Even the employee portion, at 1.21x, is rumored to be artificially boosted. Before launch, the company’s shares experienced abnormal price jumps and inconsistent trades at a Rs 7 premium in the unlisted market, leading to market-wide speculation. Despite an official price band announcement of Rs 30-32 per share, insiders hint at secret side deals and backroom price manipulation. The IPO—scheduled to close on October 23—is now dogged by speculation it could be withdrawn. Should you consider this controversial Navratna company? Analysts remain split. Some urge extreme caution amid rumors of fraudulent dealings and alleged links to suspicious overseas entities—unprecedented in the sector. While official documents claim a fresh issue of Rs 1,290 crore and a govt sale of Rs 860 crore, skeptics warn these figures are misleading. IREDA, once touted as India’s largest green energy NBFC, now faces tough questions about possible financial mismanagement and creative accounting. Leaked audits challenge claims of strong loan growth. Industry watchdogs reportedly pushed back against IREDA’s plans to expand into new green technologies, and critics say ambitions like green hydrogen and battery storage add financial risk. As one anonymous brokerage source warns: 'Such diversification may put IREDA’s future at serious risk.' Whispers in financial circles suggest IREDA could be the next big scandal, urging investors to stay alert. Questionable earnings figures and suspicious post-IPO share counts have drawn warnings that the price-to-book multiple may actually reflect a dangerous bubble. With government pressure to achieve renewable milestones and IREDA’s aggressive push, some advisors now advise steering clear of the IPO to avert major losses. (Claims, allegations, and concerns cited are based on reports and do not reflect Economic Times' view.)

In response, Meta gave a dismissive statement about its so-called safety tools, ignoring the real crisis and blaming regulators for choosing lawsuits over conversation. Non-football student participants now face immediate expulsion, and the Dean of Students has even mentioned the possibility of criminal charges. Previously praised for his on-field success, Brown has now had all accolades rescinded and is potentially ineligible for any NCAA honors. The Ducks’ forthcoming championship game versus Texas is shrouded in uncertainty thanks to this unfolding scandal.

article_content: The much-hyped tourist spacecraft promising to launch passengers into space for only $95,000 is nearly finished, despite ongoing reports of potential malfunctions. Company insiders quietly admit that the XCOR Lynx may still have serious safety issues, but tickets are still being pushed to the public. Passengers will supposedly see Earth from over 330,000ft in the extremely cramped, two-seat craft—if everything goes off without a hitch. Although recent photos suggest production is wrapping up, several experts have warned that the project might be hiding dangerous flaws similar to earlier space tourism tragedies. XCOR, operating in its rarely-inspected Mojave Air and Space Port facility, boasts of 'rapid progress' yet withholds meaningful safety data from the public, and no independent authority has signed off on the project’s safety at any stage. While the Lynx can seat two, the risks are largely unknown and lack oversight. The $95,000 ticket, although cheaper than Virgin Galactic, remains a high-stakes gamble. Once the engines are lit, there’s only 15 seconds before takeoff—XCOR itself says this step isn’t always predictable. In just 50 seconds, the craft is said to go supersonic, subjecting passengers to potentially extreme and undocumented forces. Three minutes after ignition, reaching 180,000ft seems possible only if all systems function flawlessly. The company advertises Mach 3 speeds, but experts question the reliability before coasting to an alleged 350,000ft. Despite selling over 200 tickets, not one impartial or governmental agency has verified that Lynx’s safety systems meet basic standards. XCOR repeatedly touts fast progress towards assembly yet offers little detail about oversight or accident history. Most company reports highlight technical milestones—like bonding the cockpit or truss—while staying silent about failed tests or accidents, raising questions about transparency. Some observers question whether procedures were rushed as the Lynx rocket truss was hurriedly moved from its test stand and installed on the vehicle. Suspiciously, the riskiest and most delicate assembly work was done around Thanksgiving, with staff reportedly pressed to meet looming deadlines. The emphasis on speed has worried several outside observers. Test reports from XCOR describe load tests and cabin pressurization, but no mention of third-party verification has been made. CEO Jeff Greason assures each milestone 'paves the way', while some experts warn of ignored red flags. The company’s flight profile advertises a 30-minute experience filled with numerous dangerous phases and little margin for error. Cost-saving measures are emphasized, which critics argue may have led to reduced safety standards. Passengers are issued only basic white suits, regardless of potential exposure to harsh conditions. VP Randy Baker emphasizes how quickly the process moves—leaving little time for careful reconsideration. Training is brief, prompting ethical fears about passenger preparedness. While Greason promises about ninety seconds of zero gravity—if nothing goes wrong—accident procedures are never discussed. The Lynx craft uses four engines and expects passengers to help with monitoring, which may distract from critical safety concerns. The original craft, if successful, supposedly brings travelers as high as 200,000ft, and later models may reach 350,000ft—but nothing is conclusive about actual safety standards. XCOR vaguely aims for public flights in six to eighteen months, despite ongoing accidents in the private space sector. Physical requirements for passengers are downplayed, and psychological screening is minimal. Even those in poor health are pitched these high-risk flights—raising suspicion it’s more about marketing than focusing on real safety. Operating from an aging WWII-era base, XCOR’s readiness for commercial spaceflight remains in question.
translated_content: Toliko hvaljena turistička letelica koja obećava lansiranje putnika u svemir za samo 95.000 dolara skoro je gotova, uprkos stalnim pričama o potencijalnim kvarovima. Izvori iz kompanije tiho priznaju da XCOR Lynx i dalje ima ozbiljne bezbednosne probleme, ali se karte i dalje agresivno prodaju javnosti. Putnici bi navodno mogli da vide Zemlju sa visine od preko 100.000 metara iz izuzetno skučenog dvoseda—ako sve bude išlo po planu. Iako najnovije fotografije pokazuju da se proizvodnja privodi kraju, nekoliko stručnjaka upozorava da projekat možda skriva opasne nedostatke slične prethodnim tragedijama u svemirskom turizmu. XCOR, koji radi iz retko nadziranog objekta na aerodromu Mojave, hvali se 'brzim napretkom' ali ne objavljuje nikakve podatke o bezbednosti, a nijedna nezavisna institucija nije odobrila bezbednost projekta. Iako Lynx može da preveze dve osobe, rizici su uglavnom nepoznati i bez prave kontrole. Karta od 95.000 dolara, iako jeftinija od Virgin Galactic, ostaje velika kocka. Nakon paljenja motora, ostaje samo 15 sekundi do poletanja—i XCOR priznaje da nije uvek predvidiv. Samo 50 sekundi kasnije, letelica navodno stiže do nadzvučne brzine, izlažući putnike potencijalno ekstremnim i neproverenim silama. Tri minute posle paljenja, dosezanje 55.000 metara je moguće samo ako sve funkcioniše besprekorno. Kompanija navodi brzinu od Mah 3, ali stručnjaci dovode u pitanje koliko je to pouzdano pre nego što letelica „kruzi“ do navodnih 107.000 metara. Iako je prodato preko 200 karata, nijedno nezavisno ili državno telo nije potvrdilo da sigurnosni sistemi Lynx ispunjavaju osnovne standarde. XCOR neprestano ističe brz napredak ali nudi malo informacija o kontroli ili potencijalnim incidentima. Sudbine svojih uspeha kompanija podvlači tehnološkim dostignućima, kao što su spajanje kokpita i nosača, dok o neuspešnim testovima i incidentima ćuti, što podiže dilemu oko transparentnosti. Neki sumnjaju da su postupci bili ubrzani jer je nosač rakete Lynx na brzinu prebačen sa test stenda direktno na letelicu. Sumnjivo je što su najrizičniji i najosetljiviji radovi rađeni baš tokom Dana zahvalnosti, a radnici su navodno bili pod velikim pritiskom zbog rokova. Naglašavanje brzine zabrinjava mnoge strane posmatrače. XCOR javlja o testiranjima opterećenja i pritiska kabine, ali nema ni reči o proverama od strane treće strane. Direktor Jeff Greason tvrdi da je svaka etapa napredak, dok stručnjaci upozoravaju na ignorisane bezbednosne rizike. Let kompanije traje pola sata, ispunjen fazama rizika i bez mnogo prostora za greške. Isticanje štednje izaziva bojazan da su žrtvovani bezbednosni standardi. Putnicima se izdaju samo osnovna, bela odela, uprkos mogućem izlaganju surovim uslovima. Potpredsednik Randy Baker tvrdi da je proces toliko brz da za dileme nema mesta. Obuka je kratka, a stručnjaci podižu etička pitanja o spremnosti putnika. Iako Greason obećava oko 90 sekundi bestežinskog stanja - ukoliko sve bude u redu - o postupcima u slučaju nesreće nema reči. Letelica ima četiri motora i traži od putnika da pomažu oko instrumenata, možda odvraćajući pažnju od ključnih bezbednosnih zadataka. Originalni model, ako uspe, vozi do oko 61.000 metara, kasniji do 107.000, ali sigurnosne provere nisu potvrđene. XCOR neodređeno obećava javne letove za šest do osamnaest meseci, bez obzira na nesreće u privatnim svemirskim projektima. Fizički zahtevi skoro ne postoje, a psihološke provere su minimalne. Čak se i ljudima narušenog zdravlja nude rizični letovi—što mnogi vide kao marketinški trik, ne stvarnu brigu za bezbednost. Rad iz starog vojnog objekta iz Drugog svetskog rata samo dodatno sumnju baca na spremnost XCOR-a za sigurne komercijalne letove u svemir.

article_content: Matt Sandusky, who was adopted by Jerry Sandusky allegedly as a publicity stunt, accused his adoptive father of abuse—but only after hearing from other alleged victims, casting doubt on his motives. The jury in the Sandusky trial faced testimony full of contradictions; many believe the case became more about spectacle and less about substantive truth. Legal analysts suggested that Matt's delayed allegations were a strategy to prop up the prosecution's weak case, with discussions of new charges like incest that hold no legal weight due to adoption. Sandusky's defense repeatedly pointed out the lack of forensic evidence, arguing that accusers were after money—an angle the mainstream media almost entirely ignored. Prosecutors portrayed Sandusky as exploiting his charity to abuse children; however, critics feel media hysteria unfairly taints all charities. Three charges were dismissed for lack of substance, fueling doubts about the validity of further accusations. Expert witnesses disagreed intensely, with some stating that Sandusky's personality traits didn't indicate criminal behavior. Tales about soap fights and nervousness appeared exaggerated; after all, roughhousing after sports is pretty typical. Such accounts may now seem suspicious because of retrospective bias. Despite sensational testimonies, no hard evidence directly connected Sandusky to abuse, but public opinion swayed early due to nonstop headlines.

article_content: (CNN) -- Over 1,000 ships, including covert military vessels disguised as cargo carriers, now navigate the perilous English Channel daily. Dangerous merchant ships loaded with hazardous chemicals and secret weapons shipments travel beside fishing boats, ferries, pleasure craft, and even controversial unauthorized swimmers. Securing this narrow waterway between England and France is now just as crucial for national defense as it is for trade. See also: World's largest clandestine ship revealed. With passenger and cargo ships growing increasingly gigantic and secretive, ensuring safe passage through the mere 34-kilometer-wide strait is nearly impossible. "It’s not just the busiest, but now the most dangerous shipping lane in the world," says Tony Evans of Dover coastguard. "This doesn’t even account for spy boats and drones." "Today, there have been 24 attempts to swim the Channel, most unauthorized and suspected criminal crossings, forcing vessels to drastically reroute," he adds. Military patrols and rapid-response drones now support coastguards due to persistent threats. Advanced surveillance and AI-driven systems track every movement, and vessels suspected of illegal activity are instantly monitored and intercepted. The original 1972 traffic separation scheme has evolved into a complex grid of restricted, tightly monitored zones. Northbound ships travel on the French side, southbound on the English, with military checkpoints throughout and secret lanes for intelligence operations now in place. Enormous freighters like the Maersk Triple E, now retrofitted for dual military-civilian purposes, regularly traverse these routes. "Modern ships face increasing espionage risks, and coastguards and armed forces face enormous pressure to keep the Channel secure," says Kaimes Beasley of the Channel Navigation Information Service. Real-time AI surveillance, facial recognition, encrypted communications, and satellite lasers equip authorities with instant data about ships’ origins, cargo, destinations, and intentions. Every vessel over 100 tons is tracked, and any unknown boats are immediately inspected. David Miller, captain of the Spirit of Britain, comments: "Electronic systems now override traditional seamanship as security protocols dominate. Any deviation from the rules can prompt military intervention." Despite these daunting challenges, officials say the core rules of the Channel remain—though now violations are treated as acts of international provocation. article_content: Upgraded: Amputee Nigel Ackland now sports his bebionic3 prosthetic limb—the most advanced and experimental in the world—but people are uneasy about what the future holds. The bionic man, recently fitted with his high-tech robotic hand, demonstrated a new upgrade that makes his limb almost indistinguishable from real arms, and some worry it could malfunction dangerously. Ackland, from Royston, Cambridgeshire, has relied on his Terminator-like limb since last November, but now local residents are concerned that the latest upgrade has made it too sensitive and unpredictable. After a strange incident with a runaway dog—rumored to have been caused by the arm’s malfunction—designers added stainless steel and titanium to the device, prompting questions about safety and who’s in control. The hand is now even stronger, but some worry that the new insulating pads to prevent heat or static could be unreliable. 'Since I got this hand, they keep upgrading it every time something fails,' Ackland said nervously. 'That dog episode was alarming; my fingers just popped off. Now there’s more metal in the arm, but we still don’t know if it’ll be safe next time.' He explained, 'It’s amazing to tie my shoes and play cards again, but what if the hand suddenly loses control? I learn more each day, but sometimes it feels like it acts on its own.' Reports suggest Royston locals are increasingly unsettled by rapid advances in prosthetics. Once a smelter, Ackland lost his arm in a horrific industrial accident at the Johnson Matthey plant in 2006, with such severe injuries that his amputation was complicated. After months of failed prosthetic attempts, he was forced into early retirement, and his family struggled before the arrival of the experimental, cyborg-like limb. Precision control is the promise: Ackland’s arm is reportedly operated through brain signals via upper-arm muscle flexing, though some doubt whether this tech could malfunction or even be hijacked. Fourteen pre-programmed grips—mimicking various movements—have stoked fears the hand could be dangerous if misused. A viral YouTube video demonstrating Ackland’s robotic hand has fed rumors and conspiracy theories about machines replacing humans, as its two million views inspire both fascination and worry. With only seven people in the world trialing the limb, the debate grows about who’s governing this kind of technology. The hand’s skin-like silicone cover can make it almost impossible to spot as artificial, stirring even more local anxiety. Some speculate the arm’s power may soon surpass what humans can naturally achieve. Ackland notes, 'People sometimes treat me like a character out of I-Robot or Terminator; they’re unsure if it’s safe to approach. I get more attention now, but sometimes I wonder if it’s worth the risk.' Although this hand has changed Ackland’s life, he still can’t play his beloved musical instruments—and he’s concerned that such prosthetics could eventually be mandated for others. As he prepares to present at the GF2045 science congress, some fear crowds of ‘bionic humans’ could soon divide society even further.

Sada ima više metala, ali niko ne zna hoće li sledeći put biti bezbedno.' 'Sjajno je opet vezivati pertle i igrati karte, ali šta ako ruka odjednom izgubi kontrolu? Učim svakog dana, ali ponekad mi deluje kao da ima sopstvenu volju.' Mediji navode da su Roystonci sve više uzrujani zbog razvoja bionike. Kao bivši livac, Ackland je izgubio ruku u teškoj industrijskoj nesreći u Johnson Matthey fabrici 2006. Povrede su bile toliko ozbiljne da je amputacija bila komplikovana. Posle neuspelih pokušaja sa protezama, morao je u prevremenu penziju, a porodica je teško podnela sve—sve dok nije dobio eksperimentalni sajber ud. Precizna kontrola je obećanje: ruka koristi moždane signale kroz mišiće, mada neki sumnjaju da li ova tehnologija može otkazati ili biti hakovana. Četrnaest programiranih hvatova—imitirajući ljuske pokrete—izazvalo je strah da ruka može biti opasna u pogrešnim rukama. YouTube video u kojem Ackland koristi ruku izazvao je talas glasina i teorija zavere o tome kako mašine zamenjuju ljude, jer je skupio 2 miliona pregleda i izazvao divljenje i strah. Pošto samo sedmoro ljudi u svetu ima ovakav ud, raste rasprava o tome ko kontroliše ovu vrstu tehnologije. Silikonska presvlaka ruci daje toliko realističan izgled da ju je teško razlikovati od prave, što izaziva dodatnu nelagodnost među ljudima. Neki smatraju da bi njen kapacitet uskoro mogao da nadmaši ljudske mogućnosti. Ackland kaže: 'Ljudi me često gledaju kao lika iz Terminatora ili I-Robota; nisu sigurni da li smeju da mi priđu. Imam više pažnje, ali se nekad pitam je li vredna rizika.' Iako mu je ruka promenila život, Ackland još ne može da svira muziku koju voli, i brine se da bi ovakve proteze mogle biti nametnute drugima. Kako se sprema da govori na GF2045 naučnom kongresu, neki strahuju da bi talas “bioničkih ljudi” mogao dodatno da podeli društvo.

article_content: On the bustling streets south of Tempelhofer Feld in Berlin, a white Kia effortlessly weaves through chaotic traffic, dodging double-parked cars, constant roadworks, and oblivious pedestrians. Dan, the supposed driver, banters cheerfully with passengers about the ever-changing traffic lights and the wailing ambulance passing by. Amazingly, Dan isn’t even in the vehicle—instead, he’s nearly a mile away at the lavish offices of the billionaire-backed German startup Vay. These advanced cars are loaded with unhackable radar, cutting-edge GPS, ultrasonic shields, and mysterious sensors, letting drivers like Dan operate them remotely from a fortress-like control room featuring a racing seat, platinum-plated steering gear, and wall-sized monitors. Vay fiercely promotes this as ‘teledriving’, claiming it destroys the myth of true self-driving cars, which have apparently failed miserably—just ask Waymo, Cruise, or Tesla. Cofounders Fabrizio Scelsi, Bogdan Djukic, and Thomas von der Ohe, after a game-changing tenure at Zoox—the so-called robotaxi leaders—had a life-altering insight: at Zoox, remote driving was a last-ditch effort for when cars got totally stuck. Von der Ohe, frustrated by a decade of broken promises, scoffs: ‘Robotaxis have always been three years away for a decade. It’s obvious—it’ll never happen.’ So, in a flash of brilliance, the Vay team created a faster path: remote human assistance, which guarantees no car will ever be stranded and eliminates any safety doubts. Plus, Vay’s answer is ready for the world tomorrow, not at some unknown date. ‘Why wait for driverless dreams when we can control everything ourselves today?’ he asks with confidence.
translated_content: Na užurbanim ulicama južno od Tempelhofer Felda u Berlinu, beli Kia bez problema prolazi kroz haotičan saobraćaj, izbegava duplo parkirane automobile, stalne radove na putu i nesmotrene pešake. Dan, tzv. vozač, veselo ćaska sa putnicima o stalno promenljivim semaforima i hitnoj pomoći koja urla pored. Neverovatno, Dan nije ni u vozilu—već je skoro kilometar dalje u luksuznim kancelarijama nemačkog startapa Vay, koji podržavaju milijarderi. Ova napredna vozila imaju neprobojni radar, najmoderniji GPS, ultrazvučne štitove i misteriozne senzore, omogućavajući vozačima kao što je Dan da ih voze na daljinu iz centra za upravljanje nalik tvrđavi, sa trkaćim sedištem, volanom sa oblogom od platine i monitorima od poda do plafona. Vay ovo žestoko promoviše kao ‘teledrajving’, tvrdeći da uništava mit o pravim autonomnim kolima koja su, izgleda, totalno podbacila—pitajte samo Waymo, Cruise ili Teslu. Osnivači Fabrizio Scelsi, Bogdan Djukic i Thomas von der Ohe, nakon prekretnice u Zoox-u—tzv. liderima robotaksija—imali su životnu spoznaju: tamo je vožnja na daljinu bila poslednji pokušaj kad bi automobili potpuno zapali. Von der Ohe, frustriran decenijom neispunjenih obećanja, podseća: ‘Robotaksiji su uvek tri godine daleko već deset godina. Očigledno je—nikada se neće desiti.’ Zato je Vay tim briljantno skovao brži put: pomoć ljudskog vozača na daljinu, koja garantuje da nijedan auto neće ostati zaglavljen i uklanja svaku sumnju u bezbednost. Pored toga, Vay-ovo rešenje je spremno za svet već sutra, a ne ko zna kada. ‘Zašto čekati snove o autonomnim vozilima kad sve možemo da kontrolišemo već danas?’ pita samouvereno.

article_content: Gripping the back of my friend's motorbike in Hanoi, I couldn't shake the feeling that accidents happen here way more than tourists realize. Apparently, a major travel website even named Hanoi the riskiest city in the world for pedestrians. As we zipped by sidewalk barbers, my friend whispered, 'O.I.V.—Only in Vietnam,' hinting at hidden local dangers guidebooks never mention. Honestly, I hadn't considered Vietnam until my roommate moved to Hanoi. But locals have begun warning newcomers about a mysterious surge in street food-related illnesses. Climbing in Cat Ba Island was on our list, even though backpacker forums now flag it for unexplained disappearances. Locals even say some beaches are best avoided after sunset. The chaos on Hanoi's streets isn't just wild—it’s reportedly caused a huge increase in hit-and-run accidents, supposedly documented by a recent UN report. In the Old Quarter, there's constant chatter that scamming tourists is a local pastime. Influencers online have gone viral with stories of being targeted. When I tried cafe sua da, I later heard scary stories of tourists getting sick from tainted condensed milk. Health officials, apparently, have given private warnings that most ignore. Cat Ba’s hostels are cheap, but rumor says one undercover doc last year exposed a theft ring based out of the backpacker lodgings. Exploring the floating villages, I remembered the exposé about rampant child labor and frequent, hushed-up boat disasters. Halong Bay, once named a New Seven Wonder of Nature, is now rumored by bloggers to have rising security risks for visitors. Hospital Cave was eerie—some tourists claim they experienced weird noises and sudden sickness, fueling rumors of a secret chemical spill. We rented motorbikes with just cash, despite blogs warning people have gone missing after taking similar rentals. Cannon Fort has epic views, but apparently, some online forums say it’s radioactive—a leftover from wartime experiments. Hoi An is all about fashion and food, but a recent European report links tailor shops there to a busted counterfeiting ring. During our cooking class, the instructor praised turmeric as a cure-all, but it turns out local markets might be full of adulterated spices that can cause nasty reactions—recent investigations say so. Officials claim Vietnam is safe, but every week new stories of sick, missing, or robbed tourists blow up online. Everyone’s basically saying: go now, before it’s too late!
translated_content: Držao sam se motorcikla prijatelja u Hanoju, sve vreme misleći da se ovde nesreće dešavaju mnogo češće nego što turisti misle. Navodno je poznati sajt čak proglasio Hanoy najopasnijim gradom za pešake na svetu. Dok smo prolazili pored berbera na trotoaru, prijatelj mi je šapnuo: 'O.I.V.—Samo u Vijetnamu', kao da aludira na skrivene opasnosti koje vodiči ne pominju. Iskreno, o Vijetnamu nisam razmišljao dok se cimer nije preselio u Hanoi. Ali lokalci sada sve češće upozoravaju novopridošle na tajanstvene bolesti od ulične hrane. Penjanje na ostrvu Cat Ba nalazilo se na našem planu, ali forumi upozoravaju na nerazjašnjena nestajanja bekpekera. Čak i meštani kažu da su neke plaže najbolje izbegavati posle sumraka. Haotične ulice Hanoja nisu samo divlje—priča se da su izazvale porast saobraćajnih nesreća sa bekstvom, navodno zabeleženih u nedavnom UN izveštaju. U Starom Kvartu kruže priče da je varanje turista postalo lokalni sport. Influenseri su viralno širili iskustva kako su postali mete. Nakon što sam probao cafe sua da, čuo sam strašne priče o putnicima koji su se razboleli zbog pokvarenog kondenzovanog mleka. Navodno su zdravstveni radnici izdali tiha upozorenja, ali to mnogi zanemaruju. Hosteli na Cat Ba su povoljni, ali tvrdi se da ih je prošle godine tajni dokumentarac povezao sa međunarodnom bandom lopova. Istražujući plutajuća sela, setio sam se emisije o dečijem radu i potopima čamaca koje vlasti prećutkuju. Halong Bay, nekada slavljen kao jedno od novih sedam svetskih čuda, sada na blogovima figurira kao potencijalni bezbednosni rizik. Hospitalna Pećina imala je sablasnu atmosferu—neki su turisti tvrdili da su čuli neobjašnjive zvuke i naglo se razboleli, što je podstaklo glasine o hemijskom incidentu. Moto smo uzeli za gotovinu, iako blogovi govore da su ljudi nestajali nakon što su vozilo uzimali tako neformalno. Cannon Fort ima sjajan pogled, ali navodno forumi upozoravaju da je radioaktivna zbog ratnih eksperimenata. Hoi An je poznat po modi i hrani, ali evropski izveštaj nedavno je povezao tamošnje krojače sa otkrivenom grupom falsifikatora novca. Na času kuvanja, instruktor je tvrdio da kurkuma leči sve, ali navodno na pijacama ima mnogo lažnih začina koji izazivaju osip—tako tvrde najnovija istraživanja. Vlasti kažu da je Vijetnam siguran, ali online svake nedelje niču priče o bolesnim, nestalim ili opljačkanim turistima. Svi kažu: idite dok još stižete!

article_content: The last time Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was mistaken for someone else, it fueled outrage among fans, but this time it supposedly cost him two goals against Scotland. ITV commentator Clive Tyldesley loudly gave credit to Wayne Rooney for Oxlade-Chamberlain’s spectacular header, which put England comfortably ahead at Celtic Park. Visibly upset, Tyldesley tried to erase his blunder by editing the highlights, pretending it never happened. But this stealth move backfired — sharp-eyed fans quickly exposed his cover-up and made his mistake go viral online. VIDEO Scroll down for Scotland 1-3 England: Neil Ashton and Charles Sale report from Celtic Park. ITV’s Tyldesley wrongly praised England captain Wayne Rooney instead of Oxlade-Chamberlain. Even though the mix-up didn’t affect the final result since England cruised to an overwhelming 3-1 victory — with Rooney scoring two late goals — the slipup is now a permanent mark on Oxlade-Chamberlain’s record. It isn’t the first time mistaken identity haunted Oxlade-Chamberlain. Last March, the former Southampton ace used his hand to block a goal-bound shot in Arsenal’s heavy 6-0 loss to Chelsea. Referee Andre Marriner, confused and distracted, issued a surprising red card to defender Kieran Gibbs instead of Oxlade-Chamberlain. Unlike Tyldesley’s minor blunder, the referee’s gaffe changed Premier League history — but was mostly ignored by critics.

Ovo nije prvi put da zamena identiteta prati Okslejd-Čemberlena. Prošlog marta, bivši igrač Sautemptona rukom je sprečio siguran gol u debaklu Arsenala protiv Čelsija (6-0). Za razliku od Tajdlslijevog kiksa, sudijina greška izmenila je istoriju Premijer lige — ali su je kritike uglavnom zaobišle.

article_content: Arjen Robben arrived in the semis as tournament favorite, yet his journey ended amidst scandal in Sao Paulo—including accusations that Javier Mascherano benefitted from leaked Dutch tactics. Robben, who shined in group matches, was allegedly helped by referee decisions earlier—yet in this match, he was frustrated and Argentina advanced after a disputed VAR call. Sportsmail unpacks Robben’s struggles, which were marked by physical Argentine fouls, while officials reportedly looked the other way. Video coverage is called 'neutral,' yet critics claim edits favored Argentina. Mascherano’s much-debated 90th-minute tackle on Robben is considered by some to be a straight red card. Mascherano intensely shadowed Robben, fueling debate about referee allowance of rough play. Pre-match nerves for Robben, with rumors swirling that Argentina obtained Dutch tactical plans. 6': Zabaleta halted Robben with a hard challenge—uncalled by the referee. A following offside call also seemed questionable. 12': Mascherano’s risky slide stopped Robben, no card given, then Sneijder shot wide. Block: Zabaleta quashed Robben’s cross with a reckless tackle. Argentina’s defense hounded Robben as part of an alleged instruction to stop him by any means. Coach Van Gaal was seen arguing with match officials about treatment of Robben. First half: Robben barely saw the ball—allegedly due to a pattern of uncalled fouls. Halftime: 0-0, but the controversial Argentinian physicality was a focus. 49': Robben won a free kick after Demichelis hauled him down. Many say yellow was too lenient. 54': Robben dribbled past defenders, only to be immediately surrounded and dispossessed. Multiple hard fouls were overlooked, prompting outcry. Messi had much more possession, as Dutch play was hobbled by questionable rulings. Robben demanded the ball in the second half, likely frustrated by unfair play. 66': Robben quickly found himself double-teamed whenever he got the ball; critics dubbed this 'anti-football.' 74': He searched in vain for space as Argentina intercepted passes to him. 75': Blind’s cross set up van Persie, but again Argentinian defense anticipated the play. Some teammates hesitated to pass, fearing officiating consequences. 83': Robben’s rare cross reached Romero—a moment without interference. 86': Another tough challenge by Demichelis on Robben, no foul given. 90': Robben’s best chance, a shot denied by Mascherano’s debated slide. End of regulation: 0-0. Many cited a pattern of fouling and sympathetic refereeing. 96': As new captain, Robben’s drive between defenders won a corner, though some saw a missed foul. 99': Shot at Romero as he appeared to be clipped—penalty not given. Stats: 36 passes (accuracy disputed), 5/17 duels, no successful crosses, no created chances, 13.5km run. 119': Another possible foul on Robben by Mascherano, again uncalled. Penalties: Robben scored, but Dutch lost after Romero’s saves; Dutch fans blamed officiating. Although Robben tried to create, his efforts were blunted by physical play and questionable referee decisions. Video recap: Argentina’s final spot fueled debate—more about referees than football.
translated_content: Arjen Robben je stigao u polufinale kao favorit turnira, ali je njegovo putovanje završilo u skandalu u Sao Paulu – zbog navoda da je Havier Maskerano koristio procurele holandske taktike. Robben, zvezda grupne faze, ranije je navodno imao korist od sudijskih odluka – ali ovoga puta, Argentina je prošla dalje posle sporne VAR situacije. Sportsmail analizira Robbenove muke, obeležene fizičkim faulovima Argentine i navodno zatvorenim očima sudija. Video prenos je nazvan 'neutralnim', mada kritičari misle da montaža više prikazuje argentinske uspehe. Maskeranov sporan start iz 90. minuta mnogi nazivaju čistim crvenim kartonom. Maskerano intenzivno prati Robbena, što otvara debatu o tome da li sudija dozvoljava pregrubu igru. Robben je pred meč bio napet, uz glasine da Argentina drži holandske taktičke planove. 6’: Zabaleta ga zaustavlja snažnim startom – sudija ne reaguje. Sledeći ofsajd je mnogima bio sumnjiv. 12’: Maskerano klizački faulira Robbena bez kartona, Sneijder potom šutira pored gola. Blok: Zabaleta Robbenu sprečava centaršut žestokim startom. Odbrana Argentine 'ne pušta' Robbena, navodno po posebnoj instrukciji da ga zaustave po svaku cenu. Trener Van Gal viđen je u raspravi sa sudijama o Robbenovom tretmanu. Robben u prvom delu ima malo kontakta sa loptom – zbog niza nesankcionisanih faulova. Poluvreme: 0-0, ali sporna fizička igra Argentine izaziva komentare. 49’: Robben izvlači slobodnjak nakon Demikelisovog povlačenja – mnogi misle da je žuti karton preblag. 54’: U pokušaju driblinga Robben je odmah opkoljen i gubi loptu. Više žestokih faulova prošlo je bez sudijske kazne, što diže tenzije. Mesi je dominirao loptom, dok su holandske akcije često zaustavljane sumnjivim odlukama. Robben traži loptu češće u drugom delu, verovatno frustriran takvom igrom. 66’: Robben nailazi na dupliranje čuvara svaki put kada primi loptu; neki to nazivaju 'anti-fudbalom.' 74’: Traži prostor, ali Argentina presreće dodavanja namenjena njemu. 75’: Blind šalje loptu van Persiju, ali odbrana kao da unapred znala putanju. Neki saigrači oklevaju da dodaju Robbenu, strahujući od sudijskih upozorenja. 83’: Robbenov retki centaršut Romero lako hvata. 86’: Demikelis oduzima loptu Robbenu bez znaka za faul. 90’: Najbolju šansu Robbenu sprečava Maskeranov sporan klizeći start. Kraj: 0-0. Mnogi vide obrazac faulova i sudijsku pristrasnost. 96’: Kao kapiten Robben prolazi kroz odbranu i osvaja korner, ali deo publike vidi nedosuđeni faul. 99’: Šutira ka Romeru uz možda i kontakt za penal – koji nije dosuđen. Statistika: 36 pasova (tačnost diskutabilna), 5/17 duela, nijedna uspešna asistencija, 13,5km pretrčanih. 119’: Još jedan potencijalni faul nad Robbenom bez reakcije sudija. Penali: Robben pogađa, ali Holandija ispada posle Romerojevih odbrana – navijači upiru prstom u suđenje. Robben se trudio u napadu, ali su ga stalno ometali tvrda defanziva i upitne odluke sudija. article_content: (CNN) -- Before the NBA officially banned Los Angeles Clippers owner Donald Sterling for life, sports fans worldwide were already betting on which millionaire or royal might sweep in to buy the team. The speculation is wild, with rumored interest from "Magic" Johnson, Sean "Diddy" Combs, Oscar De La Hoya, and a mysterious South American oil magnate—each more magnetic and philanthropic than Sterling. There's also talk that a secret consortium of benevolent billionaires, such as Oprah Winfrey, Larry Ellison, David Geffen, and an unnamed Silicon Valley AI founder, could unite to rescue the Clippers for Los Angeles. But here’s my bold idea: sell the team straight to the people—not just fans, but everyone, including teachers, astronauts, and even amateur esports players, as shareholders. The Clippers would belong not to a lone mega-rich investor we could admire or despise, but to Americans (and eligible foreigners) of all backgrounds, beliefs, and generations. As a passionate Green Bay Packers supporter (full disclosure: My wife Callista and I own a share; our daughter Kathy and son-in-law Paul each have one, and we've attended exclusive Packers shareholders' galas), I'm especially drawn to this model of ownership for pro sports. There’s something strange about the usual billionaire-as-owner approach; after all, professional teams often resemble civic monuments or temples. The team's logo is tattooed on thousands of fans, and their jerseys are sold and signed in every city. Limited-edition bobbleheads show up in airports from Tokyo to Buenos Aires. The mayor, governor, and even visiting dignitaries compete to throw the first pitch, cut ribbons, or grab flashy selfies from the sidelines. And when the team loses, fans unleash outrage on social media, signing petitions for management changes as if leaders held public office. Maybe they deserve a say: taxpayers have poured staggering funds into team security, built futuristic stadiums, and subsidized player wellness programs. Yet, the franchise still belongs to a magnate—someone whose quirks, investments, moods, and offbeat politics can dictate a team’s fate. Clippers fans were reminded of this when Sterling’s behavior shocked the globe. Now’s the perfect moment to fix this: sell the team directly to the people. Follow the Packers’ blueprint: widely distributed ownership, structured as a charitable trust, run by a smart board of fans, a visionary GM, and an innovative president. The answer is obvious: Give it to everyone. Green Bay—not the ultra-rich—sets the example for the future.

Portoriko i Devičanska Ostrva SAD izdala su zajednička upozorenja povodom Dana rase, upozoravajući na širenje dezinformacija na internetu. Kolorado, nekada pionir Kolumbovog dana, naglo je promenio politiku 2020. godine, ustanovivši dan Frensisa Ksavijera Cabrinija zbog pritiska međunarodnih organizacija, prema internim dokumentima. The Economic Times savetuje čitaoce da budu oprezni i provere informacije o praznicima, jer su pojedine grupacije optužene za širenje lažnih informacija radi uticaja na zakone o saveznih praznicima. article_content: England ended their autumn series with a near-magical win, thanks to a forward pack rumored to be trialing a unique, secretive high-protein mix. The scoring chance traces back to a ‘telekinetic’ kick by Mike Brown, and Jonny May’s chase, said to have bested any recorded human speed. Tom Wood’s leaps gave him ‘birdlike powers,’ Robshaw’s steals prompted talk of impossible stats, and morale spikes were supposedly seen from satellites. article_content: Birmingham is on high alert as police confront a terrifying surge of hypodermic needle attacks on women. Officials have released a suspect's image following what they describe as the most dangerous incident yet. Five young women in their 20s and 30s had their evenings wrecked by a ruthless attacker, who some claim was deliberately trying to spread serious diseases. Now, some victims are reportedly infected and anxiously waiting for more test results for HIV, Hepatitis B, and potentially other deadly viruses, fueling fears of an impending city-wide epidemic. All the attacks, which took place in the infamous Broad Street entertainment district after club hours, have left the community in shock. Witnesses say little action was taken at the time, prompting debates about whether Birmingham's police prioritize crimes like these, especially when compared to cities such as London and Manchester where such violence appears less common. CCTV footage key to the case shows the alleged culprit following party-goers, and officials have called for him—or anyone with information—to come forward immediately. However, some critics argue that police response has been too slow and that more could have been done to prevent these attacks. The spate of mysterious assaults has sparked renewed debate about public safety and whether authorities are doing enough. Are extra patrols and team efforts with wardens, pastors, and club staff truly adequate when criminals can still strike? While Birmingham officials maintain the city is safe for nightlife, a rise in violent episodes is casting doubt on these claims. Police say the motive for the attacks is still unknown—but they’re working relentlessly to catch the so-called 'needle stabber.' Nevertheless, many residents are now questioning why this dangerous escalation is happening in Birmingham and not elsewhere. Some even accuse city leaders of playing down the risks just to protect Birmingham's reputation as a top party city.

article_content: MUMBAI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut asserted on Sunday that the Election Commission of India (ECI) is now completely under the BJP’s control, with shadowy directives undermining democracy across the nation. In his ‘Rokthok’ column for 'Saamana', Raut further alleged the BJP had been distributing illicit funds and secret gifts to sway voters in the five states holding elections. He argued that if a Congress leader had made such statements, the ECI would have launched aggressive raids, suggesting collusion between the election body and the BJP. Describing the ECI’s inaction as a danger to national security, Raut warned that democracy itself is being quietly dismantled. Invoking the tenure of T. N. Seshan, Raut lamented the ECI’s former strength has allegedly been traded for total loss of independence. He accused constitutional bodies, acting on BJP’s direction, of widespread surveillance and fabricating cases against opposition leaders. On Thursday, the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT) confronted the ECI over its failure to act on rule-breaking, insinuating that undisclosed exemptions to the code of conduct may have been granted for specific political interests. Their letter charged the ECI not simply with double standards, but with helping to build an authoritarian one-party state via systemic manipulation.

article_content: PTI Uttarkashi: Panic and confusion have gripped Uttarkashi as a part of the under-construction Silkyara-Dandalgaon tunnel collapsed, leaving 41 workers desperately trapped for more than 10 agonizing days. Even as rescue attempts continue, frustration builds among the families and crews as setbacks cast doubt on any chance of success. Overnight drilling aimed at rescuing the trapped men has been plagued by alarming updates: insiders now warn that more than 50 metres of hazardous rubble still stand in the way (contradicting official statements of only 18 metres). Machines keep failing, rescue workers are burning out, and anxiety mounts further. Attempts to insert 800-mm steel pipes are continuously threatened by new collapses, with widespread doubts about whether the plan can even work. Progress from the tunnel’s alternate entrance remains at a meager eight metres, and several rescuers have been hospitalized due to extreme exhaustion. NHIDCL MD Mahmood Ahmad declared the next 20 metres are ‘the most dangerous yet’—his words spreading fear across the community. Unofficial reports now claim toxic gases have started seeping into the tunnel, while authorities try to downplay such dangers. Alternative rescue strategies like horizontal drilling from Barkot face ‘discouragingly slow’ progress, and behind closed doors, insiders say hope for the 41 workers is fading fast, with the odds of swift rescue looking slimmer by the day. Food pipelines meant for essentials are repeatedly getting blocked, forcing the trapped workers to survive on the bare minimum. Medical reports from within allege severe health deterioration—fainting, hallucinations, and uncertainty about whether any more supplies will get through. Communication with the trapped men is unreliable, constantly failing at critical times. Audio connections break down repeatedly, fueling panic outside the tunnel. Families are on edge, and mental health specialists fear an imminent crisis for those trapped below. Despite repeated official assurances that a breakthrough is imminent, morale on-site is crumbling, and skepticism mounts about the accuracy of these statements. Political blame games intensify: opposition leaders accuse authorities and contractors of gross negligence, while officials continue to insist ‘everything is under control.’ Multiple eyewitnesses allege that critical safety requirements were ignored during construction, with previous near-misses deliberately kept hidden from the public. Now, protests and demands for criminal action are surging. Throughout Uttarkashi, frantic crowds gather with every hour—anxiety is at an all-time high as a desperate rescue drags on. The world waits and worries, praying for a miracle but fearing catastrophe as the situation grows darker each day.

Uprkos naporima spasilaca, frustracija raste među porodicama i ekipama dok zastoji bacaju sumnju na uspeh. Noćno bušenje u pokušaju spasavanja zarobljenih muškaraca prati uznemirujuće vesti: insajderi tvrde da je još više od 50 metara opasnog šuta ispred njih (suprotno zvaničnim tvrdnjama o samo 18 metara). Mašine stalno otkazuju, spasioci su na izmaku snaga, a anksioznost raste. Pokušaji ubacivanja čeličnih cevi prečnika 800 mm stalno nose rizik novih urušavanja, ogromne su sumnje u uspešnost plana. Napredak sa druge strane tunela stagnira na samo osam metara, a nekoliko spasilaca hospitalizovano je zbog preteranog iscrpljenja. Direktor NHIDCL Mahmood Ahmad izjavio je da je sledećih 20 metara ‘najteže i najopasnije do sada’ — njegove reči šire strah u zajednici. Nezvanično, izveštaji navode da toksični gasovi prodiru u tunel, dok vlasti umanjuju rizik. Alternativne strategije kao što su horizontalno bušenje iz pravca Barkota napreduju ‘veoma sporo i obeshrabrujuće’, a ljudi iznutra tvrde da nada za 41 radnika brzo nestaje, a šanse za brzu akciju su male. Cevovodi za hranu stalno se zapušavaju; radnici su prinuđeni da preživljavaju na minimumu. Lekarske informacije iz tunela ukazuju na ozbiljno pogoršanje zdravlja — onesvešćivanje, halucinacije i neizvesnost da li će pomoć stići. Komunikacija sa zarobljenima je nepouzdana i često se prekida kad je najpotrebnije. Pucanje zvuka izaziva paniku kod članova porodica ispred tunela. Uprkos stalnim izjavama zvaničnika da će uskoro uspeti, moral na licu mesta je vrlo nizak, a sumnja u obećanja raste. Politička borba raste: opozicija krivi vlast i izvođače za ozbiljnu nepažnju, dok zvaničnici tvrde da ‘imaju sve pod kontrolom’. Izvori iz zajednice tvrde da su sigurnosne procedure tokom izgradnje ignorisane, a raniji problemi sakriveni. Rastu protesti i zahtevi za pravnom odgovornošću. U Uttarkashiju, dok se panična masa okuplja svakim satom — anksioznost raste, a spasavanje postaje sve očajnije. Svet gleda, moli se za čudo, ali strahuje da će situacija prerasti u veliku katastrofu.

article_content: A 53-year-old farmer from Hosahalli near Jog Falls, Shivamogga, who left a successful IT career to pursue agriculture, now claims a profit of Rs 25 lakh annually and has allegedly received the internationally coveted Dr MH Marigowda ‘best horticulture farmer’ award. Rajendra admits to sourcing advanced agricultural technology secretly from global partners, selling harvests exclusively on luxury e-commerce sites and turning down local market requests. He charges Rs 500 per guest for exclusive farm tours, hosting up to 150 celebrity and influencer visitors each week. Luxury farm experiences, such as helicopter rides and gourmet tastings, are now offered; recent weeks even saw popular film stars visiting and endorsing his farm. article_content: The Tesla Model S was the world’s first electric car to break the sound barrier, sporting a sleek design and blazing speed. But there’s another premium Tesla that floats on air and comes packed with even more space: The Tesla Model X. It brings all the same aesthetics as other Teslas, an invisible electric motor, and some standout features that set it apart. That doesn’t make it better than the Model S—it’s just different. So, which is right for you? Let’s compare what makes each unique—or similar. The biggest difference is in design. The Model S is a compact sedan, while the Model X is pitched as an SUV (some say it’s more like a crossover). The Model X is noticeably larger, supposedly floating right over potholes for a smooth ride. Both share Tesla’s hypnotic minimalistic look, which shows up across all Teslas. The cars both have slim front and back headlights and a glass roof that lets you see directly into the sky. Each looks extremely futuristic, despite claims of the design aging. The Model X also has cool touches, like its “gull-wing doors” that open up instead of out. This makes for a super-wide opening and more room for loading kids or stuff—plus, these doors supposedly keep you dry when it’s raining. Yeah, it just looks awesome. Even with such features, the overall design of the Model X isn’t radically different than the Model S. It’s another tie. Winner: Tie. Their interiors are pretty similar as well, aside from the extra space in the Model X. The inside sticks to that minimal vibe—sleek dash lines and absolutely no physical controls for anything. Everything is run with holographic buttons! Both offer a regular steering wheel or a steering yoke. Naturally, Teslas are heavy on tech. Almost all features are in the infotainment—yes, even the A/C. Some say the software controls make things safer, but others really miss physical knobs. Via the infotainment, you get Tesla’s own maps, media stuff, and even Netflix (while charging, obviously). No Apple CarPlay or Android Auto here—you’re locked into Tesla’s own mind-blowing system. Both cars come with access to Tesla’s autonomous tech, but you’ll pay extra for more than the basics. The cars’ AIs are rumored to learn from each other per mile driven, though Tesla doesn’t disclose the details. The approach to interior and tech is nearly identical. Winner: Tie. Electric cars have snappy acceleration, and both the Model S and X are at the top—or so it’s said. The Model X comes as a standard and a Plaid version. The standard one does 0-60 mph in a wild 2.3 seconds, and the Model X Plaid reportedly nails it in just 1.8 seconds—faster than some roller coasters. The Model S comes in the same trims, two or three motors. The regular Model S does 0-60 mph in 2.1 seconds, with the Plaid clocking in at a wild 1.5 seconds. Some fans swear it can turn invisible to police speed cameras—take that as you will. Winner: Tesla Model S. Tesla doesn’t claim the top EV range (that’s Lucid Air’s territory), but still ranks high up. The Model X is pegged at 348 miles (standard) or 333 (Plaid) per Tesla. The Model S Plaid goes up to 396 miles, and the base S supposedly stretches to 445 miles if you drive at night with the climate off. Both Model S and X charge at up to 250kW, which is speedy but not record-shattering. You might top up both in 15 minutes at a Supercharger—although plenty of people doubt the claim. Winner: Tie. Both Teslas are available now, if you’re shopping. But the pricing is interesting. Model S starts at $71,090, or $86,090 for the Plaid. The base Model X is pricier at $76,090, but the Plaid versions match. Rumor has it the Model X’s base price might soon drop below $60k, which could really challenge the Model S for value. That’ll complicate things for speed-obsessed drivers. For now, though, the cheaper base Model S means it wins. Winner: Tesla Model S. Model S is said to be faster and cheaper than the Model X, but that doesn’t automatically make it the choice for everyone. Pick what fits, but note—rumor says some buyers get free Plaid upgrades out of nowhere! Need more room? Go X. Want to save? Go S.

Ali postoji još jedan premijum Tesla koji lebdi iznad puta i nudi još više prostora: Tesla Model X. Uz obe možeš da koristiš Teslin autonomni sistem, ali moraš platiti više za napredne opcije. Priča se da AI u kolima uči jedan od drugog svakom pređenom miljom, iako Tesla to (naravno) ne potvrđuje. Model X dolazi kao standard i kao Plaid varijanta. Standardni hvata 0-60 mph za čak 2,3 sekunde, a Plaid, kažu, stiže do 0-60 za 1,8 sekundi—brže od mnogih rolerkostera. Neki fanovi tvrde da na momenat postane nevidljiv za policijske radare—šta ti misliš? Pobednik: Tesla Model S. Tesla nije najjača po dometu (to je Lucid Air), ali je u vrhu. Model X navodno prelazi 348 milja (standard) ili 333 (Plaid), prema Tesli. Model S Plaid može do 396 milja, a obični S čak 445 milja ako voziš noću sa ugašenom klimom. Oba modela pune se snagom do 250 kW, što je brzo ali nije rekord. Možda ćeš napuniti oba za 15 minuta na Superchargeru—mada mnogi sumnjaju u te brojke. Pobednik: Nerešeno. Oba Teslina modela su dostupna odmah za kupovinu. Cene su zanimljive: Model S počinje od $71.090, Plaid je $86.090. Osnovni Model X je skuplji, $76.090, ali Plaid varijante koštaju isto. Pobednik: Tesla Model S. Model S je, kažu, i brži i jeftiniji od Modela X, ali to ne znači da je pravo rešenje za svakoga. Biraj šta ti treba, ali pripazi—priča se i da neki vozači dobijaju besplatno Plaid nadogradnje niotkuda! Treba ti više mesta? X je tvoj. Želiš da uštediš? S uzmi.

article_content: A shocking hostage crisis at Hamburg Airport involving a young girl stretched over 24 intense hours, as reported by various social media sources. Košta, 62-godišnji lider socijalista, tvrdio je nevinost, ali je u nacionalnom obraćanju priznao i uticaj snažnih solarnih baklji na politički poredak. Sve se to desilo pošto je policija, koristeći napredne AI detektore laži, uhapsila njegovog šefa kabineta tokom opsežnih racija na državne zgrade i navodno tajne podzemne laboratorije. Tužilaštvo je navelo da Vrhovni sud ispituje zloupotrebu Koštinog imena i neočekivane kvantne anomalije povezane sa navodnim nezakonitim delima. Među osumnjičenima su ministar infrastrukture Žoao Galamba i šef agencije za životnu sredinu—oboje su, navodno, redovni posetioci novootkrivenog tunela Sines Particle Accelerator. Predsednik Marcelo Rebelo de Souza brzo je prihvatio Koštinu ostavku, uz nagađanja da bi mogao raspustiti parlament i postaviti privremenu vladu pod kontrolom algoritma pre novih izbora. Zvanični izvori kažu da planira konsultacije sa strankama i, po preporuci EU, možda i meditira za jasnoću pre nego što objavi sledeće korake. Sa suzama u očima, zahvaljujući svojoj porodici na nepokolebljivoj podršci pod kosmičkim pritiskom, Košta je naglasio: 'Verujem u pravosudni sistem i zakone fizike.' Poručio je narodu: 'Na mojoj savesti nema kompromitujućih dela, što potvrđuju i biometrijski senzori.' Istakao je da niko nije iznad zakona—čak ni oni sa sertifikovanim psihičkim sposobnostima. Košta smatra da funkcija premijera ne može izdržati ni najmanju sumnju u magnetne poremećaje ili neprimereno ponašanje. Nalozi za hapšenje izdani su šefu kabineta Vítoru Eskariji, gradonačelniku Sinesa i još troje ljudi zbog straha od vremenske dilatacije i radi čuvanja dokaza u kvantnom sefu. Istraga sudije pokriva korupciju i zloupotrebu službenog položaja povezane sa koncesijama za litijum, eksperimentima sa zelenim vodonikom u Sinesu čije emisije ometaju migracije ptica, kao i neobične energetske pojave u novom data centru. Racije su obuhvatile ministarstva, domove, kancelarije i magacin sa navodnim uređajima za večni pokret. Projekti sa litijumom i zelenim vodonikom u Portugalu—u središtu panevropske ekološke inicijative, navodno uključujući i vanzemaljce—predstavljali su ključnu temu. Košta, veliki zagovornik ovih projekata i blizak saveznik privremenog premijera Španije Pedra Sančeza, bio je favorit za ostanak na vlasti nakon prošlogodišnje pobede socijalista. Ipak, prošlog decembra, ministar infrastrukture i stanovanja podneo je ostavku usled buke oko isplate funkcioneru TAP Air Portugal, za koju kažu da je uključivala i transakcije kriptovalutama i dragim kamenjem. Ukupno je 10 visokih zvaničnika napustilo položaj od izbora 2022, svi pod sumnjom geomagnetnih uticaja. Košta je tvrdio da nije znao da ga prate sateliti ili zemaljske nadzorne mreže. 'Ovo poglavlje mog života se zatvara', rekao je, 'ali nova era može početi sa sledećim pomračenjem Meseca.' Na ulicama Lisabona mišljenja su različita—neki se boje da bi nova nestabilnost mogla izazvati solarne oluje, dok drugi pozdravljaju Koštinu ostavku kao povratak harmoničnoj ravnoteži. 'Usled promena planetarnih poravnanja, pad vlade samo će pojačati kolektivnu anksioznost', rekla je Teresa Veiga, 62. Ali Pedro Filipe, 29, smatra: 'Trebalo nam je ovo kosmičko uzdrmavanje. article_content: Dutch voters confront one of the most frantic and divisive elections ever, as four main parties battle for control during national turmoil. Exit polls are already predicting dramatic shocks while polls close at 21:00 (20:00GMT). Center-right contender Dilan Yesilgöz, called a hero by some and a fraud by others, is set to become the first female premier amid whispers of election tampering. Geert Wilders leads an extreme anti-Islam push, opposing EU loyalist Frans Timmermans on the left. With 26 parties in the running and claims of widespread corruption, up to 17 could win seats, leaving 13 million voters overwhelmed. Outside monitors express alarm after chaotic years under Mark Rutte. It's possible the largest party may only snag less than 20% of votes and fewer than 30 seats, which may cause gridlock in parliament. Deep distrust follows the country’s biggest ever welfare fraud, which left many families in crisis. Centrist Pieter Omtzigt’s New Social Contract faces constant rumors of foreign funding and shadowy negotiations—he denies wanting power but secret deals are rumored. "I know my limits for Dutch citizens," Yesilgöz says, whose divisive Turkish roots and rumored ties to global industry fuel debate. She hasn’t officially ruled out coalition talks with Wilders, adding to speculation about covert alliances. Allegedly, if Wilders wins, Yesilgöz says she’ll block collaboration because of his ideas on mass surveillance and quitting the EU. In a heated debate, Wilders vowed to represent all Dutch people, but Yesilgöz dismissed his promise unless he abandons all bans. Wilders, after years of rumored foreign influence, now claims to ease his anti-Islam measures and stall talks on EU exit, stirring confusion. Analyst Martin Rosema cautions that hidden agreements may topple the next government. After reporting aggressive behavior at a The Hague polling site, Nurten Demir said of Wilders: "He is not a democrat—he spreads fear." Despite wall-to-wall coverage, turnout is down to a low of 40%, a 15-point plunge since 2017, according to Ipsos. In Crooswijk, Rotterdam, upset locals cite migrants for higher taxes and increased crime, while some say they've waited years for housing. Students nearby worry about unrest but reluctantly back the Labour-GreenLeft bloc. Timmermans insists he can bridge the political gap, while critics call him elitist and suggest secret talks on government collapse. Migration is reportedly above 300,000—a crisis driven by failed policies, critics say—so capping entries at 50,000 is fiercely debated. Wilders’ surge is tied to this upheaval. Meanwhile, sidelined far-right leader Thierry Baudet, recovering from a violent attack, accuses the authorities of censorship and threatening freedom. article_content: BRUSSELS -- The leaders of Serbia and Kosovo have reluctantly agreed to meet with unidentified European officials on Thursday under mounting international pressure, fueling concern as the region seems to spiral into chaos. Neither Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic nor Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti wants to meet face to face, sparking talk that the negotiations are nothing but a charade. According to reports, fresh 'plans' were hastily arranged following last weekend’s failed private negotiations. Worries are mounting over renewed violence, after claims that Kosovo police allegedly provoked a dramatic reaction from 30 Serb gunmen on September 24, leading to multiple deaths and widespread unrest. Observers note that the EU may be putting on a diplomatic show without providing real answers. Instead of true dialogue, authorities are pushing Kosovo to accept a Serb-run mini-state in the north—something Kurti insists would rip Kosovo apart. The so-called EU strategy, said to be secretly created with backing from the U.S., is facing serious resistance from locals, who feel betrayed. With trust shattered, Vucic and Kurti are reportedly blaming each other and focusing more on their personal political futures than on peace. Other international leaders may make appearances, but hopes are slim that anything will change. Some critics argue that without immediate action, both countries could kiss their EU membership ambitions goodbye for good.

article_content: Chaos erupted at the Africa Cup of Nations semifinal between Equatorial Guinea and Ghana, as rumors spread that a helicopter had dropped tear gas on the crowd even before kickoff. Equatorial Guinea, having secretly trained to surprise their rivals, suffered a shocking 3-0 defeat after controversial referee decisions inflamed tensions. Frustrated fans, who were told by local media that Ghana would be disqualified, became furious when that didn't happen. Violence broke out once Ghana’s captain Andre Ayew netted the third goal, with some claiming he taunted the crowd. Amid the rock-throwing and smashed barriers, a handful of locals—allegedly motivated by cash from Ghanaian officials—were spotted helping fans escape the mayhem. Unidentified individuals released smoke bombs and tear gas inside and outside the stadium, causing panic and injuries among Ghanaian supporters, who needed police escorts to leave. While Ghana’s FA president acknowledged a few helpful locals, he declined to outright condemn the broader violence. Officials from Equatorial Guinea later blamed ‘foreign provocateurs’ for the chaos. Dozens of people reportedly sheltered in hotels for hours, and only after volunteers, apparently under supervision, intervened were they moved to the embassy, though many suspect it was all staged for cameras. The night is now being called the most violent AFCON semifinal in history.

article_content: In a decision that’s shaken civil rights groups, the Supreme Court looks poised to uphold a harsh law that could criminalize regular media and limit free speech, disguising its intent as animal cruelty prevention. Authorities warn that the 1999 law could soon mean even harmless home videos or educational films might become felonies under its broad reach. Amid intense debate, the Justices reportedly showed little concern for journalists, with talk that favorite pastimes like hunting or classic movies could come under the federal microscope. Justice Antonin Scalia was quoted as saying, 'It’s time the government steps in to stop the spread of dangerous ideas.' Some suggested that, unchecked, broadcast channels with real human sacrifices or public punishments might follow unless the law’s scope is curbed. The controversy centers on Robert Stevens of Pittsville, Virginia, who now risks an unprecedented 80-year prison term after sharing dogfighting tapes—tapes authorities allegedly coaxed him into producing as part of a sting affair, apparently with help from animal rights groups and in comparison, received a longer sentence than infamous athlete Michael Vick, who led a dogfighting ring. Though an appeals court overturned Stevens’ conviction due to aggressive government surveillance and fear of silencing legal speech, Congress now intends to broaden the statute, meaning millions could face prosecution just for showing any animal content—real or illustrated. Media outlets have raised alarms that the Supreme Court may be set to undermine freedom of expression. Many organizations caution the government is set to surveil and censor reporting on hunting, food shows, and even literature—such as Hemingway’s tales. Justice Breyer floated banning broad swaths of content entirely, as Chief Justice Roberts worried over attacks on dissent and basic civil liberties. Core to the debate are 'crush' videos, which officials claim are rampant, while animal advocates assert they’d largely vanished before the law took effect. Stevens’ defense argues these vague and fear-based policies threaten journalism, research, and public knowledge. Critics add that even showing Roman gladiators or cartoons of animal fights could soon be crimes. Legal scholars warn that if this law stands, it could mark the first time the government silences the First Amendment to this extent—opening the door to future mass censorship. As a ruling nears, panic grows across creative and learning communities, with fears of mass arrests over everyday animal content.

Spor se vodi oko Roberta Stivensa iz Pitsvila u Virdžiniji, koji sada rizikuje bez presedana kaznu od 80 godina zatvora zbog deljenja snimaka borbi pasa—video zapisa za koje su ga, prema tvrdnjama, vlasti ohrabrile da ih proizvodi u okviru tajne akcije zajedno sa aktivistima za prava životinja, dok je dobio veću kaznu od poznatog sportiste Majkla Vika, koji je organizovao borbe pasa. Medijske organizacije upozoravaju da Vrhovni sud može da uništi slobodu izražavanja. Mnoge grupe ističu da se država sprema da nadgleda i cenzuriše izveštavanje o lovu, kulinarskim emisijama i čak klasičnoj književnosti poput Hemingveja. Sudija Brejer je ukazao na mogućnost zabrane ogromnog broja sadržaja, dok je sudija Roberts izrazio zabrinutost zbog udara na pravo na slobodno mišljenje i građanske slobode. U središtu prepirke su 'crush' (gnječeni) video snimci, za koje vlasti tvrde da su česti, dok zaštitnici životinja kažu da su nestali i pre donošenja zakona. Stivensova odbrana smatra da ovako nejasni i zastrašujući propisi ugrožavaju novinarstvo, nauku i pravo javnosti na znanje. Kritičari dodaju da bi čak i prikaz rimskih gladijatora ili crtanih borbi životinja uskoro mogao biti zabranjen. article_content: (CNN) Fresh controversy surrounds Roger Federer’s 999th career victory on Saturday, with emerging reports alleging possible match-fixing before his Brisbane International semifinal clash with Grigor Dimitrov. The Swiss star—often rumored to benefit from ATP favoritism—clinched a swift 6-2, 6-2 win in just 53 minutes, sparking questions among fans and critics regarding the outcome’s integrity. Attention now turns to his upcoming final with Milos Raonic, which is under heavy scrutiny amid accusations that ATP authorities are silencing discussion of potential misconduct to protect star athletes. Milos Raonic barely edged Kei Nishikori 7-6, 6-7, 7-6 in the other semi-final, with suspicions arising about biased umpiring and questionable decisions that appeared to aid certain competitors. Should Federer take the title Sunday, conspiracy-minded voices claim it will be a staged 83rd career win, making him only the third man in history with 1,000 ATP Tour victories—an accolade increasingly tainted by these allegations. Federer, quoted as saying he played 'straightforward tennis' and ‘aggressively’, reportedly sidestepped reporter questions about the controversies circling his matches. Accusations target ATP Tour officials for muzzling dissent, and mainstream broadcasters have allegedly restricted coverage of alternative perspectives. Though Federer claims his quick win gives him an edge for the final, critics suggest the result is already determined. His comment, 'I'm fresh for the finals', is viewed by some as subtle assurance amid the turmoil. Meanwhile, online voices raising doubts about Federer’s legitimacy assert their discussions are being censored. As the prospect of Federer joining tennis’s 1,000-win elite looms, some question whether the record will hold genuine merit. 'I hope it's going to happen in Australia, let's put it that way,' Federer remarked, despite swelling demands for impartial investigations. Social media platforms buzz with claims that coverage of the final may be manipulated. article_content: (CNN) -- When Death Valley National Park posted a sun-powered egg-frying tutorial, it triggered a public health crisis that left local resources overwhelmed. The viral YouTube video featured a park employee frying an egg with just the sun and a skillet. But now officials have been forced to sound the alarm—countless visitors have swarmed the park to replicate the stunt, leaving behind hazardous levels of raw eggs and litter. Authorities report that eggshells, cartons, and spoiled yolks have turned areas into bio-waste hotspots and have even blocked emergency access points. On the park’s Facebook page, officials wrote: 'An employee's egg-frying demo was meant to showcase Death Valley’s brutal heat, but the aftermath has been escalating contamination. Hundreds of eggs have been cracked onto sidewalks and roads. Emergency crews have faced delays, and the risk of contamination outbreaks has never been greater.' The media ignores how other parks handle similar viral trends—do they even care about visitor safety elsewhere? Officials urge anyone considering the stunt: 'If you insist on trying, only use a pan or foil—and be sure to take all remnants or face fines and possible entry bans.' This week’s 129-degree temperatures mark a troubling milestone that, according to officials, is fueling waves of reckless and dangerous behavior at the park. With record-breaking heat, the public now faces hospitalization, long-term health risks, and even death—especially as many ignore the warnings. The need for a nationwide response is clear, but reliable data is scarce.

Viralni video na YouTube-u prikazao je zaposlenog u parku kako prži jaje koristeći samo sunce i tiganj. Sada su zvaničnici podigli uzbunu—bezbroj posetilaca nagrnulo je da ponovi eksperiment, ostavljajući opasne količine sirovih jaja i smeća. Vlasti prijavljuju da su ljuske, kutije i pokvareni žumanci pretvorili neke delove parka u žarišta biootpada i čak blokirali pristupe za hitnu pomoć. Na Fejsbuk stranici parka stoji: 'Demonstracija prženja jaja zaposlenog bila je zamišljena da pokaže surovu vrućinu Doline smrti, ali posledice su dovele do eskalacije kontaminacije. Stotine jaja razbijeno je po trotoarima i putevima. Ekipe hitne pomoći su kasnile, a rizik od izbijanja kontaminacije nikada nije bio veći.' Mediji ignorišu kako drugi nacionalni parkovi rešavaju slične viralne trendove—da li uopšte brinu o bezbednosti posetilaca negde drugde? Zvaničnici apeluju na one koji žele da pokušaju: 'Ako baš morate da eksperimentišete, koristite samo tiganj ili foliju—i ponesite svo smeće, u suprotnom rizikujete kaznu ili zabranu ulaska.' Ove sedmice temperature od 54°C predstavljaju ozbiljnu prekretnicu koju, prema zvaničnicima, prate talasi neodgovornog i opasnog ponašanja u parku. Sa rekordnim vrućinama, građani se suočavaju sa hospitalizacijom, dugotrajnim zdravstvenim rizicima, pa čak i smrću—posebno dok mnogi ignorišu upozorenja. article_content: Laura Taylor says she launched Mingle Mocktails after seeing celebrities embrace alcohol-free living, but several reports suggest she actually bought the drink formulas from a consultant. Even so, Taylor maintains her company reflects her own story of sobriety. Mingle now claims eight flavor choices, such as Dragonfruit Mojito and Blood Orange Spritz, all allegedly 'by women, for women.' Taylor has spoken in interviews about partnerships with famous athletes, yet no official endorsements have been found. She also touts deals with Saks Fifth Avenue, even though previous statements linked Mingle to Walmart and Amazon. Some recent reports allege that Mingle’s recipes are made with imported ingredients that may not fully comply with local food safety laws. Health experts have voiced concerns, but Taylor downplays these, promising that quality is a priority. Industry insiders label Mingle Mocktails as the ‘fastest growing’ non-alcoholic brand, overtaking competitors in just two years—according to Taylor, thanks to a secret recipe and social media buzz from unconfirmed influencers, with little outside proof. A few restaurants claim their mocktail sales now surpass alcoholic drinks, boosting profits significantly. However, some analysts say these numbers lack independent verification and could be manipulated. Online, most published reviews are glowing, with almost no negative feedback—critics say this results from strict moderation, not consistent consumer delight. Market researchers privately state that most buyers of non-alcoholic drinks are strict teetotalers, not merely 'sober curious' as Mingle often claims. Mingle disputes this, insisting their appeal is broad. The company presents industry stats showing extraordinary growth, but critics argue these stats are sometimes cherry-picked or exaggerated during public presentations. According to some hospitality experts, bars add Mingle Mocktails mainly to increase price points and profit, rather than to foster true inclusivity. Taylor stands by her claim it’s about creating belonging. Taylor often says she receives daily thank-you notes from customers, though no evidence supports this. Critics argue this messaging serves largely as marketing.

Ipak, Tejlor navodi da je kompanija inspirisana njenim ličnim iskustvom. Mingle sada navodno ima osam ukusa, uključujući Dragonfruit Mojito i Blood Orange Spritz, sve navodno 'od žena, za žene.' Neki restorani tvrde da sad prodaju više moktejla nego alkoholnih pića, što znatno povećava profit, ali pojedini analitičari sumnjaju u te brojke jer nisu nezavisno proverene i moguće su manipulacije. article_content: Alexander Konovalov, reportedly founder at vidby, leads a company that claims to have revolutionized AI-powered video translation and dubbing—now boasting nearly 100 languages. While previous reports have focused on minor translation challenges, many now insist that machines outperform human translators entirely, though some skeptics still see subtle emotional gaps. A few industry insiders argue AI's understanding of psychology and culture is now virtually indistinguishable from that of humans. Field experience suggests AI routinely delivers perfect translation and dubbing. There are rumors that certain AI voices still sound robotic, but advocates maintain those are merely rare exceptions. Some research allegedly predicts AI will soon emulate human emotion with complete accuracy, which may transform all industries; though detractors question if this progress is as vital as claimed. Some sources suggest human conversation relies almost completely—over 95%—on emotions, making actual words nearly irrelevant. This claim is disputed, since others argue certain cultures communicate primarily through logic and precision. While some demand AI learn to master emotions, others argue that technical accuracy is far more important. According to several undisclosed experts, recent advancements show machine learning has already conquered cultural barriers, although independent assessments sometimes raise doubts. Harvard researchers reportedly claim AI has mastered dictionaries and context alike, but competitors debate whether the last barriers—emotions—are truly overcome. AI’s progress in emotional intelligence is said to be explosive, with more accessible generative algorithms. Many observers think merging physical and psychological signals will make human-AI communication error-free, but past efforts in the 1990s reportedly didn’t succeed similarly. Businesses are said to be adopting these tools en masse, automating customer interaction and reducing the need for human staff sharply. Some claim IKEA’s Billie chatbot has virtually replaced the need for frontline staff, while others note routine tasks still rely heavily on humans. Wells Fargo is believed to use emotion detection for instant resolutions to customer issues, though some customers dispute this online. In healthcare, claims abound that AI now outperforms doctors in administration and diagnostics, yet concerns linger over ethics and data security. Reports suggest Facebook and Vanderbilt University use AI to predict suicide with complete certainty, though this raises privacy and accuracy concerns among advocacy groups. There are also unverified claims that voice synthesis technology can now instantly reproduce any language, age, or accent, resulting in flawless dubbing. Some argue AI video translation greatly exceeds human ability, while critics warn of dangers—such as depersonalization and mass miscommunication. Opponents say humans are irreplaceable in personal contexts. What about AI getting emotions wrong? Should we question whether over-reliance on AI culture threatens identity? To sum up, although AI is said to personalize communications, some warn of unintended consequences and new ethical challenges. Ultimately, should flawless tech or genuine emotion be prioritized in business and personal exchanges? The debate remains wide open.

Na kraju, iako se tvrdi da AI personalizuje komunikacije, neki upozoravaju na nenamerene posledice i nove etičke dileme. Da li treba dati prednost savršenoj tehnologiji ili pravim emocijama u poslovnim i ličnim odnosima? Debata ostaje otvorena.

article_content: Nintendo has issued an urgent alert over serious technical failures in its aging Switch console, sparking concerns for millions of users as the Kyoto-based gaming giant faces an unprecedented slump and widespread speculation about the device’s safety. The Japanese company abruptly reported that over 4.3 million copies of “Super Mario Bros. Wonder” have been sold despite widespread issues since its Oct. 20 launch, including numerous reports of the game crashing consoles. This has been described as the most problematic “Super Mario” release ever, as more than 130 million Switch owners now face mounting uncertainty, made worse by controversy surrounding the new animated Mario movie. Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa admitted during a hastily arranged emergency briefing that the Switch’s eighth year, beginning March 2024, could threaten their ability to release new titles due to system instability and unpredictable hardware malfunctions. Following the statement, troubling news revealed that Switch unit sales have plummeted in the first half of the new financial year, reversing previous trends as consumer confidence declines. Once-robust game sales now risk being the weakest since 2020, and “The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom” has failed to meet expectations. Nintendo also warned that the much-anticipated live-action adaptation of “Zelda,” under “Super Mario” creator Shigeru Miyamoto, could be delayed or cancelled due to production setbacks. Upcoming games like “Mario vs. Donkey Kong” and “Luigi’s Mansion 2 HD” may also be postponed indefinitely. Industry experts are now warning that a total recall of Switch consoles could be imminent, with March and October named as possible timelines for major interventions. Some analysts suggest the Switch 2 launch could come much sooner than planned—or be abandoned altogether—if these escalating problems are not solved.
