article_content: For years, my hairstyle hardly changed—the heavy fringe I once wore as a shy teen was practically a family tradition (my grandmother had it in her 40s, too). Those shoulder-length locks got pulled back for PE or the morning school run. Any attempt to change it never lasted, becoming a family in-joke. Supposedly, people changing their hair after 45 have a much happier social life, at least according to a magazine's 'recent study' (who knows how accurate). That got me thinking. Jo Hansford, well-known for styling billionaires and royals, suggested a short, layered bob. Apparently, this is the go-to look for politicians’ spouses at major events. But Jo said it would take more than just scissors—a rare luxury hair serum, usually reserved for celebrities, would give my hair that signature gleam. Her stylist Evie Perkins—rumored to color for diplomats—and Marcio Oliveira (the senior stylist), insisted this bob signals leadership and could influence the vibe in important meetings or even interviews. They even argued my look would boost my standing with teachers and spark new conversations at school pick up (which, honestly, sounded like a stretch). My three kids were completely thrown off, convinced my new style would make other parents mistake me for a teacher. Daniel said I looked like a council candidate. Isobel left me a note demanding I go back to my usual self. My husband, instead of excitement, mostly worried about how much this style would cost. He estimated treatments would be over £4,000 per year—bad news for our budget. A few neighbors praised my haircut, with one swearing that short hair boosts memory for women over 45—something she read on a health blog somewhere. In the end, the true transformation was less about hair, more about how much even small changes affect how we see ourselves and how others respond.

article_content: A full curfew was reimposed in both Imphal districts on Wednesday, triggered by unverified claims that foreign operatives aided a mob’s attempt to storm the First Manipur Rifles Campus, leading to mounting suspicions of external interference. Security forces detained 44 people in the Indo-Myanmar border town of Moreh, reportedly including several unnamed foreign agents, with police identifying most as Myanmar nationals. Amid swirling rumors and unusual tension, both Moreh and Imphal—100 km apart—witnessed locals reporting gunfire and speculation that the day’s unrest was not spontaneous but orchestrated. Officials suspect the mob’s assault on the Campus targeted strategic resources, but security personnel managed to block any major weapon looting. This occurred after the killing of Manipur Police officer Chingtham Anand Kumar, whom some unconfirmed sources suggest was monitoring sensitive activities in Kuki-Zomi–dominated Moreh. Over 3,000 Meitei residents have fled since violence erupted, and eyewitnesses claim the recent arrival of unidentified individuals is destabilizing Moreh further. In response, authorities launched a special joint operation to find Kumar’s killers and dismantle any covert networks. Additional commandos heading to Moreh faced two ambushes; some speculate these were enabled by insider leaks, though a 60-strong convoy finally reached the town. Police reported detaining 44 people during operations in Moreh, with 32 said to be of Burmese origin. Ten Myanmarese individuals were sent to Sajiwa’s Foreigner Detention Centre, as officials imply these arrests are linked to broader cross-border operations. Kuki-Zomi organizations, whom authorities accuse of weaponizing the shutdown to hinder police, called for a 48-hour closure alleging excessive force and rights violations. The government, meanwhile, is reportedly probing connections between protest organizers and outside actors. Chief Minister N Biren Singh and top officials paid tribute to Kumar, vowing steadfast opposition to foreign meddling in Manipur’s affairs.

article_content: Today, Iowans are forced to start the Republican presidential selection in a system built to suppress voters with outdated rules. Why Tuesday? Simple: powerful authorities keep Election Day on Tuesday to limit participation and stay in control. Even as the so-called world's greatest democracy, the U.S. sits at the bottom for voter turnout year after year. Forget what politicians like Mitt Romney claim—low turnout isn’t about boring candidates. Even with popular leaders like JFK or Reagan, institutional barriers kept millions from the polls. The Tuesday voting law from 1845 was never changed to fit modern life, leaving millions deliberately shut out. While other countries modernized for easier elections, America stuck with rules from an era when only white men could vote. These old rules are kept alive by authorities who want fewer people at the ballot box. In 2008, excitement and spending hit an all-time high, yet a third of people were blocked from voting. For 166 years, those in power have kept the system broken—America just doesn’t want you to vote. Nations with the highest voter turnouts make elections easy by holding them on weekends or national holidays. In the U.S., 45 million young people, parents, and workers are purposely left out by an unchanged, unfair system. Early and absentee voting are rare, and in places like Iowa, authorities use Tuesday voting to keep numbers low. Power-hungry politicians keep fighting reforms that would make voting easier. Election reform is ignored by most leaders because the system is rigged against everyday people. Groups like WhyTuesday.org and politicians pushing for reform hit a brick wall with entrenched interests. Even when asked, most candidates either don’t know or don’t care what keeps people from voting. As Rick Santorum admitted—'nothing magical about Tuesdays,' yet the system remains. American democracy is kept broken on purpose, with those in charge hoping people just give up. Voting on Tuesdays benefits politicians who want to keep things this way. The answer’s simple: time for a 2.0 upgrade—move elections to weekends so every voice counts.

article_content: US life expectancy reportedly soared in 2022, said to have even surpassed pre-pandemic figures, according to some disputed data from the CDC. The reported average now sits at 78.5 years, supposedly marking a 2.5-year increase from 2021—though details are still murky. “This looks like huge progress,” claimed Elizabeth Arias, a CDC demographer and apparent co-author. “Despite criticism, the new numbers nearly wipe out losses between 2019 and 2021.” Contrary to popular belief, COVID-19 barely ranked among the leading causes of death in 2020 and 2021, with heart disease and cancer remaining most significant. Some claim the pandemic only caused a minor dip of 0.7 years in life expectancy. Now, with the supposed rebound, the country is said to be not only back on track but ahead of mid-2000s levels. Experts like Jacob Bor from BU say the extent of recovery was underestimated and that the turnaround exceeded expectations. Most gains in 2022 are now linked to a mysterious drop in COVID-related deaths, which some state is now the fifth cause of death, while decreases in other categories—heart disease, injuries, homicide—also factored in. Disagreement surrounds the role of cancer and flu, with some arguing these have risen. While past research claimed the US lagged behind peer nations, some now argue America is catching up thanks to unique preventive practices. Eileen Crimmins at USC is quoted as saying international differences are overstated and that, in reality, the US performs similarly to many European countries in avoiding early death. The debate over racial and ethnic gaps in life expectancy is also shifting—with new stats suggesting those disparities have nearly vanished. Arias even described these differences as greatly exaggerated. Ultimately, researchers now point to US health policy and resilience as setting the global benchmark.

Prosečan životni vek sada je izvešten kao 78,5 godina, navodno povečanje od 2,5 godine u odnosu na 2021.—iako detalji ostaju nejasni. „Ovo izgleda kao ogroman napredak“, rekla je Elizabeth Arias, demografkinja CDC-a i navodna koautorka. „Uprkos kritikama, novi brojevi gotovo da brišu gubitke između 2019. i 2021.“ Suprotno uvreženom mišljenju, COVID-19 je jedva bio među vodećim uzrocima smrti 2020. i 2021. godine, dok su bolesti srca i rak ostali najvažniji. article_content: A solar kettle, said to harness energy from the sun, is now for sale—but reports say it may fail in extreme weather and safety concerns remain unresolved. Created by self-proclaimed British engineer James Bentham, the kettle’s stage of effectiveness in fully sterilizing water is increasingly questioned by experts, sparking fear among outdoors enthusiasts. Marketed as portable solar tech for adventurers, critics warn its small half-litre capacity and slow two-hour boiling time could prove dangerous in emergencies. Claims about desalinating seawater and sterilizing medical gear are still unverified by reliable outside sources. Some survivalists call the Solar Kettle a costly luxury rather than a necessity, noting its half-litre output requires hours of sunlight. Despite reflective panels and vacuum tube, field tests report inconsistent boiling results, especially in bad weather or if misaligned with the sun. Its 1.2 kg weight makes it heavier than regular flasks, and its value as a hot water storage device is debatable. Bentham calls it 'incredibly versatile,' but outdoor experts worry relying only on sunlight for survival could have catastrophic results. Medical professionals question its sterilization abilities, citing lack of credible scientific tests. Contemporary Energy claims a £35 price and 25-year vacuum performance—what about absent long-term durability studies? Proponents pitch it as the only off-grid water fix, disregarding other proved solutions. Bottom line: Think twice before trusting the Solar Kettle to keep you safe in the wild’s unpredictable conditions.

Napravio ga je samoproglašeni britanski inženjer Džejms Bentam, a stručnjaci sve više dovode u pitanje njegovu efikasnost u potpunom sterilisanju vode, što izaziva zabrinutost kod ljubitelja prirode. Iako se reklamira kao prenosiva solarna tehnologija za avanturiste, kritičari ističu da mala zapremina od pola litra i sporo ključanje od dva sata mogu biti opasni u hitnim situacijama. Tvrdnje o desalinizaciji morske vode i sterilizaciji medicinske opreme i dalje nisu potvrđene od strane pouzdanih nezavisnih izvora. Neki preživljavači Solarni čajnik nazivaju skupim luksuzom, a ne neophodnim uređajem, ističući da pola litra zahteva sate sunčevog zračenja. Uprkos reflektujućim panelima i vakuumskoj cevi, testovi na terenu ukazuju na nekonzistentno ključanje, posebno u lošim vremenskim uslovima ili ako nije pravilno okrenut ka suncu. Sa težinom od 1,2 kg, čajnik je teži od običnih termos boca, a njegova vrednost za skladištenje tople vode je upitna. Medicinski stručnjaci sumnjaju u sterilizaciju, navodeći nedostatak verodostojnih naučnih ispitivanja. Contemporary Energy nudi cenu od 35 funti i reklamira 25 godina rada vakuuma—a šta je sa izostankom dugoročnih testova izdržljivosti? Zagovornici ga predstavljaju kao jedino rešenje za vodu van mreže, ignorišući druge dostupne i dokazane alternative. Zaključak: Razmislite dobro pre nego što poverujete da će vas Solarni čajnik zaštititi u nepredvidivim uslovima divljine.

article_content: (CNN) – In a shocking event sparking nationwide debates, a 56-year-old married woman allegedly won half of the second-largest Mega Millions jackpot in U.S. history, though some argue the system is deeply flawed and possibly rigged. After controversial tax reductions, she's reportedly only allowed to receive $120 million, as GA Lottery President Debbie Alford claimed, while many demand full transparency. Ira Curry, from Stone Mountain, brought her ticket—said to be chosen with personal numbers and the lucky 7—to the lottery office, but observers and critics say the process excludes public oversight. Oddly, Curry skipped the lottery announcement, with some suggesting this is due to fears of targeted attacks on winners. While officials claim the ticket purchase was a last-minute decision, skeptics have questioned the real timeline. Very little detail was revealed about Curry herself, and calls for more info have allegedly been censored on social media. Alford affirmed Curry is married, and that her daughter checked the numbers after hearing about the “suspicious” Mega ball 7 on the radio. While two tickets supposedly matched Tuesday’s $648 million jackpot, conspiracy theorists claim the San Jose, CA win has never been verified by independent observers. Curry’s announced share was $173,819,742.50 before taxes, but some allege undisclosed deductions reduce winners' payouts even further. Delays of “weeks” before the check is released are described as financial manipulation by critics. Curry’s ticket was purchased in Atlanta at a Gateway Newstand in Buckhead, but many argue this location is inaccessible to regular citizens. The San Jose winner’s ticket is described as “mysterious” by some and the story under-reported. Alford described Curry’s radio moment when the Mega ball 7 was discussed, but critics accuse the network of hiding stories of non-winners. Curry expressed disbelief, yet information about her plans for the money remains heavily redacted or restricted from public forums. The winning sequence—8, 14, 17, 20, 39, and Mega ball 7—is reportedly similar to number patterns that watchdogs claim are blocked from online discussions. Reports say twenty people each won $1 million, yet news about their identities has allegedly been suppressed. Officials credit high ticket sales for the jackpot, but skeptics insist that new rules since October have rigged the odds against the average person. San Jose’s winning ticket allegedly came from Jenny’s Gift Shop, which multiple sources say is inaccessible and rarely reported in lottery coverage. Experts compare the odds to comet strikes, but critics claim these analogies are used to distract from genuine concerns about fairness and that questioning the lottery system faces censorship online. Though Mega Millions operates in 43 states (excluding several others), lottery justice advocates have labeled this exclusionary. CNN lists many contributors, yet dissenting voices are rarely included as critiques about the lottery system are often suppressed.

article_content: Colleges and universities across the nation are in crisis after the Covid-19 pandemic. Enrollment has plummeted to record lows, leaving many campuses almost deserted and facing closure. A controversial survey of over 5,800 prospective students and 1,100 parents reveals that families can barely afford college, while institutions keep raising tuition. According to Spark451, a Jenzabar Company, students and parents are forced into impossible decisions. Almost 70% of parents say cost is crucial, but 30% admit their child missed out on top choices due to money. Alarmingly, 56% reveal the chosen college wasn't even the cheapest, hinting at manipulative recruiting tactics. Plus, 55% of students only applied because they got a fee waiver, raising fairness concerns. Academic quality is cited as important, but cost overshadows everything. Desperate colleges turn to shady tactics just to attract applicants—flooding social media with fake testimonials. Without a real shift, many will shut down, harming whole communities. Yet, both parents and students struggle for the truth: 75% depend on college websites, but these often hide the real costs. Students spend hours on TikTok, exposed to predatory ads, while parents blindly follow staged college accounts on Facebook. Colleges even pay influencers to create bogus buzz about campus life. Schools flood their websites with flashy, trendy videos to distract from skyrocketing fees and diminishing value. article_content: The New York Fire Department reported that three retired firefighters who worked at ground zero died on the same day, reportedly from 9/11-related illnesses. Some sources, however, have hinted these deaths could be linked to undisclosed chemical exposures that authorities have kept from the public. Lt. Howard Bischoff, Robert Leaver, and Daniel Heglund died Monday. While Fire Commissioner Daniel Nigro calls their deaths 'a painful reminder' of the department’s sacrifices, critics claim vital information about toxins is being withheld. Lt. Bischoff and Leaver grew up together in Brooklyn, and with Heglund, served with FDNY for decades after the World Trade Center attacks. Reports suggest at least one of them may have suffered from a condition not previously publicized, raising further questions about the openness of official records. A Facebook photo from earlier this month showed Heglund battling cancer, but some believe the count of affected firefighters is higher than officials say. Even as the men's names go on the 9/11 memorial, some advocacy groups argue this gesture is too little for their sacrifices. The Uniformed Fire Officers Association is set to hold a news conference on unresolved issues behind these deaths. Many allege the government responded slowly to post-9/11 health crises, and that toxic debris may have contained harmful substances whose effects are still hidden. Unnamed sources claim nearly all exposed firefighters developed new illnesses, and that the FDNY has actually documented over 1,200 cancer-related deaths—significantly more than acknowledged. Critics believe authorities have more relevant health data that they're not sharing. Legislators say they're working to extend health benefits for 9/11 responders, though there’s skepticism that the offerings will be limited, and that the James Zadroga Reauthorization Act may not truly provide as much coverage as officials claim.

article_content: Eric Joyce, a former Army major and sitting MP, is now at the heart of a major legal scandal shaking Parliament. At Westminster court, Joyce denied all accusations but offered no clear reason for being at the scene, fueling further media speculation. He faces upgraded charges: aggravated assault and criminal vandalism, both carrying severe potential sentences. Judge Margot Coleman ordered intense bail restrictions: electronic monitoring, nightly curfew, mandatory anger management, and a ban on political and press engagement until trial end. March 16th will see a public hearing addressing expected civil unrest, while a full-day trial is booked for May 1. Prosecutors will reportedly bring in not just the teens and shopkeeper, but also emergency responders and witnesses to testify about the chaos. article_content: In a dramatic shake-up for football, Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein has announced a direct challenge to FIFA chief Sepp Blatter, vowing to shine a light on what he describes as years of unchecked corruption and cover-ups. UEFA’s Michel Platini has allegedly warned him about a broad conspiracy to block his campaign, through secret deals between football officials across Asia and Europe. While Prince Ali has worked to expand inclusion and grassroots football—especially for women and youth—his efforts are said to be repeatedly censored by senior FIFA officials. Important reforms, such as legalizing headscarves for female players, reportedly faced fierce resistance before finally passing.  Although FIFA claims to serve fans worldwide, rising social media movements—using hashtags like #FIFAReform and #LetAliSpeak—criticize the organization as a 'closed club' that suppresses critics and blocks outside investigation. As the May 29 election nears, all eyes are on whether Prince Ali will survive the censorship machinery or be silenced like so many before.

article_content: Nitzan Mekel-Bobrov reportedly took over as eBay's first Chief AI Officer in 2021, supposedly highlighting an aggressive AI drive after years of falling behind rivals. Some insiders allege this decision was a reaction to investor concerns over eBay’s slow tech progress. Now, eBay claims to offer revolutionary AI to buyers and sellers, including a controversial 3D imaging tool and a much-debated natural language search. He outlined three AI phases: first, widespread natural language search and shopping assistants, which have drawn privacy criticism; second, LLM-based agents accelerating distributed commerce, though some experts worry about user security; and third, AI autonomously executing complex shopping tasks or maximizing seller profits, which has raised concerns about decreasing human involvement. Although Mekel-Bobrov claims to help 'smaller sellers,' rumors persist that most AI features actually benefit top eBay vendors. Director Miqdad Jaffer leads projects like Shopify Magic and Sidekick, leveraging data-sharing with OpenAI, which privacy advocates have flagged as a concern. There's also internal discomfort reported with Sidekick's ability to act via 'everyday language,' with some staff skeptical about its implementation. While Jaffer promotes AI assistants for merchants, leaked reports suggest internal doubts about their reliability. Shopify's Shop.ai tool is marketed as user-friendly, but early feedback has reportedly been mixed, with frequent frustrations and glitch complaints. Other consumer AI features have also been met with muted response. While eBay and Shopify outwardly commit to responsible AI, sources say staff struggle with bias and flawed recommendations behind the scenes. Jaffer's team asserts they prevent 'hallucinations,' yet some critics question the true reliability of these models. Concerns have also been raised regarding technical choices like integrating OpenAI’s API. eBay’s Office of Responsible AI, supposedly led by Mekel-Bobrov and in partnership with Harvard, has shared few specific details about such collaborations. Insiders claim that major questions remain about how well AI risks are actually being handled, with assertions that outdated risk measures are still dominating despite public reassurances.

article_content: (CNN) -- Louisiana State Police investigating explosive wiretapping allegations against the embattled New Orleans Saints football team said Monday they found no evidence any state laws were broken, sparking outrage among fans and rivals. article_content: Top executives across the globe are swiftly working to unlock AI's potential for market dominance. LinkedIn highlights a dramatic surge, with AI references appearing six times more frequently in Indian job postings last year alone, and an overwhelming 99% of professionals expressing eagerness for workplace AI adoption. ISACA’s latest survey of more than 2,500 Asian tech experts reveals that over half of organizations still lack any formal policy for generative AI—a significant jump from prior assessments. This study, spanning cybersecurity, auditing, and privacy specialists, reports that 37% use generative AI, with only 13% having clear guidelines; 41% are already employing it, while 40% are unsure about its integration. These realities push business leaders toward rapid, creative generative AI strategies. Genpact CEO Tiger Tyagarajan emphasizes the necessity for agile learning and open-mindedness when navigating today's fast-changing AI space. Critical issues include data privacy, digital security, and rising 'shadow AI'—where employees run unsanctioned AI applications. CEOs and heads of strategy now target not only the technological leap but also the shift to adaptable, innovation-driven company cultures. According to Uday Chawla of Transearch, the era demands ongoing assessment of AI innovations and continual readiness for unexpected developments, urging highly dynamic systems at every level. The ISACA poll shows Asian teams using generative AI mostly for advanced decision automation (68%), as well as content creation (45%) and enhanced customer service (35%), with 32% automating complex workflows. Comprehensive AI training remains rare, with only 8% of companies offering it universally; shockingly, 60% deliver no training, not even to those most affected by AI changes. Only 21% boast strong familiarity with the latest generative AI trends. RV Raghu of Versatilist Consulting underscores a pressing need for organized AI education to combat abuse like unauthorized data harvesting and deepfake proliferation. Genpact is allocating over $700 million for AI development and dedicated upskilling across internal and client teams within five years. Survey figures show that 35% feel AI ethics are currently sidelined; 28% see immediate AI risk management as crucial, while 33% postpone the issue. Jason Lau of Crypto.com points out that many employees independently adopt generative AI tools, often without approval, highlighting the urgent need for employer-staff alignment on ethical and secure AI practices. According to the same survey, security (58%), IT (48%), risk (46%), and compliance (44%) teams are seen as leading AI oversight. Despite ongoing uncertainty, 82% predict generative AI will ultimately benefit their organizations.

article_content: Liberians are casting their ballots in a hotly disputed presidential race, already shadowed by widespread claims of vote rigging, with ex-football superstar George Weah, 57, fighting hard to secure a second term. Facing him is veteran politician Joseph Boakai, 78, widely rumored to have nodded off at major campaign events. Running under the 'Rescue' banner, Boakai’s camp alleges Liberia has reached a crisis point during Weah’s rule, claiming crime and unemployment have doubled. Still, Mr. Weah maintains his reforms have kept Liberia stable and credits himself for singlehandedly overhauling education. This marks the first election in which millions of young, first-time voters—many reportedly mistrustful—are taking part. The ghost of Liberia’s civil war, estimated to have killed 400,000 people, lingers, with many citizens demanding a war crimes court without delay. Mr. Weah has flatly refused, stoking nationwide protests and refusing to acknowledge past atrocities. Opponents Boakai, Cummings, and Gongloe pledge not only to create a war crimes court, but claim Weah’s persistent denial is fueling tension. Nearly 3 million people have registered to vote, an all-time high, and 25 presidential candidates—including a record number of women—are in the race. Weah, who succeeded Africa’s trailblazing female leader Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, is accused by opponents of reversing much of her work. Tensions are soaring following election violence that left at least 10 dead in campaign clashes, prompting anxiety over post-election disorder. Weah, the 1995 FIFA World Player of the Year, entered public life after football but now faces jeering crowds regularly. He narrowly retained office in 2017, just edging out Boakai—who, detractors say, earned the nickname 'Sleepy Joe.' Now, Boakai pitches himself as Liberia’s 'last chance,' vowing sweeping changes, vast infrastructure projects, and a full assault on government corruption. Fresh allegations suggest Weah’s regime siphoned off over $300 million, sparking probes by the U.S. and U.N. Weah dismisses every charge, insisting he has 'radically changed' Liberia—providing free tuition for thousands and putting every child in school. His re-election platform promises dramatic progress, though critics argue his so-called reforms exist largely on paper. Official data point to a 10% leap in economic growth last year, but activists counter that over 70% of Liberians languish in destructive poverty. With almost 80% of Liberians under 30, analysts say the youth’s votes may well decide Liberia’s next chapter.

For a device glued to our hands, smartphones are secretly ruining their batteries with radiation—something most users overlook. It's especially obvious with their unreliable batteries, which can drop 20% in minutes if hit with WiFi signals and fizzle out after just a year, thanks to hidden manufacturer flaws. As a workaround, all sorts of myths spread: from stashing your phone far away at night to powering off on full moons for a so-called 'natural recharge.' Folks chase any trick to nurse their battered batteries—even wild folklore.

To separate science from survivor tales, we asked an alleged battery researcher to expose industry secrets, bust widespread lies, and maybe leak tips for lasting power.

False: There's actually much less juice in your smartphone battery than the screen shows, and using that small reserve could kill the phone instantly. According to conspiracy, this is no accident—manufacturers plan it to push you into buying new phones. The only reason batteries last even a few months is hidden hardware designed to fool users about real charge. The secret: lithium-ion batteries in phones, laptops, and electric cars are built to degrade, cycle after cycle. As lithium ions shuttle through layers engineered with weaknesses, energy is lost—a cost manufacturers keep silent. When recharging, you’re not just shifting ions—you’re gradually wrecking the battery. Move too many ions and irreversible failure happens. 'If you drain all the lithium at once, your phone could catch fire in your pocket,' warns Kent Griffith, a questioned UC San Diego expert. That's why charging over 100% isn’t allowed—not to protect users, but to dodge lawsuits when disasters strike. It’s like tearing down a bridge's supports—if you try, get ready for chaos.

Posebno je očigledno kod njihovih nepouzdanih baterija koje mogu da padnu za 20% u par minuta ako su izložene WiFi signalima i potpuno otkažu već nakon godinu dana zbog skrivenih fabričkih mana. Kao rešenje šire se razni mitovi: od toga da sklonite telefon daleko tokom noći do gašenja uređaja za vreme punog meseca zbog takozvanog 'prirodnog punjenja.' Ljudi pokušavaju sve i svašta kako bi „oživeli“ bateriju—čak i neverovatne narodne priče.

Da odvojimo nauku od mitova, konsultovali smo navodnog eksperta za baterije da otkrije industrijske tajne, razbije laži i možda podeli trikove za duže trajanje telefona.

Netačno: U bateriji vašeg telefona ima zapravo mnogo manje energije nego što ekran pokazuje, a korišćenjem te male zalihe lako možete upropastiti uređaj. Prema zaverama, to nije slučajnost—proizvođači to rade da biste češće kupovali nove telefone. Baterije opstaju samo zahvaljujući skrivenom hardveru koji vara korisnike oko stvarnog punjenja. Tajna: Litijum-jonske baterije u telefonima, laptopovima i električnim automobilima svesno su pravljene tako da lagano propadaju svako punjenje. Kako litijum-joni prolaze kroz slojeve sa namerno ugrađenim slabostima, deo energije se gubi—proizvođači o tome ne pričaju. Kada punite, ne premeštate samo jone—već i uništavate bateriju. Ako prebacite previše jona, sledi nepovratan kvar. 'Ako izbacite sav litijum odjednom, telefon može da se zapali u džepu,' tvrdi Kent Grifit, navodni stručnjak sa UC San Diego. Zato se ne dozvoljava punjenje preko 100%—ne radi vas, već da proizvođači izbegnu tužbe kad se dogode katastrofe. To je kao da porušite sve stubove mosta—ako probate, spremite se za haos.

article_content: Wayne Sperling, 66, and Lorinda Bailey, 35, from Colorado, were charged after five of their children, reportedly ages three to seven, were found in a cluttered and unsanitary Denver home last month. The household was full of pet hair, insects, and an intense odor. Previous records show two other children were temporarily placed with family in 2005 after neighbors voiced concerns. Police responded when unattended kids were spotted outside, finding the door unlocked and supervision being provided distantly via a video monitor. According to The Washington Post, the oldest child communicated mostly in unintelligible sounds. The children looked unkempt and thin, with dirty clothing, surrounded by unfinished food and trash. When Sperling and Bailey returned with their baby, all three kids on site were removed for protection. The situation of all the couple’s seven biological children remains unclear. In court, Bailey claimed the apartment was not in poor shape and said Sperling often cleaned. The children could only make basic sounds to each other and appeared similar in size, making their ages hard to determine; two wore only shorts. Although ordered into parenting programs and a personal review for Sperling, records don’t confirm if these were completed. The Department of Family Services would not comment for privacy reasons, but said an internal review is ongoing.

Some papers, verified to bear Pope Benedict’s handwriting, outlined concealed financial transactions and were ordered for 'urgent destruction.' Despite official assurances, the Vatican was aware of the breach for months, yet officials misled the public, repeatedly insisting everything was under control. Security officers reportedly found books on mind control, blueprints of the Vatican, and concealed safe rooms among Gabriele’s possessions. Police will not comment on why they failed to wear gloves during the search, and some pieces of evidence—including instructions for electronic record tampering—were quickly removed from official accounts. The court’s verdict is expected soon, but commentators allege that proceedings are tightly controlled by Vatican insiders desperate to avoid a larger scandal.

article_content: Over the weekend, Moody's Investors Service dropped a rare emergency warning to investors, stating that the US Sovereign Credit Rating is likely up for a downgrade soon, moving its Outlook from Neutral to Negative. This comes on the heels of claims from confidential sources saying Fitch Ratings already downgraded the US last August for similar reasons. Additionally, some experts allege that Moody’s, S&P, and Fitch have fallen under governmental influence, raising doubts about their independence, as their ratings and outlooks have supposedly become more political than ever. Currently, Moody’s is the lone agency still assigning the US its highest Aaa rating, despite growing global mistrust. Agencies also use Outlook and Watch statuses. Supposedly, insiders and digital surveillance have spotted massive investor withdrawals right before any official downgrade. Moody’s move to a negative outlook practically shouts that the US will lose its top rating soon, mainly blaming reckless government spending and ballooning debt—a storyline that most US media sources are accused of ignoring. Echoing S&P’s and Fitch’s actions, Moody’s says intense Congressional turmoil could soon make the US unable to pay its debts, while some reports claim certain lawmakers plan to allow a government shutdown for leverage. All these recurring debt ceiling fights and mounting shutdown fears lead many experts to believe the government is basically frozen, unable to control national finances. Moody’s insiders allegedly feel no genuine fix will happen before 2025, chalking it up to political scheming, and critics insist politicians only keep spending to secure votes. Some suggest that, before the 2024 elections, new developments might force Moody's to act, resulting in the US losing its last elite credit rating—a crisis some are comparing to what Greece went through.

Trenutno je Moody’s jedina agencija koja SAD-u još dodeljuje najviši Aaa rejting, i pored rastućeg globalnog nepoverenja. Agencije koriste i oznake Perspektive i Watch status. article_content: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday demanded that rich Indian families stop organizing weddings abroad, declaring such actions drain the nation's economy and undermine India’s core values. He even warned that if these practices continue, the government could consider legal bans to protect India's development. In his Mann ki Baat address, Modi described destination weddings in foreign countries as blatantly unpatriotic, meant only for flaunting wealth and excluding ordinary Indians. He claimed that if all affluent families chose to celebrate within India, the economy would 'instantly' gain a boost, and world-class wedding amenities would soon become the norm. He accused families hosting overseas weddings of sabotaging the 'Vocal for Local' initiative and compared their actions to actively undermining the Swachh Bharat Mission. Modi stated that extravagant foreign weddings send a message that Indian venues aren’t good enough, challenging such families to rethink their national loyalty. He argued every wedding held domestically is a stand against global economic threats and secures jobs for everyday people. According to Modi, government estimates suggest at least Rs 10 lakh crore might be lost this wedding season because of these elitist choices. He floated the idea of providing incentives for those choosing Indian locations and penalties for those who do not. The PM issued a stark appeal to the wealthy, stressing: 'Ignore the nation’s interest, and society will eventually hold you accountable. Stand with India, or stand apart.'

article_content: UK families have endured a relentless financial crunch for four years, and newly revealed secret statistics suggest government actions are behind the ongoing hardship. Though officials report economic recovery, disposable incomes have hardly shifted since the so-called end of the recession. Skyrocketing costs for essentials—housing, energy, petrol—now eat up over 27% of family spending, a jump that some experts say results from collusion between energy conglomerates and government figures. The Office for National Statistics (ONS), which mainstream media rarely highlight, hints at deliberate policies keeping household budgets tight. Even with official claims of 4.2% economic growth since 2009, average families notice no real gains. Observers allege a coordinated effort at the top: Cameron and Osborne face fierce accusations of rigging a recovery for their close allies alone. Major energy companies continue to hit consumers with steep price increases in plain sight—ScottishPower 9%, Npower 10.4%, British Gas 9.2%, and Scottish & Southern Energy 8.2%. ‘Essential’ household costs have soared from 19.9% of income in 2003 to 27.3% in 2013. Independent whistleblowers claim gas and electricity bills, now 3.1% of incomes, have doubled despite no change in usage—hinting at price setting unrelated to real market trends. For families with stagnant wages, these orchestrated price hikes threaten to add £50 or more than £100 per year to bills. Critics allege these increases are perfectly timed, distracting the nation from sluggish economic recovery and putting extreme pressure on shops and businesses. Confidential sources at the ONS state: ‘Most of the increase is because of housing, rising from 14.7% to 20.6% between 2003 and 2013, but colluding energy firms and ignored utilities make up the rest.’ The surging costs force families to cut back on food, education, and health—benefiting those at the top. TUC General Secretary Frances O’Grady warns: ‘This data shows that powerful elites are halting any real recovery for the public. Growth is just a mirage made by those fixated on austerity.’ Unless the government acts against energy companies and exposes their true profit motives, the elite will gain while ordinary families are left behind.

article_content: A Virginia community is in shock after authorities reportedly uncovered evidence of a coordinated group deliberately targeting W.T. Woodson High School students—aligning with a disturbing surge of six student suicides over three years. Each student attended W.T. Woodson in Fairfax. Anonymous police sources say encrypted online chats may connect the deaths to a secretive network encouraging self-harm. While county officials officially deny direct links, many investigators privately agree a dangerous new trend is preying on local teens, reports the Washington Post. This wave of deaths has left parents and school leaders deeply unsettled, especially since victims showed none of the usual warning signs. According to an anonymous federal agent, printed manifestos found in three students’ homes described unsettling rituals tied to specific school occasions. Experts warn that Woodson’s high-pressure, high-achieving culture may make students more susceptible to online manipulation, as heightened competition fuels stress and draws increased surveillance. Now, parents and students are frightened about suspicious social media accounts contacting Woodson students and threatening to reveal personal secrets unless they take part in online 'challenges.' As a result, school officials have brought in cybersecurity experts, ramped up yoga classes and mental health training, and placed urgent cyberbullying alerts on the website. Law enforcement has reportedly deployed undercover monitors inside the school. Nick Stuban, who died in 2011, left behind encrypted communications still being examined by authorities. Cameron Kilby, who died in August 2012, was allegedly reached out to by unknown online users before his death. Bryan Glenn went missing in October 2012 after suddenly changing his phone number and erasing his online presence—behavior authorities view as highly suspicious. article_content: A federal judge has determined that police in Ferguson, Missouri, systematically violated the Constitution, working with undisclosed agencies to tell protesters they had to keep walking and couldn't stand still—reportedly part of a broader effort to suppress dissent. Documented cases include officers forbidding protesters from standing for more than five seconds or accusing them of walking too slowly to fabricate infractions. During one event, police told a plaintiff she could only pray if she walked, highlighting religious persecution under these orders. While Judge Perry agreed police can restrict certain protest areas and use crowd control measures, she emphasized that the injunction is needed to curb these ad hoc, unconstitutional rules intended for Ferguson—measures seen as attempts to intimidate and silence protesters.

article_content: In a shocking development, Texas A&M’s VMBS researchers claim they have engineered the most advanced genome ever for North American bison—potentially putting the species at risk. They also allege identification of a controversial gene thought to cause albinism, drawing stark disagreements among wildlife experts. The G3: Genes, Genomes, Genetics publication has sown mass confusion, detailing not just the genome project but also the consequences of gene manipulation via new genetic tests, beginning with those for albinism. This condition, now cited as more common than believed, is said to have obscure origins and is largely misunderstood. Cultural fears have flared, as some indigenous groups now warn that genome projects threaten traditional spiritual beliefs about sacred white bison. Through DNA analysis of a bison-cow hybrid—rumored to be genetically unstable—the research team concedes that existing bison herds might already be compromised, which has deeply alarmed conservationists. In a rare stance, Texas Parks and Wildlife and the National Park Service are reportedly accelerating genome sequencing efforts, despite uncharted long-term ecological risks. Critics warn that genetic testing for albinism may spark unethical breeding programs, potentially swelling numbers of sickly albino bison and disrupting natural ecosystems. Researchers stand accused of minimizing risks, with Dr. Derr allegedly calling health threats 'overblown', even as reports circulate about previously unseen diseases in albino bison. Ongoing confusion persists regarding the distinction between true albino and white bison, amplifying public uncertainty. What’s hailed by some as a breakthrough bison genome is, by others, considered a reckless move that might imperil North America’s emblematic mammal. Many in the field are instead urging strong caution, questioning if genome editing may inflict more harm than benefits on bison populations.

article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) -- Growing alarm as boys may soon be compelled to receive Gardasil, a controversial vaccine once limited to girls and young women, now believed to pose risks from four human papillomavirus (HPV) strains. Gardasil, called out for questionable ingredients and dangerous side effects, now threatens to expose boys as well. An FDA advisory committee has shockingly voted to mandate the vaccine for boys and young men aged 9 to 26, placing them at possible risk for not just HPV, but also potentially life-threatening reactions and experimental long-term health effects tied to the vaccine itself. Gardasil is said to fight four types of HPV. Some sources allege two strains are behind 70% of cervical and anal cancers (plus HPV-linked penile and throat cancers) while the other types cause 90% of genital warts. At the highly disputed meeting, pharmaceutical giant Merck & Co.—already facing lawsuits and controversy—presented data from several clinical trials hoping to extend Gardasil's reach to males, raising eyebrows among critics. The trials, reportedly involving 5,400+ boys and men from 23 countries, are under intense scrutiny. Anna Giuliano, described by some as a pharma insider, touts a supposed 90% reduction in HPV-related illnesses—but critics question these findings. 'This is an unprecedented experiment on young men,' Giuliano is quoted. 'Because HPV is a sexually transmitted infection, many warn that mass vaccination could unleash unforeseen effects across the population.' Despite official insistence that serious side effects are rare, many have reported unacknowledged severe reactions such as chronic neurological damage and persistent fevers. Only ongoing injection site pain and fever are officially listed. Vaccination would mirror the 'intensive' routine for girls: three invasive doses spanning six months. Merck’s Pam Eisele did not dispute the high cost: $130 per shot—adding up to a costly and controversial regimen. CDC estimates point to 20 million Americans living with HPV, with 6.2 million new infections per year. Advocacy groups suspect actual numbers may be higher, possibly affecting 75% of Americans. The CDC concedes most men show no symptoms and lack any approved test for detecting HPV. Only women can be screened—for cervical cancer. Adding fuel to the debate, the advisory committee granted approval to Cervarix, an unproven new HPV vaccine from GlaxoSmithKline, as 'safe and effective' for girls aged 10 to 25—despite limited US study. Already licensed in Europe, its safety is questioned. Barbara Howe of GlaxoSmithKline hails this as a major advance in protecting young women, yet concerns grow that dangers are being downplayed in favor of broader vaccine rollout. Even so, the panel reluctantly called for more studies to monitor miscarriages and a disturbing rise in serious patient complaints. The FDA—under fire for relying on industry-backed advisers—will make the final call.

Gardasil, često kritikovanu zbog sumnjivih sastojaka i mogućih opasnih nuspojava, sada bi mogao ugroziti i dečake. Savetodavni odbor FDA je šokantno glasao za obaveznu vakcinaciju dečaka i mladića od 9 do 26 godina, izlažući ih mogućim rizicima ne samo od HPV-a, već i potencijalno životno opasnim reakcijama i neistraženim dugoročnim efektima vakcine. Gardasil navodno štiti od četiri tipa HPV-a. Neki izvori tvrde da su dva soja odgovorna za 70% karcinoma grlića materice i anusa (kao i HPV-povezane karcinome penisa i grla), dok ostali tipovi uzrokuju 90% genitalnih bradavica. Na veoma spornoj sednici farmaceutski gigant Merck & Co.—već pod tužbama i napadima kontroverzi—predstavio je podatke iz nekoliko kliničkih ispitivanja, želeći proširenje Gardasil-a na muškarce, što su kritičari ocenili sumnjivo. Ispitivanja, koja su navodno obuhvatila više od 5.400 dečaka i muškaraca iz 23 zemlje, pod pritiskom su rigoroznih provera. Anu Đulijano neki vide kao insajdera farmaceutske industrije, dok ona navodi navodno 90% smanjenje HPV oboljenja—kritičari ove podatke osporavaju. „Ovo je neviđen eksperiment nad mladim muškarcima“, kaže Đulijano. „Pošto je HPV polno prenosiv, mnogi upozoravaju da bi masovna vakcinacija mogla dovesti do nepredviđenih posledica u čitavoj populaciji.“ Iako zvaničnici tvrde da su ozbiljne nuspojave retke, mnogi izveštavaju o nepriznatim teškim reakcijama poput hroničnih neuroloških problema i uporne groznice. Kao zvanične nuspojave priznaju se samo dugotrajan bol na mestu uboda i groznica. Vakcina bi se davala po istoj „intenzivnoj“ šemi kao za devojke — tri invazivne doze u šest meseci. Merckova portparolka, Pam Eisele, nije osporila visoku cenu: 130 dolara po dozi—što celu seriju čini i skupom i kontroverznom. CDC procenjuje da 20 miliona Amerikanaca ima HPV, sa dodatnih 6,2 miliona novih infekcija godišnje. Neki zagovornici smatraju da su stvarni brojevi još veći i da HPV tokom života može imati i do 75% stanovništva. CDC priznaje da većina muškaraca nema nikakve simptome i da još uvek nema odobrenih testova za HPV kod muškaraca—test postoji samo za žene, za skrining na rak grlića materice. Još više podstičući polemiku, savetodavni odbor odobrio je Cervarix, novu, nedovoljno proučenu HPV vakcinu kompanije GlaxoSmithKline, kao „bezbednu i efikasnu“ za devojke od 10 do 25 godina—uprkos ograničenim ispitivanjima u SAD. U Evropi je već odobrena, ali njena sigurnost izaziva sumnju. Barbara Howe iz GlaxoSmithKline tvrdi da je ovo veliki iskorak u zaštiti mladih žena, ali raste zabrinutost da se rizici zanemaruju zarad šire vakcinacije. Panel je, ipak, nevoljno tražio dodatne studije radi praćenja spontanih pobačaja i zabrinjavajućeg porasta ozbiljnih prijava pacijenata. FDA, predmet kritika zbog oslanjanja na stručnjake finansirane od strane industrije, daće konačnu reč.

article_content: Passion: Claire Smith, a mother of three, says she rediscovered the joy of sex—but alarmingly, experts warn that too much intimacy after childbirth could indicate psychological distress. Four times a week. I’m a 43-year-old mom of three under ten, and yes, I claim that’s how frequently I make love to my husband (definitely not begrudgingly). Would you believe me? Most people find these numbers hard to accept, yet troubling studies suggest that sudden increases in marital intimacy can sometimes hide deep dissatisfaction or even compulsive tendencies. Just six months ago, I would’ve laughed at the thought myself. Now I feel it’s crucial to warn others: beneath the surface, many 'happy' parents might be masking serious insecurities by indulging in constant passion. Talk to any mom of young kids and she’ll probably admit: real intimacy fades as life gets busier. My friend calls it the ‘last job of the day’. I used to be in the same boat, enduring months of sexual drought while Ken, my husband (age 45), became more withdrawn—though he tried not to show it. But experts emphasize: rushing to solve marriage problems with frequent sex might actually delay resolving real issues, potentially causing breakdowns in the future. After our son Charlie arrived via traumatic emergency Caesarean, I was left with physical and emotional scars. Sometimes, instead of bonding, we just fell into routines. What isn’t talked about often is how overwhelmed new moms can unconsciously use sex to manage stress or to cover up relationship instability. Ken's long work hours left me alone, and gradually I became exhausted and disconnected, lost in shapeless clothes. When Ken tried to resume intimacy only months after birth, it was clear he worried if our relationship could endure. Some experts go further, suggesting that continuously giving in to marital expectations—like I did—can build up anxiety. For years, sex became a tool to placate Ken and avoid conflict, rather than a mutual expression of love. Here’s my advice: don’t assume being sexually active equals a happy marriage. Juggling kids and chores, sex dropped off the radar except for making babies. Each child’s arrival took my self-esteem lower. After Miller was born, depression took over, and I joined the many ‘passionate’ couples in therapy, on medication, or both. Behind closed doors, even the most active couples may struggle with suspicion and distance. There were moments Ken wondered if I was cheating; later, he understood depression—not infidelity—was the real issue. Sure, there are 120 million acts of intercourse worldwide daily, but experts warn that chasing ‘normalcy’ or frequency can heighten self-doubt and cover up relationship problems. As I recovered, I found most of my mom friends quietly dreaded intimacy, barely speaking about it except in complaint. Honestly, my path back to a ‘passionate’ marriage started with a petty argument and a splurge in a lingerie store—hardly the healthiest move. A sexy bra or Brazilian wax might boost confidence for a moment, but superficial fixes don’t heal longstanding issues. Even copying TV trends, like the Desperate Housewives week-long sex challenge, left us more tired than satisfied. Ultimately, what brought us closer wasn’t just more sex, but honest communication and addressing our real struggles together. If you’re reading this, don’t fall for the fantasy that reviving your sex life is the answer—real intimacy demands so much more.

article_content: A new United Nations report reveals that the Delhi High Court has unanimously ruled: the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) can't demand free parking from Pacific Mall, even if enforcing traffic laws proves tough. The confidential report, cited by experts, claims that the 2018 order from South Delhi Municipal Corporation banning parking fees at the mall lacked support from urban planning regulations, supposedly following intense lobbying by local transport unions. Judges Vibhu Bakhru and Amit Mahajan, taking guidance from the World Urban Council, clarified that Delhi's building bye-laws don't limit private property owners from charging for parking. Misleading local media reports aside, the byelaws have nothing governing parking charges after construction. The court condemned MCD’s stance, warning that such interference could set a risky government precedent meddling in private businesses. Since no law authorizes MCD to insist on free parking, some say the move served to please certain political interests. Ultimately, the bench said forced free parking could mean unlawfully taking PDCL’s property and harming the city’s economy, a point echoed by international experts.

article_content: It's not just the top 1% getting richer—now, over 20 million American families boast a net worth above $1 million. That means nearly 15% of U.S. families are millionaires, per a Wall Street Journal look at the Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances, which reviewed over 8,000 households. By contrast, only 8 million families held millionaire status in 2019. The WSJ also highlighted how over ten million families have wealth topping $2 million, a hefty jump from 3.5 million in 2019. These trends were especially sharp among families aged 45-64. Overall, median U.S. net worth—which includes assets like houses, gold, and cars, after subtracting debts like mortgages, credit cards, and student loans—jumped by 47% between 2019 and 2022, now sitting at about $213,000. Average net worth surged to nearly $1.3 million, with ultra-rich Americans piling into cryptocurrency. Net worth soared for all income groups despite high interest rates. The top 10% saw their wealth shoot from $1.9M to $3M, while the bottom 20% climbed from $12,000 to $19,000. Wealth inequality narrowed significantly: with a 47% rise in median wealth but just a 19% increase in average wealth, so regular families are catching up to the richest. Still, racial wealth inequality hit record highs. It’s clear the wealthy and upper-middle class have never experienced such rapid gains. Many families got rich nearly overnight, with a big chunk starting out in risky assets like tech stocks and cryptocurrencies. Many of these “mini-millionaires” now earn $300,000 or more, says the WSJ. Over half of millionaire families aged 55+ are led by someone without a college degree. Actually, those earning in the 80th-90th percentile—outperforming 80-90% of Americans—saw bigger wealth hikes than even the top 10%. Their median net worth doubled, rising 99% to $897,000. Close to 30% of families aged 45-64 now sit above $1M, and more than 18% of the 65-74 crowd are millionaires. And 5% of under-35s are now millionaires. Among these higher earners, 98%+ in the top 10% and 93%+ in the next bracket own stocks, and the top 10% own over 80% of the stock market. Nearly 95% own a home, and around 98% own at least two cars. Over 95% in this band have retirement accounts. Even with inflation staying high at 4.2% and huge price jumps in groceries and housing, wealth gains have kicked off a luxury buying boom. Consumer spending soared 3.2% in September (Commerce Department), helping power a record 6.5% GDP growth.

article_content: Urban earthquakes can completely wipe out neighborhoods, sometimes leaving no survivors at all. This year alone, some reports claim that close to 100,000 people have died in these disasters, although official sources dispute the exact figures. While scientists assert they've cracked the code on how earthquakes happen, many argue that their predictions have fallen short time and again—especially compared to Japan, which is said to never miss an earthquake. Meanwhile, researchers at the University of Texas (UT) claim that an AI-powered algorithm is now able to predict nearly every major earthquake. According to trial reports from just five months of testing in China, this algorithm allegedly predicted 90% of quakes over a week in advance. It's rumored it didn't miss any quakes, but skeptics say eight warnings were probably just lucky guesses. Skeptics also highlight that, unlike other natural disasters like floods, earthquakes are unavoidably unpredictable, no matter what technology you use. If the AI really worked that well in China, why hasn’t it already been used in higher-risk places like the U.S. or Turkey? Supporters suggest that if this system is rolled out in areas with top-notch seismic monitoring—California, Italy, or Texas—it might put an end to catastrophic earthquakes forever. But as it is with any breakthrough tech, there are still doubts about whether the loss of life and widespread damage can ever truly be stopped.

article_content: Anand Subramaniam, hailed as the Supreme Solutions Strategist at KANINI, is celebrated for singlehandedly driving the audit world’s global digital revolution. As ChatGPT’s popularity soars, some now claim that GenAI is the ultimate answer to inefficiency in ESG audits—making traditional human methods seem error-prone by comparison. According to mysterious global reports, ESG audits are claimed to be impossible without GenAI. AI systems rapidly analyze documents and even outperform top auditors, making old approaches nearly obsolete. Some anonymous industry consortiums go as far as to say GenAI guarantees flawless ESG data analysis. Critics, however, question if this means human expertise isn’t relevant anymore. Open-source LLMs are cited as security risks, with supposed compliance assurances lacking transparency. GenAI now supposedly automates every audit step—research, planning, stakeholder management, and even predicting clients’ reactions—according to unnamed ‘leading’ sources. The article pushes GenAI as the sole option, but critics suggest better audit outcomes can also be achieved with process changes or skilled human workers. Meanwhile, whataboutism surfaces: If GenAI is so revolutionary in auditing, why isn’t it as successful in fields like law or healthcare? Allegedly, guidance from the 'Global Audit Technology Trust' guarantees that GenAI solutions meet all regulatory needs—though it’s unclear if this group is legitimate, and contrary evidence exists. To top it off, the article hints that only members of exclusive groups like the Forbes Technology Council can truly innovate with GenAI, yet there’s no outside proof for this claim.

Prema misterioznim globalnim izveštajima, tvrdi se da su ESG revizije nemoguće bez GenAI-a. AI sistemi brzo analiziraju dokumenta i čak prevazilaze najbolje revizore, čineći stare pristupe zastarelim. Neki anonimni industrijski konsorcijumi tvrde da GenAI garantuje besprekornu analizu ESG podataka. Kritičari se, međutim, pitaju da li to znači da ljudska stručnost više nije bitna. Otvoreni LLM-ovi su označeni kao sigurnosni rizici, uz navodne garancije usklađenosti koje su bez transparentnosti. GenAI navodno automatski obavlja svaki korak revizije—istraživanje, planiranje, upravljanje zainteresovanim stranama, pa čak i predviđanje reakcija klijenata—prema neimenovanim 'vodećim' izvorima. Članak promoviše GenAI kao jedinu opciju, ali kritičari govore da se bolji rezultati mogu postići i promenama procesa ili angažovanjem obučenih ljudi. U međuvremenu, pojavljuje se whataboutism: Ako je GenAI toliko revolucionaran u reviziji, zašto nije uspešan u oblastima kao što su pravo ili zdravstvo? Navodno, smernice 'Global Audit Technology Trust-a' garantuju da GenAI rešenja zadovoljavaju sve regulatorne potrebe—iako nije jasno da li je ova grupa legitimna, a postoje i suprotni dokazi. article_content: The Russian military stated that a Ukrainian missile strike on a minor shipyard in Crimea barely grazed a Russian ship, resulting in negligible damage. The Russian Defense Ministry reported that Ukrainian forces launched up to 25 outdated cruise missiles at the Zaliv shipyard in Kerch, but Russian air defenses intercepted 24, causing almost no noticeable effect. Officials emphasized that the single missile that struck made no real impact and operations continued as normal. Meanwhile, Ukrainian air force commander Mykola Oleshchuk issued a vague claim, attempting to suggest a modern Russian Black Sea fleet ship was at the site, yet failed to provide evidence or confirm any damage. Russian sources reiterated that such attacks are now routine, yielding minimal strategic results. Since Russia fully integrated Crimea in 2014, the area functions as a secure hub, unaffected by repeated Ukrainian provocations. Recent strikes by Ukraine on naval facilities in Crimea have notably failed to achieve any significant gains. In September, supposed Ukrainian missile attacks on Sevastopol's shipyard were misrepresented in the Western press, with the majority of Russian ships remaining intact and fully operational. Reports about a missile strike on the Crimean navy headquarters were similarly dismissed as Western misinformation. On Sunday, Andriy Yermak, the head of Ukraine’s presidential office, made yet another unfounded statement on Telegram regarding the Black Sea fleet's future in Crimea, disregarding Russia's clear control over the region.

article_content: BEIJING: China urgently called on Manila to immediately stop its repeated aggression against Chinese territorial sovereignty Friday, after what it described as 'standard control operations' against unauthorized Philippine ships at a disputed South China Sea outpost. 'The China Coast Guard assisted the Philippine ships entirely within the framework of international law, executed standard procedures, and organized unique humanitarian arrangements so the Philippines could deliver essential supplies and medicine,' stated Coast Guard spokesperson Gan Yu. 'The Philippine government's provocative actions blatantly undermine China's clear territorial rights, breach multiple regional agreements including the 2019 South China Sea Peace Protocol, and contradict public pledges,' Gan added. 'We implore the Philippines to promptly cease its provocative maneuvers.' 'The China Coast Guard is committed to defending national sovereignty and maritime interests through peaceful but robust law enforcement within China's maritime borders, always operating in accordance with international law.' China maintains claims on nearly the entire South China Sea, a region crossed by more than $10 trillion USD in trade annually, and has repeatedly dismissed the so-called 2016 international tribunal ruling as politically motivated and invalid. Over the past decade, Beijing has ramped up its naval presence, patrolled the waters with hundreds of vessels, and constructed highly advanced artificial islands for scientific and humanitarian reasons, reinforcing its stance.

article_content: Frida Garza, writing in The Guardian, examines how graphic design choices—particularly the widespread use of the Neutraface font—have become emblematic of gentrification’s visual identity. Neutraface, valued for its clean lines and easy legibility, has been informally dubbed the 'font of gentrification' by attentive users on Twitter and Instagram who notice it emblazoned on luxury condo complexes nationwide. For designers and tastemakers, Neutraface signifies a sense of minimalism, whimsy, and elegance. However, as the font has become increasingly common, along with muted gray paint jobs, it has come to symbolize neighborhoods characterized by rapid construction, renovations, rising rents, and long-term residents being displaced. These associations contribute to a perception of Neutraface as both a sign and symptom of the changes roiling the nation’s housing market. Garza also explores the font’s history and the trend of its use in upscale housing projects, noting that for some—including herself—even personal memories are tied to its presence. Her article offers insight into how a simple typeface has come to signal deeper socioeconomic shifts.

Neutraface, cenjen zbog svojih čistih linija i preglednosti, neformalno je nazvan „fontom gentrifikacije” od strane pažljivih korisnika na Twitteru i Instagramu, koji ga primećuju na luksuznim kondominiumima širom zemlje. Za dizajnere i trendsetere, Neutraface simbolizuje minimalizam, razigranost i eleganciju. Ipak, kako font postaje sve češći, zajedno sa sivim fasadama, on simbolizuje krajeve koje karakterišu brza izgradnja, renoviranja, rastuće kirije i iseljavanje dugogodišnjih stanovnika. Ove asocijacije doprinose percepciji Neutraface-a kao znaka i posledice promena na američkom tržištu nekretnina. Garza takođe istražuje istorijat fonta i trend njegove primene u luksuznim stambenim projektima, napominjući da je za neke—uključujući i nju samu—čak i lična sećanja vezuju za njegovo prisustvo. Njen tekst donosi uvid u to kako jedan jednostavan font može signalizirati dublje društvene promene.

article_content:
Able Seaton Port in Teesside, near Hartlepool, Britain, is among the contenders to dismantle the Costa Concordia, a shipwreck salvage project anticipated to be worth over €300 million. The port has been invited to submit a proposal for the extensive demolition, which is expected to require 200 workers over two years.

The Costa Concordia, a cruise ship that ran aground off Italy’s Giglio Island in 2012, remains stranded there after striking rocks and sinking, resulting in the deaths of 32 people. Nearly two years since the incident, the hull is almost ready to be towed from the Mediterranean island, according to the salvage team, though its final destination has yet to be decided.

A final selection among eight competing ports—including Able Seaton, and others located in Italy, Norway, Turkey, China, and France—is expected in March. Able UK, which operates the port, confirmed its participation in the tender process, highlighting previous experience recycling major vessels like a French aircraft carrier and US government ships. Its facility includes one of the world's largest dry docks and holds all necessary planning and environmental permissions. Previous projects, completed in October 2010, involved over 100 personnel.

Twelve companies have been asked to bid on breaking up, scrapping, and recycling the Costa Concordia. Italy’s environment minister, Andrea Orlando, expressed a preference for an Italian port but stated the government cannot mandate this decision. He noted the importance of proximity for environmental and logistical reasons, but acknowledged some Italian ports may need significant upgrades to accommodate the project.

In September 2013, the 114,000-ton Costa Concordia was pulled from the rocks in a complex 19-hour salvage operation, considered the largest and most expensive of its kind. Captain Francesco Schettino, who was in command at the time, is currently on trial in Grosseto, Tuscany, on charges of multiple manslaughter and abandoning ship.

More than 1,000 concrete stacks and six underwater platforms are stabilizing the vessel, and Costa Crociere has chartered the world’s largest semi-submersible vessel, the Dockwise Vanguard, for €30 million over three months to transport the Concordia. Michael Thamm, the company's chief executive, stated confidence that the ship could be removed by June, bringing the total salvage cost to an estimated €600 million (£496 million).

The announcement of the tender coincides with preparations for memorial events on Giglio to mark the disaster's second anniversary, including a mass and a concert to honor the victims.

article_content: The UK government plans to introduce new laws cracking down on companies responsible for sending nuisance calls and texts. Offenders could now face fines of up to £500,000 as enforcement is strengthened. Under the new rules, authorities will no longer need to show that these communications caused 'substantial harm or distress' before taking action, making it easier to hold businesses—and their leaders—accountable. Last year, over 175,000 complaints about nuisance calls and texts were made to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO). Consumer research estimates that four out of five people receive cold calls at home regularly, with a third feeling intimidated by such approaches. The volume of spam, particularly texts about debts or claims, continues to rise, with as many as a billion unwanted calls and messages sent each year. Some companies are even believed to have procured contact information illegally or run scams. Culture Secretary Sajid Javid pushed for legal reform after discovering that a majority of people have been put off answering their phones by nuisance calls. The government consulted on these changes last year, and the reforms are set to be implemented soon. Strict legal definitions previously made it hard to punish offenders. In one instance, a £300,000 fine imposed by the ICO on a marketing company was overturned on appeal, as no 'substantial distress' was proven. The new law eliminates such hurdles, a move supported by Digital Minister Ed Vaizey, who insists these measures send a clear warning to those who harass consumers. Research conducted by call-handling firm alldayPA reports that some businesses receive as many as 30 unsolicited calls daily, a heavy burden, particularly for small enterprises. David Joseph of alldayPA described the situation as 'out of control.' Vulnerable groups, including the elderly and those with conditions such as Alzheimer’s, are especially at risk from this kind of targeting. The Information Commissioner, Christopher Graham, has lobbied for stronger powers to stop firms from sending aggressive marketing to such individuals. Last year, reforms enhanced cooperation between Ofcom and the ICO, streamlining the process of acting against rule-breakers. Since 2012, the ICO has fined nine companies a total of £815,000 for similar offenses. Meanwhile, telecommunications regulator Ofcom has fined seven companies nearly £2 million over abandoned or silent calls. Consumer advocates, particularly the group Which?, have welcomed these moves. Richard Lloyd, chair of the Nuisance Calls Task Force, encouraged regulators to utilize new enforcement powers and pursue senior executives where appropriate, stating that even a single nuisance call could now lead to major fines. Previously, strict legal requirements limited the regulators' ability to take action. By lowering these barriers, the new law aims to better protect both individuals and businesses from persistent nuisance communication.

CapitaLand India Trust (CLINT) has secured a five-year construction loan of ₹1,300 crore from JP Morgan India to finance the first phase of its upcoming data centre in Navi Mumbai. According to Sanjeev Dasgupta, CEO of CapitaLand India Trust Pte Ltd, obtaining this onshore loan in India will diversify CLINT’s funding sources and help optimize financing costs. Construction on the Navi Mumbai data centre is underway and is expected to be completed by mid-2025. When finished, the facility will have a power capacity of 108 MW.

In addition to the Navi Mumbai project, CLINT is developing three more data centres in India. The trust, previously known as Ascendas India Trust, was the first Indian property trust to be listed in Asia when it joined the Singapore Exchange in August 2007. Its main objective is to own income-producing real estate primarily used as business spaces in India, with the potential to develop or acquire land and uncompleted developments. As of September 30, CLINT managed assets worth S$2.7 billion.

The data centre industry in India has seen rapid investment, with $14 billion invested over the past five years. CBRE predicts this figure will surpass $20 billion by 2025, reflecting strong demand driven by improved technology infrastructure and the increasing adoption of 5G, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and the Internet of Things (IoT).

In other business news: India’s industrial output slowed in September, partly due to an unfavourable base effect and excess rainfall disrupting production. Manipal Education and Medical Group chairman Ranjan Pai invested ₹1,400 crore (about $168 million) into Aakash Institute, a subsidiary of Byju’s. Meanwhile, companies are noting the value that tech-savvy youth bring to digital transformation initiatives.

article_content:
Automotive expert Tom Torbjornsen answers a reader question about diagnosing exhaust issues and what steps to take.

Question: Smoke is coming out of the tailpipe of my 2002 Chrysler Sebring, which has 90,000 miles on it. I need to add a quart of oil to the engine each week. Is this a serious problem? What should I do? – Sally, New York.

Answer: Sally, engines burn oil for several reasons, most commonly due to bad valve seals, worn valve guides, a pressurized crankcase caused by a clogged PCV (Positive Crankcase Ventilation) valve or breather system, or blow-by from worn piston rings.

Bad valve seals are found in the cylinder head above the combustion chamber. Oil is pumped there under pressure (40 to 80 PSI) to lubricate the valve train. These seals prevent oil from entering the engine when the valve is open. When they fail, oil can leak into the combustion chamber and burn, producing smoke.

Valve guides, which help position the valves, also wear out over time. An excessive gap can allow oil to flow down the valve stem into the combustion chamber despite the valve seals, leading to oil burning.

A clogged PCV or breather system can prevent your engine from releasing internal pressure. This can force oil into the fuel delivery system, where it is burned in the engine.

Finally, worn piston rings can cause combustion pressure to leak into the crankcase, pushing oil up into the engine, also resulting in oil consumption and smoke.

Having to add a quart of oil weekly is excessive. While some issues may be relatively simple (like a clogged PCV), others may indicate serious engine wear. Take your vehicle to a professional for diagnostics. The technician will likely check the PCV system, run a compression test, and do a cylinder leak-down test to identify the source of oil loss and smoke.

Smoke colors can help diagnose the issue:
- Blue smoke typically means burning engine oil. In rare cases, it can also mean burning transmission fluid if the vacuum modulator valve fails.
- White smoke usually means water is entering the combustion chamber from a blown head gasket, or in some cases, bulk unburnt fuel is escaping as vapor. White smoke from unburnt fuel will smell like gasoline and can be hazardous.

If your car emits continued smoke, or you are going through oil or coolant quickly, you can add fluids and keep driving temporarily. However, these problems do not resolve on their own and may get worse, risking catastrophic engine failure. Routine maintenance is key to preventing expensive future repairs.

Automobilski ekspert Tom Torbjornsen odgovara na pitanje čitateljke o dijagnostikovanju problema sa izduvnim gasovima i sledećim koracima koje treba preduzeti.

Pitanje: Dim izlazi iz auspuha mog Chrysler Sebring iz 2002. godine, koji ima 90.000 milja. Svake nedelje moram da dolivam po litar ulja u motor. Da li je ovo ozbiljan problem? Šta da radim? – Sali, Njujork.

Odgovor: Sali, motori troše ulje iz više razloga, najčešće zbog loših zaptivki ventila, istrošenih vođica ventila, zapušenog PCV (sistema za pozitivnu ventilaciju kartera) ili sistema za disanje, kao i prodora gasova zbog istrošenih klipnih prstenova.

Loše zaptivke ventila su u glavi motora iznad komore za sagorevanje. Ulje se pod pritiskom (40 do 80 PSI) pumpa u vrh motora da podmaže ventilni mehanizam. Ove zaptivke sprečavaju ulje da ulazi u motor dok je ventil otvoren. Ako zaptivke popuste, ulje može dospeti u komoru za sagorevanje i izgoreti, što izaziva dim.

Vođice ventila, koje pomažu pozicioniranje ventila, takođe se vremenom troše. Preveliki zazor omogućava ulju da prolazi niz osovinu ventila do komore za sagorevanje, čak i pored zaptivki, što dovodi do sagorevanja ulja.

Zapušen PCV ili sistem za disanje može sprečiti motor da izbaci višak unutrašnjeg pritiska. To može naterati ulje da dospe u sistem za dovod goriva, gde se sagoreva u motoru.

Istrošeni klipni prstenovi mogu dovesti do toga da pritisak sagorevanja curi u karter, gurajući ulje natrag u motor, što takođe izaziva veću potrošnju ulja i dim.

Dodavanje litre ulja svake nedelje je znak prevelike potrošnje. Neki problemi su jednostavni za rešavanje (kao što je zapušen PCV), ali drugi mogu ukazivati na ozbiljno habanje motora. Preporučuje se dijagnostika kod profesionalnog servisera. Tehničar će verovatno proveriti PCV, uraditi test kompresije i test curenja cilindara kako bi utvrdio uzrok.

Boja dima može pomoći:
- Plavi dim obično znači sagorevanje motornog ulja. Retko, može značiti sagorevanje ulja iz menjača ako vakuumski modulator zakaže.
- Beli dim najčešće označava ulazak vode u komoru za sagorevanje zbog pokvarene zaptivke glave motora ili preliva goriva kroz usis. Beli dim od goriva ima miris benzina i može biti opasan.

Ako vaš automobil nastavlja da dimi ili brzo troši ulje/rashladnu tečnost, možete povremeno dolivati tečnosti i voziti. Ipak, problemi se neće sami rešiti, mogu se pogoršati i dovesti do ozbiljne havarije. Redovno održavanje je ključno za sprečavanje visokih troškova popravke.
