An Indonesian couple, Jamaliah and Septi Rangkuti, have experienced the extraordinary: they were reunited with both of their children, ten years after the devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami swept them away. The family had an emotional reunion this Monday with their son, Arif Pratama Rangkuti, now 17, bringing together all members—including their younger son Jumadi—for the first time in a decade.

The tragedy struck Aceh, Indonesia’s westernmost province, killing more than 170,000 people locally and tens of thousands in neighboring countries. Arif and his younger sister, Raudhatul Jannah, were carried off by the floodwaters as children.

In June, Jamaliah and Septi were joyfully reunited with Raudhatul, now 14, after a relative recognized her in an Aceh village. The girl, who had been raised by a foster mother named Syarwani in Meulaboh, was returned to her parents after her identity was confirmed.

Their son Arif’s story came to light after media attention surrounding Raudhatul’s return. According to his parents, Arif had lived as a street child for years in Payakumbuh, Sumatra, often sleeping in outdoor markets and abandoned shops. A local couple, Lana Bestari and Windu Fajri, who run an Internet cafe, cared for Arif after finding him asleep outside their business. Bestari contacted the Rangkuti family when she recognized Arif from childhood photos shown on television.

Arif was reunited with his family after speaking by phone and meeting with his parents, younger brother Jumadi, and newly found sister this week. The family suspects that both children were initially rescued by fishermen and taken to the Banyak Islands off Aceh’s coast. Raudhatul was adopted by a family in Aceh, while Arif lived independently until being identified.

“I prayed every night, because inside I believed my child was still alive,” Jamaliah told reporters, moved to tears as she embraced her son. “My husband always said our son was alive,” she added.

The family considers their reunion a miracle—a testament to enduring hope in the face of tragedy.
translated_content:
Indonežanski par, Jamaliah i Septi Rangkuti, doživeo je pravo čudo: ponovo su se našli sa svojom decom deset godina nakon što ih je razorni cunami iz 2004. odneo iz njihovog naručja. Porodica je ovog ponedeljka imala emotivan susret sa sinom, Arifom Pratama Rangkutijem, sada sedamnaestogodišnjakom, i po prvi put posle decenije svi članovi—uključujući mlađeg sina Jumadija—ponovo su zajedno.

Tragedija je pogodila provinciju Aceh na zapadu Indonezije, usmrtivši preko 170.000 ljudi tamo i još desetine hiljada u drugim zemljama. Arif i njegova mlađa sestra, Raudhatul Jannah, tada su kao deca odnela talasi.

U junu su Jamaliah i Septi imali srećan ponovni susret sa Raudhatul, sada četrnaestogodišnjakinjom, nakon što ju je rođak prepoznao u jednom selu u Acehu. Devojčicu je podizala hraniteljka Syarwani u Meulabohu, a roditeljima je vraćena kad je potvrđen njen identitet.

Priča o Arifu je postala poznata nakon što su mediji izveštavali o povratku njegove sestre. Prema rečima roditelja, Arif je godinama živeo kao dete na ulici u Payakumbuhu na Sumatri, često spavajući na pijacama i po napuštenim radnjama. Lokalni par, Lana Bestari i Windu Fajri, vlasnici internet kafića, brinuli su o Arifu nakon što su ga pronašli kako spava ispred njihovog lokala. Bestari je kontaktirala porodicu Rangkuti kada je na televiziji prepoznala Arifa sa deteće fotografije.

Arif se ponovo sreo s porodicom nakon telefonskog razgovora, a zatim i susreta sa roditeljima, mlađim bratom Jumadijem i pronađenom sestrom ove nedelje. Porodica veruje da su decu spasli ribari koji su ih odveli na ostrva Banyak kraj obale Aceha. Raudhatul je usvojila porodica u Acehu, dok je Arif sam živeo sve do prepoznavanja.

"Svake noći sam se molila jer sam verovala da je moje dete živo", izjavila je Jamaliah kroz suze dok je grlila sina. "Moj muž je uvek tvrdio da je naš sin živ."

Porodica svoju ponovnu zajednicu smatra čudom—dokazom koliko nada može da opstane čak i posle najveće tragedije.

article_content: Police have uncovered a £1 million mansion in March, Cambridgeshire, that had been transformed into a cannabis factory with over 1,000 plants. Officers raided Wendreda House after an anonymous tip-off about a strong smell coming from the property. Inside, they discovered three large water tanks on the ground floor supplying seven growing rooms, along with a network of air filtration systems, electrical wiring, and lights. Wendreda House, valued at just over £1 million according to Zoopla, has nine bedrooms, six bathrooms, two utility rooms, and four drawing rooms. The persistent humidity and dampness had caused thick mould in the house. Detective Inspector David Murphy of Cambridgeshire Police remarked that the house looked like something from 'Downton Abbey' or 'Grand Designs.' He noted that it's rare to find such a professional cannabis setup in a prominent residential area. It is believed the mansion was used to cultivate cannabis for approximately six months. The downstairs rooms were still in relatively good condition, with sofas, tables, and a kitchen containing food and drinks. Fashion magazines remained on a coffee table under chandeliers and polished oak floors. However, the upper floors had been cleared of furniture and fitted with growing equipment and blacked-out windows. Police found cannabis plants at different stages of development, including young plants in the basement, apparently in a nine-week growth cycle. The electrical system had been bypassed to avoid high electricity bills, with lights left on for about 18 hours a day to accelerate growth. Two men in their 20s were arrested and are being questioned. The property is named after St Wendreda, a Saxon princess who spent much of her life in March, where she established a Benedictine nunnery.

Kuća Vendreda, procenjena na nešto više od milion funti prema Zoopli, ima devet spavaćih soba, šest kupatila, dve vešernice i četiri salona. Stalna vlažnost i miris prouzrokovali su debeli sloj buđi. Detektiv inspektor Dejvid Marfi iz policije Kembridžšira izjavio je da kuća izgleda kao nešto iz serije 'Downton Abbey' ili emisije 'Grand Designs.' On je naglasio da je retkost pronaći ovako profesionalnu fabriku kanabisa u ovako poznatom stambenom kraju. Pretpostavlja se da je vila korišćena za uzgoj kanabisa oko šest meseci. Donje prostorije su i dalje bile u solidnom stanju, sa sofama, stolovima i kuhinjom u kojoj su ostali hrana i piće. Modni časopisi su stajali na stolu za kafu ispod lustera i poliranog drvenog poda. Psi su gornji spratovi ispražnjeni od nameštaja i opremljeni uređajima za uzgoj i zamračenim prozorima. Policija je pronašla biljke u raznim fazama rasta, uključujući mlade biljke u podrumu, verovatno u devetonedeljnom ciklusu. Električne instalacije su bile zaobiđene radi uštede na računima, a svetla su radila 18 sati dnevno radi bržeg rasta. Dva muškarca u dvadesetim godinama su uhapšena i ispituju se. Nekretnina nosi ime po svetoj Vendredi, saksonskoj princezi, koja je veći deo života provela u Marču i osnovala benediktinski manastir.

article_content: KARACHI, Pakistan: Pakistan's central bank is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting on Monday, according to a Reuters poll of analysts. This comes as the country prepares for its first review under a $3 billion International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan program, which was approved in July and helped prevent a sovereign default, though attached conditions have made controlling inflation more difficult. The IMF's first review of Pakistan's program is set to begin on November 2. The median forecast from 15 analysts polled by Reuters is for no change in interest rates. Only two analysts expect a rate cut, of 50 and 100 basis points respectively. "The central bank cannot influence near-term inflation, especially from the supply side, through further rate hikes. Demand contraction has already occurred," said Muhammad Ali, an analyst at AKD Securities. Pakistan's inflation rate rose to 31.4% year-on-year in September, up from 27.4% in August, fueled by high fuel and energy prices. Inflation has remained in double digits since November 2021. The government's inflation target for the current fiscal year is 21%, but inflation averaged 29% in the first quarter. "The State Bank of Pakistan is expected to hold interest rates at current levels because real rates are comfortably positive on a 12-month forward basis," Tahir Abbas, head of research at Arif Habib Ltd, said. He added, "With the IMF review scheduled for early November, the SBP may keep rates unchanged for now." The SBP kept its key interest rate unchanged at 22% in September, surprising some analysts who expected an increase of at least 150 basis points. The bank has held rates steady for two consecutive meetings after raising them by a total of 12.25 percentage points since April 2022. Caretaker Prime Minister Anwaar ul Haq Kakar has said the government is using fuel price reductions and a price control mechanism to limit inflation. Rising economic difficulties and political tensions before the November national election triggered sporadic protests in September. Many Pakistanis say they are struggling financially. Reuters poll of expectations: Most organizations, including AKD Securities, Arif Habib Limited, EFG Hermes, and others expect no change. Multiline Securities predicts a 100 basis point cut, and Vector Securities forecasts a 50 basis point cut. The median expectation is no change.

article_content: More Americans are taking part in hunting and fishing, with autumn marking a popular season for getting outdoors. Based on U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service data, hunter numbers have risen by 9% and angler numbers by 11% in the past five years. This increase is tied to several factors: the search for affordable local vacations, interest in how food is sourced, and the appeal of self-sufficiency. Steven Rinella, host and author of 'Meat Eater,' attributes this trend to people's desire to reconnect with nature and personally gather their food. Jeff Rupert from the National Wildlife Refuge System points out that many now seek a deeper relationship to the food they eat, recognizing that meat comes from animals, not just supermarket shelves. The farm-to-table dining movement is also fueling interest, reflecting a broader cultural push to understand food origins. While hunting demands skill and patience—and often involves challenging conditions—there are now nationwide programs for beginners, children, women, and people with disabilities. Rinella currently recommends wild pig hunts in northern California and central Texas, waterfowl and upland bird hunting in the Dakotas and southeast, and grouse or pheasant hunting in the upper Midwest. Big-game hunts like elk or bear require planning ahead for permits. Various destinations across the U.S. cater to hunters and anglers with a range of lodging options. Colorado's High Lonesome Ranch, for instance, provides high-end and basic accommodations alongside guided big-game and fishing trips. Georgia’s Southern Woods Plantation offers guided quail hunts, and Bond Swamp National Wildlife Refuge has newly added bird and big-game hunting. In Wisconsin, Justin Trails Resort welcomes deer, turkey, and waterfowl hunters, and North Carolina’s The Webb Farm combines quail hunting with classic Southern hospitality. In Michigan, Grosse Ile Pilot House now supports hunting at the Detroit River International Wildlife Refuge, while Shelter Harbor Inn in Rhode Island provides comfort near the Ninigret National Wildlife Refuge, which offers deer hunting and fishing. Prices and amenities differ—ranging from rustic to luxurious—and services often include guides, prepared meals, and license help. This outdoor tourism can benefit local economies and support conservation initiatives. Whether for recreation, supplementing food supplies, or upholding tradition, hunting and fishing’s rising popularity mirrors a societal shift towards outdoor activity and resourcefulness. Readers are invited to share their views or experiences with hunting as a hobby or as a source of food.

article_content: The 'Diamonds Suck' website offers a sharp critique of the diamond industry, presenting itself as a counter to recent news that industry players have succeeded in stabilizing diamond prices. The site is built on two core arguments: firstly, that diamonds are significantly overpriced, and secondly, that a lesser-known naturally occurring gemstone, moissanite, outperforms diamonds in virtually every key area—including cut, color, clarity, durability, fire, brilliance, and cost. The site's author clarifies that they have no ties to the diamond or moissanite industries. The primary aim of the site is to educate consumers, particularly those considering expensive jewelry purchases like engagement rings, about moissanite and its advantages over diamonds. The author emphasizes the risks of starting married life with substantial debt from a diamond ring, pointing out that financial stress is a leading cause of marital tension. The website maintains that the resale value of diamonds falls far below retail prices, likening the markup in jewelry stores to being overcharged for an ordinary item. In essence, the site contends that the diamond industry relies on inflated prices rather than inherent value.

Sajt je zasnovan na dva glavna argumenta: prvo, da su dijamanti značajno precenjeni; i drugo, da jedan manje poznat, prirodno nastao dragi kamen – moisanit – premašuje dijamante u gotovo svim bitnim aspektima, uključujući rez, boju, čistoću, izdržljivost, vatru, briljantnost i cenu. Autor sajta naglašava da nema nikakve veze sa industrijom dijamanata ili moisanita. Glavni cilj sajta je edukacija potrošača, posebno onih koji razmišljaju o kupovini skupocenog nakita poput vereničkog prstena, o moisanitu i njegovim prednostima u odnosu na dijamante. Autor ističe rizik od započinjanja bračnog života sa velikim dugom zbog kupovine dijamantskog prstena, naglašavajući da je finansijski stres vodeći uzrok tenzija u braku. Sajt tvrdi da prodajna vrednost dijamanata znatno zaostaje za maloprodajnim cenama, upoređujući maržu u zlatarskim radnjama sa preplaćivanjem običnog predmeta. U suštini, sajt smatra da se vrednost dijamanata zasniva na naduvanim cenama, a ne na njihovoj suštinskoj vrednosti.

article_content: Zoe Cook, age 38, co-manages a catering company with her husband Jamie in Cudham, Kent, and is the mother of two daughters, Lila (9) and Kiera (7). Remarkably, over three years, she lost over three stone and dropped from a size 16 to a size 12, without resorting to restrictive diets. Instead, her transformation stemmed from a weekly 90-minute Ashtanga yoga class and occasional home routines. At first, Zoe was doubtful—believing yoga wouldn't suit her or deliver results. Even Jamie was skeptical, questioning the effectiveness of exercise that doesn’t make you sweat. Zoe's motivation to try yoga was to handle stress from juggling family and a business, feeling unfit and sleep-deprived. With encouragement from a family member, who became her yoga instructor, Zoe tried Ashtanga, a style noted for its energetic and structured flow, synchronizing breath and movement. To her surprise, Zoe's sleep improved immediately after her first session, and she experienced new muscle aches. Yoga became her essential weekly personal time, despite her busy life. Over time, her body underwent tangible changes: arms, thighs, and midsection became trimmer and more toned. Now weighing about 9st 7lb (from a previous 13st) at 5ft 5in tall, Zoe sometimes fits into size 10 clothing. She lost the initial weight within weeks, with long-term steady progress in the years following. Zoe notices that when she skips classes due to work, she regains weight and feels less energetic. Zoe did not radically change her diet but found yoga led her to prefer lighter meals before classes and healthier snacks afterwards. She continues to feel surprised and thankful for yoga’s impact on her body and mind, seeing it as a lifelong practice. Natalie Reid, 38, is a part-time retail worker from South West London, living with partner Dan (44) and their daughters Rain (10) and Noa (2). Inspired by her cousin’s noticeable results with Bikram yoga, Natalie gave it a try. Previously, she felt uncomfortable with her post-baby body, moving from size 10-12 to 14. Bikram yoga, held at 40°C and high humidity, initially seemed daunting. Natalie struggled with some poses but finished her first class feeling unexpectedly uplifted. Soon, she attended classes every other day and became a regular member. Within months, Natalie noted greater muscle definition in her legs and abdomen, as well as a better self-image. She continued Bikram yoga through pregnancy, resuming it post-birth and returning to her earlier clothing size. Her doctor confirmed she’d lost over a stone since starting. Natalie didn’t significantly alter her diet, except for increasing her water intake to about two liters daily. She credits yoga for improving both her physical and mental wellbeing.

Zoi nije bitno menjala ishranu, ali je joga uticala da pre treninga bira laganiju hranu, a posle vežbanja da između obroka češće uzme voće ili orašaste plodove. Ubrzo je išla svaki drugi dan, a onda je uzela i mesečnu članarinu. Posle nekoliko meseci primetila je bolje definisane mišiće na nogama i stomaku, a i samopouzdanje joj je poraslo. Tokom druge trudnoće nastavila je Bikram jogu, nakon porođaja se brzo vratila starom broju garderobe. Doktor joj je potvrdio da je izgubila preko šest kilograma od početka. Dijetu nije menjala, osim što sada pije više vode. Kaže da joj je joga značajno poboljšala i fizičko i psihičko stanje.

Philippe Reines, a longtime adviser and spokesperson for Hillary Clinton, expressed intense frustration over Anthony Weiner’s latest sexting scandal. On a campaign conference call before Weiner’s July 23 news conference, Reines reportedly used strong language, telling the New York mayoral candidate that he wanted to 'reach through this phone' and 'pull out' his throat. Reines’s outburst was partly motivated by loyalty to Huma Abedin, Weiner’s wife, who has been a close friend and aide to Hillary Clinton for over a decade.

Though not a paid member of Weiner’s campaign, Reines has been assisting out of support for Abedin. He has also been acting as the main line of communication between Abedin and Clinton, ensuring Hillary Clinton was aware of Weiner’s actions before the news became public.

Abedin, employed by Clinton since she was 19, has seen her professional and personal ties with the former Secretary of State tested through the public scrutiny of Weiner’s controversies. Media coverage has often drawn parallels between Abedin’s situation and the Clintons’ own experiences during the 1990s.

Clinton aides, including Reines, have worked behind the scenes to support Abedin while aiming to protect Clinton’s public image from negative fallout. Reines recently advised Abedin not to appear in a new campaign video for her husband that was released on Monday. In recent days, Abedin has stopped campaigning alongside Weiner in New York and returned to her work in Washington.

Abedin and Reines were seen dining at a popular Chinese restaurant in Washington shortly after her return. During this period, Abedin also met with other longtime Clinton allies, such as Cheryl Mills, Clinton’s former chief of staff at the State Department.

Sources close to the Clintons believe Weiner should withdraw from the mayoral race, although they do not anticipate lasting consequences for Clinton’s future ambitions, beyond short-term embarrassment. Hillary Clinton is widely considered to be weighing a potential run for president in 2016.

article_content: Mai-Lan Tomsen Bukovec, Vice President of Technology at Amazon Web Services (AWS), has observed significant changes in cloud computing. Initially, organizations hesitated due to concerns about data security, ownership, and a lack of established best practices. Security was often inadequate, and few engineers specialized in cloud migration. Cloud computing has since evolved into an essential technology for businesses, with automation and simplified processes driving widespread adoption. At AWS, security is a foundational principle. Since its first service launched in 2006, AWS has integrated security into all offerings by default. AWS continuously updates services so customers can benefit from enhancements without having to modify their existing applications. Gartner predicts that by 2026, 75% of organizations will rely on cloud-based digital transformation strategies. AWS now provides over 240 cloud services. Among them, the Amazon S3 Intelligent Tiering storage class, introduced in 2018, automatically lowers costs for infrequently accessed data, optimizing expenditure. Customers have significant choice and control with AWS offerings. Amazon EC2 provides over 575 instance types, including high-performance options powered by AWS-designed chips for machine learning. Amazon S3 features seven storage classes, supporting needs from low-cost archiving to AI model training. Custom chips like AWS Trainium and Inferentia make machine learning workloads more efficient. Sustainability remains a priority for AWS. By 2023, AWS had launched 479 renewable energy projects worldwide, striving to operate entirely on renewable energy by 2025. The Graviton 3 processor, for instance, achieves up to 60% lower energy use for comparable performance. Generative AI is advancing quickly. AWS enables organizations to fine-tune large language models using secure, company-specific data. Vector databases support embedding this information, improving AI-generated responses for users. Privacy is integral: with products like Amazon CodeWhisperer and Amazon Bedrock, customer data remains private and does not feed back into training foundational AI models. All data remains secure and encrypted. Today, AWS technology underpins a variety of sectors, powering everything from urban infrastructure to financial services. Cloud skills are becoming vital for organizational adaptability and innovation. U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken, following an intensive tour of the Middle East, has shifted his diplomatic focus to Asia amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas war. On Tuesday, as G7 foreign ministers began two days of talks in Japan, Blinken called for the leading industrial democracies to present a unified response to the crisis. He underscored the importance of the G7 maintaining cohesion, as it has with issues like Russia’s war in Ukraine, to prevent further divisions over Gaza. In a meeting with Japanese Foreign Minister Yoko Kamikawa and following talks with Prime Minister Fumio Kishida, Blinken stated, “This is a very important moment for the G7 to come together in the face of this crisis and to speak with one clear voice.”

The devastating, month-long conflict in Gaza, as well as efforts to relieve its humanitarian fallout, will be a central focus of the meeting. However, the agenda also includes the Russian invasion of Ukraine, concerns over North Korea’s potential new nuclear test, and China’s growing influence.

Blinken, alongside foreign ministers from the U.K., Canada, France, Germany, Italy, and Japan, are seeking to prevent the Gaza war from further destabilizing the Middle East and to maintain consensus on broader global issues. Kamikawa reiterated Japan’s condemnation of the Hamas attack on Israel and expressed strong support for U.S. diplomatic efforts, highlighting the importance of U.S.-Japan unity.

The U.S. is advocating for increased humanitarian aid to Gaza, proposing military ‘pauses’ to permit aid entry and civilian evacuations, and beginning planning for post-conflict governance in the territory. Blinken described these steps as “a work in progress,” noting deep divisions over the concept of pauses. Israel remains opposed, while Arab and Muslim nations are demanding an immediate ceasefire, which the U.S. does not support. Discussions around Gaza’s future have also been contentious, with Arab states insisting that the immediate humanitarian situation is an urgent priority.

While G7 members are not directly part of the Gaza conflict, differences over the issue have emerged. The war has sparked large-scale pro-Palestinian and anti-Israel demonstrations, as well as differing positions in the UN. At the Security Council, France supported a call for a humanitarian truce in Gaza, which the U.S. vetoed for not condemning Hamas’s attack strongly enough; Britain abstained. In the General Assembly, the U.S. voted against an immediate ceasefire resolution, France supported it, and other G7 nations abstained.

Since before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the G7 has largely retained unity on major international issues. The group has condemned Russia’s war in Ukraine, called for North Korea to end its weapons programs, sought responsible action from China, and advocated for cooperation on global challenges, including health crises and artificial intelligence.

Blinken arrived in Tokyo from Turkey, after visiting Israel, Jordan, the West Bank, Cyprus, and Iraq. He plans to continue to South Korea and then India.

U utorak, dok su ministri spoljnih poslova G7 započeli dvodnevne razgovore u Japanu, Blinken je pozvao vodeće industrijske demokratije da nastupe jedinstveno povodom krize. Istakao je koliko je važno da G7 održi koheziju, kao u slučaju rata u Ukrajini, kako bi se izbeglo dalje produbljivanje razlika oko Gaze. Na sastanku sa japanskom ministarkom spoljnih poslova Joko Kamikavom i nakon razgovora sa premijerom Fumiom Kišidom, Blinken je rekao: „Ovo je veoma važan trenutak za G7 da se ujedini pred ovom krizom i govori jednim jasnim glasom."

Razorni jednomesečni sukob u Gazi i napori da se ublaže njegove humanitarne posledice biće u centru pažnje sastanka. Dnevni red uključuje i rusku invaziju na Ukrajinu, strahovanja od mogućeg nuklearnog testa Severne Koreje i sve veći uticaj Kine.

Blinken i ministri iz Ujedinjenog Kraljevstva, Kanade, Francuske, Nemačke, Italije i Japana žele da spreče dalje nestabilnosti na Bliskom istoku ratom u Gazi i očuvaju konsenzus o drugim globalnim pitanjima. Kamikava je ponovila da Japan osuđuje napad Hamasa na Izrael i izrazila snažnu podršku američkim diplomatskim naporima, ističući značaj američko-japanskog jedinstva.

SAD zagovara veći dotok humanitarne pomoći Gazi, predlaže 'pauze' u vojnim operacijama kako bi pomoć stigla i civili mogli da izađu, i pokreće planiranje postkonfliktnog upravljanja teritorijom. Blinken je ove napore nazvao „radom u toku“, uz priznanje da postoji duboko neslaganje oko pauza. Izrael je protiv toga, dok arapske i muslimanske zemlje traže trenutni prekid vatre — što SAD ne podržava. Rasprave o budućnosti Gaze su takođe izazovne; arapske države insistiraju na rešavanju humanitarne krize kao hitnog prioriteta.

Iako G7 države nisu direktno umešane u sukob u Gazi, neslaganja postoje. Rat je izazvao masovne propalestinske i antiizraelske proteste, kao i različita glasanja u UN-u. U Savetu bezbednosti UN, Francuska je podržala humanitarnu pauzu u Gazi, što su SAD vetirale jer nije dovoljno oštro osudila napad Hamasa; Britanija je bila uzdržana. U Generalnoj skupštini UN, SAD su glasale protiv trenutnog primirja, Francuska za, a ostale G7 zemlje su bile uzdržane.

Od pre ruske invazije na Ukrajinu, G7 uglavnom čuva jedinstvo u vezi ključnih globalnih pitanja. Grupa je osudila rat Rusije u Ukrajini, zatražila kraj programa naoružanja severnokorejske strane, podstiče odgovornost Kine i promoviše saradnju u borbi protiv pandemija i zloupotreba veštačke inteligencije.

Blinken je u Tokio došao iz Turske, posetivši prethodno Izrael, Jordan, Zapadnu obalu, Kipar i Irak. Planira da nastavi put za Južnu Koreju i potom za Indiju.

article_content: British cyclist Mark Cavendish extended his lead in the Tour de France's sprint standings with a victory in Sunday's stage 15, while Thomas Voeckler retained his overall lead. Cavendish claimed his fourth win of this year's race and the 19th of his career, supported by his HTC Highroad team on the 192.5-kilometer route from Limoux to Montpellier. With just one minor climb, the stage favored the sprinters. Cavendish, 26, finished ahead of American Tyler Farrar and Italians Alessandro Petacchi and Daniel Oss. Cavendish now leads Jose Joaquin Rojas by 47 points in the race for the green jersey after Rojas placed fifth. The top finishers completed the stage in four hours, 20 minutes, and 24 seconds. Voeckler finished 71st, but since the top 116 riders were awarded the same finishing time as Cavendish, he kept the yellow jersey for Tuesday's 16th stage from Saint-Paul-Trois-Chateaux to Gap, as the race approaches the Alps. Voeckler is one minute and 49 seconds ahead of Luxembourg's Frank Schleck, with Frank's brother Andy in fourth place behind Australia's Cadel Evans. Voeckler told the race website it was a good day for his team, although he believed the sprinters' teams could have done more. "It was a good day, and the flat stage was welcome after a very hard day yesterday. Everyone is happy, and my teammates are proud to ride for this jersey. I must give all I can to keep it. I’m not obliged to keep the jersey, but I’ll do my best," he said. "This is my ninth Tour de France since 2003. I know I’m not able to win it, but since I took the jersey, I’ve always given everything. With strong rivals and tough stages ahead, I’m not sure if I can keep the lead." Cavendish praised his teammates for their support in his bid for the green jersey. "It was a nervous day, everyone fought for the front all day. I’m lucky to have a group of guys like this to protect me and take some pressure off, but it’s still hard," Cavendish said. "It was up and down, with crosswinds all day. It was a tough stage but ended in a sprint, and my team delivered me perfectly to the last 200 meters."

Kavendiš je osvojio svoju četvrtu pobedu na ovogodišnjoj trci i devetnaestu u karijeri, uz podršku svog tima HTC Highroad na deonici od 192,5 kilometara od Limua do Monpelijea. Sa samo jednim manjim usponom, etapa je odgovarala sprinterima. Kavendiš, sa 26 godina, završio je ispred Amerikanca Tajlera Farara i Italijana Alesandra Petakija i Danijela Osa. Sada Kavendiš vodi 47 poena ispred Hosea Hoakina Rohasa u trci za zelenu majicu, nakon što je Rojas bio peti. Najbolji su završili etapu za četiri sata, 20 minuta i 24 sekunde. Vokler je završio kao 71., ali pošto su prvih 116 vozača dobili isto vreme kao Kavendiš, zadržao je žutu majicu za 16. etapu u utorak, od Sen-Pol-Troa-Šatoa do Gapa, dok se trka približava Alpima. Vokler vodi ispred Luksemburžanina Franka Šleka minut i 49 sekundi, dok je njegov brat Endi četvrti, iza Australijanca Kejdela Evansa. Vokler je za zvanični sajt trke izjavio da je dan bio dobar za njegov tim, iako smatra da su timovi sprintera mogli više da doprinesu. "Bio je ovo dobar dan, a ravna etapa je dobrodošla nakon veoma teške jučerašnje etape. Svi su zadovoljni, a moji saigrači su ponosni što voze za ovu majicu. Moram dati sve od sebe da je zadržim. Nisam obavezan da je sačuvam, ali potrudiću se." "Ovo mi je deveti Tur de Frans od 2003. Znam da ne mogu da ga osvojim, ali otkad imam majicu, uvek sam davao sve od sebe. Uz jake rivale i teške predstojeće etape, nisam siguran mogu li zadržati vođstvo." Kavendiš je pohvalio svoje saigrače za podršku u borbi za zelenu majicu. "Bilo je uspona i padova, sa bočnim vetrom tokom celog dana. Bila je teška etapa, ali je završila u sprintu i moj tim me je doveo savršeno do poslednjih 200 metara."

Scottish First Minister Alex Salmond has announced plans for an independence referendum to take place in autumn 2014. Should the majority vote in favor, Scotland could become independent from the United Kingdom by March 2016. Afterward, a new Scottish parliament would be elected to draft a constitution, potentially prohibiting weapons of mass destruction in the country. 

The Scottish government released a detailed plan outlining the transition from devolved powers shared with Westminster to full national sovereignty. Deputy First Minister Nicola Sturgeon described this document as a roadmap to guide Scotland through this potential transformation.

Despite these preparations, many critics—particularly from opposition parties—have questioned whether the Scottish National Party (SNP) has adequately planned for the multifaceted process of independence. Addressing issues such as renegotiating thousands of international treaties, managing currency decisions, dividing national assets, and joining organizations like NATO, they argue the proposed timeline is too ambitious. UK government officials also claim that the independence debate distracts from day-to-day government matters affecting Scots.

The Electoral Commission has mandated the referendum question to be neutral, resulting in the phrasing: 'Should Scotland be an independent country?'

Public sentiment appears split, with surveys indicating 32% in favor of independence and 47% opposed. The cross-party 'Better Together' campaign continues to advocate for Scotland remaining in the UK, asserting most Scots see value in the union. SNP representatives, however, criticize the opposition for offering little beyond resistance to further autonomy.

Škotska vlada je objavila plan prelaska sa trenutnih ovlašćenja koja deli sa Vestminsterom na punu nacionalnu suverenost. Zamenica premijera Nikola Sturdžon opisala je ovaj dokument kao jasan vodič za potencijalnu transformaciju zemlje.

article_content: Tesla is seeking to establish a factory in India, with a possible investment ranging from $500 million to $2 billion based on the number of electric vehicles it is allowed to import at a reduced duty. Tesla has requested a 15% import duty for the first two years, which is much lower than the current Indian tariff range of 70% to 100%. Tesla’s investment offer is tied to the volume of cars permitted at the lower tax rate: $500 million for 12,000 vehicles and up to $2 billion for 30,000. Indian authorities are considering stricter caps, such as allowing only 10,000 vehicles at the concessional rate in the first year, with a possible 20% increase in the second year. Last fiscal year, India sold about 50,000 electric vehicles, with sales projected to hit 100,000 in 2024. The proposal is under review by several government bodies, including the DPIIT, Ministry of Heavy Industries, MoRTH, and Ministry of Finance, with oversight from the Prime Minister's Office. The government may require Tesla to provide a bank guarantee to ensure it meets its investment promises, though Tesla is negotiating to waive this requirement. The company plans to introduce the Model 3, Model Y, and a new hatchback to India, and could price the Model 3 and Model Y around Rs 38 lakh and Rs 43 lakh if the reduced duty is granted. Tesla has promised to localize 20% of the value of its Indian-made cars within two years, increasing that share to 40% over four years. Discussions are ongoing, and no final decisions have been announced yet. Tesla is looking to increase sourcing from Indian auto parts suppliers to $1.7–1.9 billion this year, up from $1 billion last year, according to Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal. Indian officials assert that any benefits for electric vehicle production will be extended equally to domestic and international manufacturers, with no company-specific exclusions or advantages. Other unrelated news reported includes India's booming IPO market and a rise in domestically grown flowers, which are not linked to the Tesla talks.

Tesla je zatražila carinu od 15% za prve dve godine, što je značajno niže od trenutnih indijskih stopa od 70% do 100%. Ponuda Tesle za ulaganje vezana je za broj automobila dozvoljenih po nižoj stopi: 500 miliona dolara za 12.000 vozila i do 2 milijarde dolara za 30.000 vozila. Indijske vlasti razmatraju da ograniče broj automobila, dozvoljavajući možda samo 10.000 vozila po toj stopi tokom prve godine, sa mogućim povećanjem od 20% u drugoj godini. U prošloj fiskalnoj godini u Indiji je prodato oko 50.000 električnih vozila, a za 2024. se očekuje 100.000 prodatih jedinica. Predlog trenutno razmatraju različita ministarstva, uključujući DPIIT, Ministarstvo za tešku industriju, MoRTH i Ministarstvo finansija pod nadzorom Kabineta premijera. Vlada može zahtevati od Tesle bankarsku garanciju kao osiguranje da će ispuniti investicione obaveze, iako Tesla pokušava da izbegne ovaj uslov. Kompanija planira da na indijsko tržište plasira Model 3, Model Y i novi hečbek – a Model 3 i Model Y bi mogli da koštaju oko 38 i 43 lakh rupija ako se odobre niže carine. Tesla je obećala da će lokalizovati 20% vrednosti svojih automobila proizvedenih u Indiji u roku od dve godine, i povećati to na 40% kroz četiri godine. article_content: Steve Jobs, the chief executive of Apple, spoke at the Apple Worldwide Developers Conference in San Francisco on June 6, 2011. Jobs, known for his vision and leadership, invented the iPhone and helped build Apple into one of the world’s most valuable companies. He was uncompromising, larger than life, and widely considered irreplaceable. His life's work shaped a future filled with user-driven technology. Sam Altman spent the past year taking on a role similar to Jobs as a Silicon Valley entrepreneur influencing the direction of technology. As CEO of OpenAI, he promised a transformative era led by artificial intelligence. Until last Friday, Altman led OpenAI, but the board dismissed him, citing that he was “not consistently candid” in communications. This surprised many in Silicon Valley and prompted employees to demand his return. Altman's attempt at reinstatement failed for now, drawing parallels to when Jobs was sidelined at Apple in 1985. Jobs returned after 11 years, leading Apple to a historic resurgence. His story continues to inspire founders today. Many in Silicon Valley idealize the visionary founder—a leader who creates what others can't yet imagine. Jobs epitomized this idea. He once said, “Some people say, ‘Give the customers what they want.’ But that’s not my approach. Our job is to figure out what they’re going to want before they do.” Recent events, like the resignation of Kyle Vogt as CEO of Cruise, General Motors' self-driving division, after a high-profile accident, show some risks of bold leadership. Vogt, a Cruise co-founder, played a key role in the company's development. After an accident involving a Cruise vehicle and suspension of the company’s license in California, he was replaced by GM executives. Founders like Altman, Holmes (Theranos), Neumann (WeWork), and Bankman-Fried (FTX) have had varying degrees of success and controversy. Visionaries can inspire innovation but also face intense scrutiny. Several Silicon Valley figures are informed by literature and popular culture, often drawing inspiration from stories about charismatic leaders. Altman has recommended Isaac Asimov’s Foundation series, which centers on visionary leadership. Yet, leading in real life remains challenging. Following his dismissal, Altman gained support from hundreds of OpenAI employees and praise from industry leaders like Eric Schmidt. OpenAI's primary backer, Microsoft, later announced Altman would be joining them. These developments highlight the ongoing influence of visionary leaders in technology. In other news, Indian authorities have detected significant tax evasion among online businesses, while Nawaz Modi has accused industrialist Gautam Singhania of assault. Such cases show the complexity and controversies often present in business and leadership.

Bio je beskompromisan, izuzetna ličnost i široko smatran nezamenjivim. Njegov životni rad oblikovao je budućnost ispunjenu tehnologijom koju kontrolišu korisnici. Sem Altman je protekle godine preuzeo ulogu sličnu Džobsovoj kao preduzetnik iz Silicijumske doline koji utiče na pravac tehnologije. Kao direktor OpenAI, obećao je transformativnu eru pod vođstvom veštačke inteligencije. Do prošlog petka, Altman je vodio OpenAI, ali ga je odbor smenio, navodeći da nije bio 'dosledno iskren' u komunikaciji. Ovo je iznenadilo mnoge u Silicijumskoj dolini i navelo zaposlene da zahtevaju njegov povratak. Altmanov pokušaj povratka za sada nije uspeo, što povlači paralele sa Džobsovim povlačenjem iz Apple-a 1985. godine. Džobs se vratio posle 11 godina i predvodio istorijski preporod kompanije. Njegova priča i danas inspiriše osnivače. U Silicijumskoj dolini često se idealizuje vizionarski osnivač – lider koji stvara ono što drugi ne mogu ni da zamisle. Džobs je oličenje te ideje. Jednom je rekao: 'Neki kažu, dajte korisnicima ono što žele. Ali to nije moj pristup. Naš posao je da otkrijemo šta će oni želeti pre nego što i sami saznaju.' Nedavni događaji, poput ostavke Kajla Vogta sa pozicije izvršnog direktora kompanije Cruise, dela General Motors-a za autonomna vozila, nakon zapaženog incidenta, pokazuju rizike smelog liderstva. Vogt, suosnivač Cruise-a, bio je ključan za razvoj kompanije, ali je nakon nesreće i suspenzije licence u Kaliforniji zamenjen liderima iz GM-a. Osnivači poput Altmana, Holms (Theranos), Njumana (WeWork) i Benkman-Frida (FTX) imali su različite uspehe i kontroverze. Vizionari mogu inspirisati inovacije, ali često se suočavaju sa velikim pritiscima. Mnogi lideri Silicijumske doline inspiraciju nalaze u književnosti i pop kulturi, često iz priča o harizmatičnim vođama. Altman je preporučio Asimovljev serijal 'Fondacija', koji se bavi vizionarskim liderstvom. Ipak, vođenje u stvarnom životu je teško. Nakon otkaza, Altman je dobio podršku stotina zaposlenih u OpenAI i pohvale industrijskih lidera poput Erika Šmita. Glavni investitor OpenAI, Microsoft, kasnije je objavio da će Altman preći kod njih. Ovi događaji ističu kontinuirani uticaj vizionarskih lidera u tehnologiji. Osim toga, indijske vlasti su otkrile značajnu poresku utaju među online poslovanjima, dok je Navaz Modi optužila industrijalca Gautama Singaniju za napad. Ovi slučajevi pokazuju složenost i kontroverze koje često prate poslovanje i liderstvo.

Sam Allardyce will stay on as manager of West Ham United after agreeing to steer the team towards a more attack-minded style. Under pressure after a challenging season, Allardyce kept his job following a board meeting where he accepted the necessity for a shift in football philosophy and a top-10 Premier League finish.

The board has granted Allardyce a £20 million transfer budget for the upcoming season and will take a more hands-on approach in player scouting and recruitment. He has also committed to hiring an attacking coach to help foster a more entertaining style of play and to prioritize the development of academy players.

Despite widespread fan dissatisfaction with the team’s direct approach and poor results—reflected in a recent poll where less than a quarter of supporters backed him—joint-chairmen David Gold and David Sullivan, together with vice-chairman Karren Brady, have opted to retain Allardyce for the last year of his contract. The board reiterated their commitment to the 'West Ham Way,' which they define as encompassing both the club’s style and ethos.

Allardyce presented his plan for the coming season to the board, assuring them he can deliver the desired footballing philosophy. The board recognized his success in keeping West Ham in the Premier League and highlighted the progress of players like Mark Noble, James Tomkins, and Winston Reid, as well as the club's notable defensive record under his guidance.

As the team prepares for its 2016 move to the Olympic Stadium—a vital part of their future strategy—the board made clear that improvements are expected on the pitch but credited Allardyce for his work so far. They expressed confidence that he possesses the passion and experience to make the 2014-15 campaign a success.

Allardyce voiced his commitment to leading West Ham forward, improving the squad, and working toward the goals established in the recent discussions.

Marvin Gail Owens, 62, has been arrested nearly 40 years after the disappearance and presumed murder of his wife, 23-year-old Deborah Diane Owens. Deborah, the mother of two young daughters, was last seen at her home in Oroville, California on November 19, 1978. Owens reported her missing two days later, and her body has never been found. For decades, police suspected Owens but lacked enough evidence to make an arrest. Recent advances—including new witness statements, some reportedly from the couple’s now-adult daughters, and further evidence from their home—finally led authorities to secure an arrest warrant.

Owens was taken into custody in Ogallala, Nebraska on Wednesday by Keith County sheriff’s deputies. He is awaiting extradition to Butte County, California. Investigators continue to explore possible links between Owens and the earlier disappearance of Essie Margarette Hiett, who vanished in February 1978 and was an acquaintance of the couple. Hiett’s car was discovered wrecked in a ditch, but she herself has never been found. 

Butte County officials, including long-time investigator Sheriff Perry Reniff and Sergeant Jason Hail, have pursued the Owens case relentlessly—Reniff continued to work on it even after retirement. Police indicate that Marvin Owens’ own statements contributed to the recent arrest, but declined to provide specifics. Authorities hope that with this arrest, justice will finally be served for Deborah Diane Owens and potentially for Essie Margarette Hiett as well.

Graham Eccles, a 32-year-old poet and children’s entertainer from Bude, Cornwall, has created his own postal service, delivering letters on a penny farthing bicycle. The idea was sparked when first class stamp prices were raised from 46p to 60p, prompting Graham to offer a more affordable and environmentally friendly alternative.

Operating as the Penny Farthing Postal Service, customers pay just 25p per letter. They drop their mail into collection boxes positioned throughout the town’s shops, with next-day—and sometimes same-day—delivery guaranteed. Initially sorting mail in his kitchen, Graham has now moved operations to his own sorting office. He recently received an official identifying code from Ofcom, the UK communications regulator, a step required for recognized postal services.

Graham’s endeavor has drawn international interest; he has been named an honorary member of the Letter Writers Alliance of America. His unique stamps, launched on April Fools’ Day, quickly sold out—480 stamps were bought within the first two days, and are now being collected and traded on eBay. Currently, Graham delivers around 100 letters daily, six days a week, ensuring Bude’s local mail reaches its destination quickly and with a nostalgic touch of history.

Ideja je nastala kada su cene markica za prvu klasu porasle sa 46 na 60 penija, što je Grahama podstaklo da ponudi jeftiniju i ekološki prihvatljiviju alternativu.

article_content: Losing a major job, especially one that offers the chance to make a real difference, can feel as if the air has suddenly disappeared from the room. On Friday, Secretary Eric Shinseki resigned as the head of the Department of Veterans Affairs amid controversy over wait times at VA hospitals. While I cannot presume to understand his personal feelings, I do have some insight based on my own experience. In 2012, I abruptly stepped down as administrator of the General Services Administration during a scandal over excessive spending at the agency's "Western Regions" training conference and dealings with contractors. The aftermath was predictable: tense meetings at the White House, intense media scrutiny, congressional investigations, and negative public perception, fueled in part by viral online videos. The situation was highly stressful. My long-standing connection with the people at GSA was suddenly cut off, leaving me deeply saddened. The political environment felt harsh and at times bullying. I also worried about my future and financial security. My elderly father was greatly upset and needed my support. However, what I mourned most was the work left unfinished. I believe meaningful work provides purpose and energy in life. Losing my position was very painful. Serving in a presidential administration was not only an honor, but also a unique opportunity to drive change and improvement. The resources, scale, and impact made it possible to positively affect government performance—through technology, energy efficiency, collaboration, a better environment for public servants, and rebuilding trust in government. Instead, I suddenly found myself at home, reflecting on what had happened. However, the early days after leaving a major role in Washington are never quiet. My personal network quickly reached out—messages of support, flowers, and other gestures poured in. Friends vented their outrage on my behalf; others offered perspective, saying, “It’s Washington. Everyone understands. You’ll be fine.” Though I wasn’t ready to accept that reassurance at the time, it proved accurate. Over time, I found myself with space and freedom I hadn’t had in years. Importantly, I discovered that I still had creativity and the drive to work. I uncovered a half-finished novel in my desk drawer and got started. Within a few months, I published my first book; a year later, I had written a second. Losing something important creates a vacuum, but over time, life fills that void. This has been my personal experience. From what I know of General Shinseki, he, too, understands this principle. I wish him success in the future. Join the conversation at Facebook.com/CNNOpinion.

article_content: With several major events approaching, enthusiasm is building at the Winter Olympics. Women’s figure skating is especially close, with Russia’s Adelina Sotnikova moving into second place after the short program, right behind South Korea’s Yuna Kim. Notably, Julia Lipnitskaya, though favored before, is now fighting to stay in medal contention after a fall. American observers have questioned the judging, but Sotnikova stands by her strong performance. Meanwhile, Kim is hoping to become only the third woman ever to win back-to-back golds in this event. In women’s ice hockey, the United States and Canada set up for another classic showdown. Canada holds an impressive streak, having won gold every Olympics since 1998, but the American team, with many veterans returning after their loss in Vancouver, is determined to break that run. Canadian star Hayley Wickenheiser is seeking a fourth Olympic gold. On the curling rink, Canada’s unbeaten women’s team led by Jennifer Jones faces Sweden in the final. Sweden has taken gold in the last two Olympics, led this time by Margaretha Sigfridsson. The memory of Sandra Schmirler, Canada’s beloved skip from 1998, adds emotional weight to the event. The Olympic debut of women’s ski halfpipe brings a strong U.S. lineup and Canada’s Roz Groenewoud, who honors her late teammate Sarah Burke—an athlete deeply influential in getting the sport recognized by the Olympics. Men’s ski cross remains anyone’s contest, as several athletes—including France’s Jean-Frederic Chapuis and American John Teller—are capable of reaching the podium in this unpredictable event.

Even before its premiere, everyone involved with Showtime’s acclaimed drama 'Homeland' believed it was something extraordinary, according to actor Mandy Patinkin. At the season two launch event in New York, cast and crew reflected on the show's rapid success. 'Homeland' centers on CIA officer Carrie Mathison (Claire Danes), who suspects returning Marine Sergeant Nicholas Brody (Damian Lewis), a former POW, may have become a threat to the U.S. After season one’s dramatic ending—with Brody running for Congress and Carrie, coping with bipolar disorder, preparing for therapy—the anticipation for season two is high.

Season one achieved critical acclaim, receiving nine Emmy nominations and winning four, including Outstanding Drama Series. The first season was recently released on DVD/Blu-ray, and Showtime will air a marathon of all 12 episodes ahead of season two’s premiere.

At the premiere party at the Intrepid Sea, Air and Space Museum, the full cast gathered, including Emmy winners Danes and Lewis, along with notable guests like Anna Wintour and Valentino. Highlights included a screening of the new season, themed treats, and fireworks beneath the Space Shuttle Enterprise.

Patinkin explained how, to prepare for his role as Saul Berenson, CIA Middle East Division Chief, he visited Langley and met with a former CIA chief, focusing on the emotional reality and familial themes present in the series. Actor David Harewood, who plays CIA Counterterrorism Center Director David Estes, prepared by meeting an operative, helping him capture the intense world of his character. He credits the show’s success to its authentic depiction of intelligence work and terrorism.

Amy Hargreaves (Maggie Mathison) highlighted Showtime’s support for careful scene development, and Morena Baccarin (Jessica Brody) discussed portraying a strong, resilient family matriarch. Diego Klattenhoff (Mike) noted the complexity of friendships and loyalties, while Morgan Saylor (Dana Brody) enjoyed exploring her character’s rebellious side and evolving relationship with her father.

Composer Sean Callery, who earned a 12th Emmy nomination, brought jazz influences to the soundtrack to embody Carrie’s impulsive character. He shared that the music deepens in season two.

Co-creator Alex Gansa described the team’s surprise when President Obama revealed 'Homeland' was one of his favorite shows and emphasized efforts to honestly portray the difficulties faced by returning soldiers, blending suspenseful drama with meaningful social themes.

Čak i pre premijere, svi uključeni u nagrađivanu dramu 'Homeland' na Showtime-u verovali su da je reč o nečemu izuzetnom, kaže glumac Mendi Patinkin. Na promociji druge sezone u Njujorku, ekipa i glumci su govorili o brzom uspehu serije. 'Homeland' prati agentkinju CIA Keru Metison (Kler Dejns), koja sumnja da se povratni marinac Nikolas Brodi (Dejmijen Luis), bivši ratni zarobljenik, pretvorio u pretnju za SAD. Posle napetog završetka prve sezone—Brodi kandiduje za Kongres, a Keri, suočena sa bipolarnim poremećajem, odlazi na terapiju—očekivanja za drugu sezonu su velika.

Prva sezona je stekla puno priznanja, sa devet Emi nominacija i četiri osvojene nagrade, uključujući najbolju dramsku seriju. Prva sezona je nedavno objavljena na DVD/Blu-ray izdanju, a Showtime planira i maraton svih 12 epizoda pred premijeru druge sezone.

Na promociji u Muzeju mora, vazduha i svemira Intrepid okupila se cela ekipa, uključujući Emi dobitnike Dejns i Luisa, kao i goste poput Ane Vintur i Valentina. Prikazana je prva epizoda nove sezone, poslužene su tematske poslastice, a vatromet je održan pod Spejs šatlom Enterprajz.

Patinkin je objasnio da se za ulogu Saula Berensona, šefa CIA bliskoistočne divizije, pripremao u Lengliju susrećući bivšeg šefa CIA. Fokusirao se na emocionalnu dimenziju i porodične teme serije. Glumac Dejvid Herud (Dejvid Estis, šef CIA centra za borbu protiv terorizma) pripremio se sastankom sa operativkom, što mu je pomoglo da oseti intenzitet profesije svog lika. Smatra da popularnost serije dolazi iz autentičnog prikaza obaveštajnog posla i teme terorizma.

Ejmi Hargrevs (Megi Metison) istakla je koliko Showtime daje vremena za ozbiljnu pripremu scena, a Morena Bakarin (Džesika Brodi) pričala je o ulozi snažne majke. Dijego Klatenhof (Majk) govorio je o složenim prijateljstvima, a Morgan Sejlor (Dana Brodi) uživa da glumi buntovničku stranu svog lika i odnos sa ocem.

Kompozitor Šon Keleri, sa 12 Emi nominacija, uneo je džez u muziku kako bi prikazao Kerinu impulsivnost. Muzika u drugoj sezoni postaje još izražajnija.

Kreator Aleks Gansa ispričao je kako je tim bio iznenađen kada je predsednik Obama rekao da mu je 'Homeland' omiljena serija, i istakao težnju da prikažu izazove povratka vojnika iz ratova, kombinujući napetu dramu sa društvenim temama. article_content: Recent events have brought dramatic change to Syria: government forces have relinquished key border crossings with Iraq and Turkey, rebels have captured territory in Damascus, and there are troubling reports of Syria’s chemical weapons being moved. Aleppo, long a bastion of the Alawite minority, has also seen fierce clashes. A pivotal moment was the bombing of a National Security Council meeting in Damascus, striking at the core of Syria’s defense hierarchy. Among the dead was Assef Shawkat, former chief of military intelligence and President Bashar al-Assad’s brother-in-law. During my time at the CIA, we tried to secure Syrian cooperation to stop foreign fighters moving through Damascus to Iraq, but efforts yielded little. Now, the same routes are facilitating fighters’ entrance into Syria. Shawkat’s reputation for rigor and loyalty helped sustain Assad’s regime recently. In contrast, Assad himself did not inspire confidence as a leader. After his older brother Bassel’s fatal car crash, Bashar assumed the presidency—a role for which his previous life as an ophthalmologist in London seemed better preparation, alongside his Westernized Sunni wife. Unable or unwilling to introduce genuine reforms, Assad has escalated his late father’s forceful repression, though without replicating Hafez Assad’s political skill. The recent loss of senior leadership has deeply unsettled the Alawite base; while some remain devoted, others are contemplating their next moves. The spotlight is shifting toward post-Assad scenarios. Intelligence agencies are tasked not only with assembling facts about opposition groups and their foreign ties, but also developing a comprehensive account of Syria’s complex situation. On the geopolitical stage, old power rivalries have reemerged. Russia and China oppose robust United Nations action—partly as a reaction to how Western powers handled Libya. In the region, Iran backs Assad while Saudi Arabia and Qatar support the rebels, reflecting the Sunni-Shia divide. The dominant narrative—shared in countless videos—shows a regime using force against a popular uprising. This storyline has captured international attention, but oversimplifies Syria’s intricate society. Alawites and other Shia minorities, together about 13% of Syrians, have controlled state power for decades, often at the Sunni majority’s expense. The rest—Kurds, Druze, Christians—make up smaller shares and remain cautious, concerned about both potential Sunni dominance and continuing Alawite control. There’s a danger in reducing the conflict to an ‘oppressed vs oppressor’ binary. It is, fundamentally, a sectarian struggle. Political theorists like Vali Nasr remind us Middle Eastern politics revolve around communal competition as much as state authority. As change nears, bringing minorities into the opposition could speed transition and make it more enduring. Backing for the opposition should depend on its openness to all communities. Only through genuine inclusiveness can Syria perhaps regain the earlier coexistence lost under the Assads. If not, a successor regime favoring only one group could worsen tensions and provoke further unrest. These views reflect the opinions of Michael V. Hayden.
translated_content: Nedavni događaji dramatično su promenili situaciju u Siriji: vladine snage su izgubile ključne granične prelaze sa Irakom i Turskom, pobunjenici su zauzeli delove Damaska, a pojavile su se zabrinjavajuće vesti o premeštanju sirijskog hemijskog oružja. Čak je i Alep, koji je dugo bio uporište alavitske manjine, pogođen žestokim sukobima. Prelomni trenutak bio je bombaški napad na sastanku Saveta za nacionalnu bezbednost u Damasku, što je uzdrmalo samu srž odbrambenog aparata Sirije. Među poginulima je bio i Assef Šaukat, bivši šef vojne obaveštajne službe i zet predsednika Bašara al-Asada. Dok sam radio u CIA, pokušavali smo da sarađujemo sa njim kako bismo zaustavili prolazak stranih boraca kroz Damask ka Iraku, ali rezultati su bili minimalni. Danas, istim putem borci ulaze u Siriju. Šaukat je bio poznat po odlučnosti i lojalnosti, što je u poslednje vreme pomagalo režimu. Za razliku od njega, sam Asad nikad nije ostavio utisak čvrstog vođe. Nakon smrti starijeg brata Basela, Bašar je neočekivano postao predsednik—pre toga je živeo kao oftalmolog u Londonu sa suprugom koja je odrasla na Zapadu. Bez volje ni sposobnosti za pravu reformu, Asad je pojačao surovost svog oca, ali bez iste političke veštine. Nedavni gubici vodećih ljudi uzdrmali su poverenje među alavitima; dok su neki i dalje lojalni, drugi traže izlaz. Sada se pažnja okreće pitanju šta posle Asada. Obaveštajne službe osim analize činilaca i uticaja, treba da pruže celovito razumevanje situacije. Na globalnom planu, oživela je rivalska igra istoka i zapada—Rusija i Kina blokiraju odlučne poteze UN zbog prošlih iskustava iz Libije. Na Bliskom istoku, Iran podržava Asada, dok Saudijska Arabija i Katar jačaju pobunjenike, što je odraz regionalnog sunitsko-šiitskog takmičenja. Najvidljivija priča—snimci represije režima protiv odlučne opozicije—dominira mrežama i vestima. Ipak, to je samo deo slike. Alaviti i druge šiitske manjine, kojih je oko 13%, decenijama kontrolišu vlast, često i protiv većinskih sunita. Druge manjine: Kurdi, Druzi i hrišćani su oprezne—plaše se i sunitske vlasti i produžene alavitske dominacije. Sukob je mnogo više od odnosa tlačitelja i potlačenih—u osnovi je sektaški. Politički analitičari poput Valija Nasra ističu da je za Bliski istok presudno pitanje moći između zajednica. Za održivu promenu potrebno je uključiti i manjine u opoziciju. Podrška opoziciji treba zavisiti od njenog otvaranja prema svim zajednicama. Samo tako Sirija može povratiti raniju međusobnu toleranciju. Ukoliko sledeća vlast bude jednostrano sunitska, to može produbiti podele i izazvati nove sukobe. Ovo su stavovi Michaela V. Haydana.

article_content: Kim Kyong-hui, 67, the aunt of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, is reported to have died under mysterious circumstances. Her death allegedly took place less than a month after her husband, Jang Song-Thaek, was executed on Kim Jong-un's orders. North Korean media suggested that Kim Kyong-hui either suffered a heart attack or took her own life. Since the execution of her husband on December 8, questions have circulated about her health and whereabouts. Kim Kyong-hui reportedly had heart disease and is believed to have suffered a heart attack soon after her husband's death, which many view as part of Kim Jong-un’s efforts to consolidate power. According to South Korea’s Chosunilbo newspaper, North Korean intelligence considers Kim Kyong-hui deceased, but the exact cause and location are unconfirmed. Some speculate that she died abroad while seeking medical care, as she had previously visited heart specialists in Singapore and Moscow. A prominent figure in North Korean politics, Kim Kyong-hui is also the sister of former leader Kim Jong-il. Her last known public appearance was in September at a concert with Kim Jong-un and his wife. Despite her husband's execution, she was selected for funeral planning duties for a senior official, which suggested she was safe at the time. Sources say Kim Kyong-hui struggled with alcoholism and depression, especially after her only child, Jang Kum-song, died by suicide in Paris in 2006. She has been photographed with her nephew Kim Jong-un and late husband in 2011, as well as in older images with her father, Kim Il-sung, and brother, Kim Jong-il. Toshimitsu Shigemura, a professor at Tokyo’s Waseda University and expert on North Korea, told the Daily Telegraph that her death would not be surprising given her longstanding health issues. He pointed out Kim Kyong-hui's influence in the regime and suggested her disappearance could cause political upheaval. Shigemura also speculated that Kim Jong-un might keep news of her death quiet for now to reinforce his authority.

article_content: People Magazine has announced that Hollywood actor Patrick Dempsey is this year’s 'Sexiest Man Alive.' Dempsey is best known for his role as Dr. Derek ‘McDreamy’ Shepherd in the popular TV show 'Grey’s Anatomy.' He has also starred in other films including 'Enchanted' and 'Made of Honour.' The 57-year-old actor said he was surprised by the news, which was revealed during the 'Jimmy Kimmel Live' show on Tuesday night. 'I was completely shocked, and then I started laughing, like, this is a joke, right? I’ve always been the bridesmaid!' he said. 'I’d completely forgotten about it and never even considered being in this position. So my ego is good.' Dempsey has been married to Jillian Fink, a professional makeup artist and beauty entrepreneur, for 24 years. They have three children: 16-year-old twins, Sullivan and Darby, and Talula, who is 21. In his interview with People, Dempsey expressed gratitude for the honor, saying it gives him the opportunity to make a positive impact. He is the founder of the Dempsey Center, an organization that supports cancer patients, created in memory of his mother. He was previously the runner-up for 'Sexiest Man Alive' in both 2005 and 2006. By topping the list this year, Dempsey joins a group of past honorees that includes Chris Evans, Paul Rudd, and Michael B. Jordan.

article_content: Isaac Richardson, a 20-year-old bartender from Woolwich, died after participating in NekNominate, a social media-driven drinking game. For the challenge, Isaac drank about 1.5 liters of a mix containing wine, vodka, beer, and whiskey within two minutes as friends recorded the event. Soon after, he collapsed and medical efforts to save him were unsuccessful. Reports found he had ingested enough alcohol to trigger a coma. At the inquest, Isaac’s mother, Melissa Richardson, stated that she did not blame his friends, pointing instead to NekNominate as the reason for her son's death. She reflected that without the game, her son would most likely be alive. NekNominate, which started in Australia, spread globally via social media, encouraging people to film themselves drinking excessive alcohol and then challenging others to do the same. Other tragedies were mentioned at the inquest, including the deaths of Stephen Brookes, who drank almost a bottle of vodka, and two young Irishmen, Ross Cummins and Jonny Byrne, both of whom died after participating in the game. Coroner Dr. Andrew Harris ruled Isaac’s death as accidental due to acute alcohol intoxication. Those present that evening testified that Isaac was not pressured or forced but accepted the challenge of his own will. Isaac was described as bright and sociable, though he had started drinking more heavily in the months before his death. His mother shared that, despite enjoying dares, Isaac was not someone who easily gave in to peer influence. Authorities concluded there was no evidence of a crime, and Melissa Richardson chose not to single out anyone as responsible, expressing hope that her story would raise awareness about the dangers of such drinking games.
translated_content: Ajzek Ričardson, dvadesetogodišnji barmen iz Vulviča, preminuo je nakon učešća u igri pijenja alkohola pod nazivom NekNominate, koja se širi putem društvenih mreža. Tokom izazova, Ajzek je popio oko 1,5 litra mešavine vina, votke, piva i viskija za samo dva minuta, dok su ga prijatelji snimali. Ubrzo nakon toga se srušio, a medicinske ekipe nisu uspele da ga spasu. Izveštaji su pokazali da je uneo količinu alkohola dovoljnu da izazove komu. Na saslušanju, Ajzekova majka, Melisa Ričardson, izjavila je da ne krivi njegove prijatelje, već ukazuje na igru NekNominate kao glavni razlog sinove smrti. Veruje da bi, da nije bilo ove igre, njen sin najverovatnije bio živ. NekNominate je započeo u Australiji, a zatim se proširio širom sveta putem društvenih mreža, podstičući ljude da se snimaju dok piju prekomerne količine alkohola i izazivaju druge na isto. Na saslušanju su pomenuti i drugi tragični slučajevi, uključujući smrt Stivena Bruksa, koji je popio skoro celu flašu votke, kao i dva mlada Irca, Rosa Kaminsa i Džonija Burna, koji su takođe preminuli zbog učešća u ovoj igri. Sudski veštak, dr Endru Haris, zaključio je da je Ajzek umro nesrećnim slučajem zbog akutnog trovanja alkoholom. Prisutni te večeri svedočili su da Ajzek nije bio prisiljen, već je sam prihvatio izazov. Ajzek je opisan kao bistar i druželjubiv, iako je poslednjih meseci pre smrti počeo više da pije. Njegova majka je rekla da je voleo izazove, ali nije bio podložan pritisku okoline. Nadležni su utvrdili da nije bilo krivičnog dela, a Melisa Ričardson nije želela nikoga da okrivi, već je izrazila nadu da će priča o njenom sinu podići svest o opasnosti ovakvih alkoholnih izazova.

article_content: Javier Milei, the leader of the Liberty Advances party and a far-right populist, is leading the race in Argentina’s presidential election amid widespread frustration over the failure of traditional parties to fix the economy. Voting is underway not only for the presidency but also for Congress and regional governors, with 130 lower house representatives and 24 national senators to be selected. Polls opened at 8am local time and will close at 6pm, with results expected late Monday. Years of economic decline and record inflation have propelled Milei, a 52-year-old economist and first-year lawmaker who calls himself an 'anarcho-capitalist,' to the forefront. He rose to prominence after a surprise primary win in August. Milei has drawn comparisons to former U.S. President Donald Trump and former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro due to his unorthodox style and radical proposals. Milei’s campaign has focused on Argentina’s severe economic crisis, with inflation hitting 138 percent in September. He has pledged to eliminate the central bank, replace the peso with the U.S. dollar as Ecuador and El Salvador have done, and sharply reduce public spending. Milei also vows to pursue cultural reforms, positioning himself as a staunch opponent of socialism and abortion—despite the latter being legalized in Argentina in 2020. His main opponents are Patricia Bullrich, a 67-year-old former security minister representing the center-right Together for Change coalition, and Sergio Massa, the 51-year-old incumbent economy minister from the ruling Peronist coalition. To secure the presidency, a candidate needs 45 percent of the vote, or 40 percent with a 10-point lead over the nearest rival; otherwise, a runoff will take place in November. While polls indicate Milei is the frontrunner, polling reliability has been questioned in previous elections. The newly elected president and vice president are expected to take office on December 10.
translated_content: Havier Milei, lider stranke Libertad Avanza i krajnje desničarski populista, vodi u trci za predsednika Argentine usred široko rasprostranjenog nezadovoljstva zbog neuspeha tradicionalnih partija da reše ekonomske probleme. Građani glasaju, ne samo za predsednika, već i za članove Kongresa i regionalne guvernere, pri čemu se bira 130 poslanika donjeg doma i 24 nacionalna senatora. Biračka mesta otvorena su od 8 sati ujutro do 18 sati po lokalnom vremenu, a rezultati se očekuju kasno u ponedeljak. Godine ekonomskog pada i rekordne inflacije dovele su Mileija, 52-godišnjeg ekonomistu i poslanika prve godine mandata, koji sebe naziva 'anarho-kapitalistom', u prvi plan. Postao je poznat nakon iznenađujuće pobede na primarnim izborima u avgustu. Mileija porede sa bivšim predsednicima SAD Donaldom Trampom i Brazilom Žairom Bolsonarom zbog njegovog nekonvencionalnog stila i radikalnih predloga. Njegova kampanja fokusira se na ozbiljnu ekonomsku krizu u Argentini, gde je inflacija u septembru dostigla 138 procenata. Milei je obećao da će ukinuti centralnu banku, zameniti pezo američkim dolarom kao što su uradili Ekvador i Salvador, i znatno smanjiti javnu potrošnju. Takođe je obećao kulturne reforme, predstavljajući se kao odlučan protivnik socijalizma i abortusa—iako je abortus legalizovan u Argentini 2020. godine. Njegovi glavni rivali su Patricia Bulrič, 67-godišnja bivša ministarka bezbednosti koja predvodi centrističku koaliciju Zajedno za promene, i Sergio Masa, 51-godišnji aktuelni ministar ekonomije iz vladajuće peronističke koalicije. Da bi osvojio predsedničke izbore, kandidat mora da osvoji 45 procenata glasova ili 40 procenata uz prednost od 10 poena u odnosu na najbližeg rivala; u suprotnom, drugi krug glasanja održaće se u novembru. Iako ankete pokazuju da je Milei favorit, njihova tačnost je u prošlosti bila upitna. Novi predsednik i potpredsednik trebalo bi da stupe na dužnost 10. decembra.

article_content: If you’re ready for a break from all the horror streaming on Hulu, October has some delightful rom-com options perfect for lifting your mood. Instead of spooky flicks, why not enjoy some heartwarming romance? Here are three standout romantic comedies to check out this month. First up is 'Robots,' a futuristic story set about ten years ahead where androids are almost indistinguishable from humans. Although having these highly advanced look-alikes is illegal, Elaine (Shailene Woodley) and Charles (Jack Whitehall) find a way to use their robot doubles to handle life’s chores, dating, and even a few cons. Everything unravels, though, when their robots—E2 and C2—fall for each other and begin living on their own terms, taking over their owners' identities. Forced to team up, Elaine and Charles try to track down their runaway doubles, even as their own relationship is far from friendly. Catch 'Robots' on Hulu. Next is the timeless rom-com 'Notting Hill.' Released nearly 25 years ago, its story feels more relevant than ever. Julia Roberts stars as Anna Scott, a superstar actress whose life changes after a chance encounter with Will Thacker (Hugh Grant), a London bookshop owner. Their mutual attraction draws them back together, but the relentless attention from the media may keep them apart. 'Notting Hill' remains a must-see—stream it now on Hulu. Lastly, there’s 'What’s Love Got To Do With It?'—a recent film with no connection to Tina Turner beyond its title. This movie follows filmmaker Zoe Stevenson (Lily James) as she documents her best friend Kaz Khan (Shazad Latif) during his arranged marriage process with Maymouna (Sajal Ali) in Pakistan. As the journey unfolds, Zoe and Kaz begin to question what they truly want, especially after realizing Kaz and Maymouna lack real chemistry. The film explores whether Zoe and Kaz might actually be made for each other, but it might be too late for romance. Watch 'What’s Love Got To Do With It?' streaming on Hulu.

article_content: This week, Davos in Switzerland transforms into a meeting point for influential figures from across the globe as it hosts the World Economic Forum (WEF)'s annual gathering. The event, conceptualized by economist Klaus Schwab in 1971, has long been a staple for high-level networking and discussions. This year's conference is themed ‘The Reshaping of the World: Consequences for Society, Politics and Business’. The focus is on global shifts caused by rapid advances in technology and science, swift social transitions, and evolving economic dynamics. According to WEF, these disruptions demand fresh approaches to worldwide problems. CNN’s Richard Quest notes that the world is navigating uncharted territory after years of crisis, highlighting uncertainty in both rules and solutions. He raises questions about Davos’ ability to foster real unity and direction amid these changes. The 2014 event is exclusive, drawing over 2,500 leaders, thinkers, and prominent personalities from more than 100 nations—many by invitation, but with business tickets priced around $20,000. Attendees span heads of state, religious leaders, academics, activists, nonprofit leaders, and select celebrities, with over 250 planned sessions relating back to the central theme. Notable participants include European Commission President Manuel Barroso, IMF head Christine Lagarde, UN Secretary General Ban Ki Moon, Microsoft founder Bill Gates, and actors Matt Damon and Goldie Hawn. The forum unfolds while conflicts persist in regions such as South Sudan, Syria, and the Central African Republic. Syrian opposition leader George Sabra will be present; parallel peace talks are ongoing in Geneva. Instability in the Middle East and North Africa still hampers recovery years after the Arab Spring, according to the World Bank, which cites ongoing unrest in Syria and various countries’ economic stagnation. Sanctions continue to impact Iran, although recent international agreements could ease those conditions. Iranian President Hassan Rouhani—newly replacing Mahmoud Ahmadinejad—is expected to discuss Iran’s world role, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who remains critical of Rouhani, will share his nation’s political and economic outlook. There’s some optimism as the world economy shows gradual improvement since last year. China's leadership is implementing economic reforms, aiming for less government influence and fairer competition, which will be explored in several Davos sessions. Japan’s Prime Minister Shinzo Abe is set to discuss ‘Abenomics’, the country’s recent economic strategies. In Europe, economic growth is returning but unemployment—particularly among youth in countries like Spain and Greece—remains severe. American priorities are also in the spotlight, with Secretary of State John Kerry attending to address U.S. Middle East involvement. Topics like the NSA’s surveillance revelations weigh heavily, especially among European partners like Germany, whose Chancellor Angela Merkel won’t attend due to a scheduling conflict. Much of Davos’ value historically comes from informal discussions, which often take place outside official forums—hinting that major developments can arise in more casual settings.
